articleTitle: Estimation of Carbon Emissions from Green Grid Infrastructure Projects Based on PSO-LM-BP
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Due to the lack of comprehensive understanding of the key characteristics of the “photovoltaic storage direct flexible” system in power grid infrastructure projects, it is difficult to reduce the losses generated during power transmission, resulting in significant difficulty in estimating carbon emissions. Therefore, a green power grid infrastructure project carbon emission estimation based on PSO-LM-BP is proposed. The carbon emission distribution calculation based on PQ decomposition method is completed through the trend distribution algorithm, and a BP neural network is introduced to construct a carbon emission estimation model. The LM algorithm is used to perform secondary optimization on the ellipsoid parameters, and the PSO algorithm is applied to obtain the global optimal particle for carbon emission estimation, optimizing the emission estimation model. The experimental results show that the carbon emission estimation error of the research method is always below <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 2\ \text{t CO 2}$</tex>, and the correlation coefficient of the estimation results remains above 8.5, indicating a high overall estimation accuracy.

Author Keywords: Estimation of Carbon Emissions from Green Grid Infrastructure Projects Using LM

articleTitle: Synchronization Stability Analysis and Control of Renewable Energy Generation Connected to the Grid Through Power Electronic Converters
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: In recent years, the installed capacity and power generation of renewable energy have been increasing continuously. The integration of large amounts of renewable energy generation into the grid brings challenges to power system stability. In this paper, the impacts of converter control strategy, impedance parameter and network topology on the synchronization stability of renewable energy generation system are explored in a single-converter infinite-bus system and a multi-converter system by using simulation method. Based on the simulation results, suggestions are given to improve the synchronization stability of renewable energy generation connected to the grid through power electronic converters.

articleTitle: The Mechanism of Synchronous Condenser in Voltage Sag Mitigation During FRT of Renewable Energy Integrated Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: With the large-scale integration of renewable energy, the application of power electronic converters in power systems has become increasingly widespread. Renewable energy units, constrained by short-circuit current limits, provide insufficient voltage support during fault ride-through (FRT) periods, resulting in severe system voltage sags. Synchronous condenser (SC), offering dynamic reactive power support, can mitigate system voltage sags during faults. This paper first analyzes the relationship between voltage sag propagation and electrical distance within the system. It then derives the relationship between the voltage support effectiveness of SC and factors such as electrical distance to the node and the condenser's capacity. Finally, simulation experiments are conducted to validate the proposed voltage sag propagation patterns and the mechanism by which SC mitigate system voltage sags.

articleTitle: Hybrid Transmission Expansion Planning for Renewable Power Systems Considering AC/DC Line Operation Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: With advancements of power grid technologies and the growing demand for long-distance power transmission, large-scale regional power grids have evolved into hybrid alternating-current/direct-current (AC/DC) configurations, which are also expected to play a critical role in future renewable energy power systems. Effectively planning these hybrid AC/DC grids-especially through mathematical optimization models-requires detailed representations that capture the operational differences between AC and DC lines, thereby providing a more accurate reflection of real-world performance. To this end, this paper proposes a hybrid transmission expansion planning model that incorporates operational features such as short-term capacity increases for AC lines, the non-reversibility of DC line flows within a day, and the utilization rates of DC lines. A case study on a 27-bus system demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed model.

articleTitle: AI Operator Evaluation Methods and Technical Research in the Power Industry
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: With the digital transformation of the power industry, the application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies in fields such as smart grids, equipment monitoring, and load forecasting has become increasingly pervasive. As the fundamental computational units in neural networks, AI operators play a crucial role. However, existing AI operators often lack optimization tailored to the specific needs of the power industry, and their performance varies significantly across different hardware platforms. This paper proposes an AI operator evaluation method for the power industry, aimed at comprehensively assessing operators' execution performance, efficiency, power consumption, and customization capabilities on various hardware platforms, providing the power industry with efficient, stable, and scalable AI operator support. The paper first constructs a multi-dimensional evaluation framework covering key indicators such as hardware adaptability, algorithm integration capability, execution efficiency, and robustness, and evaluates the operators on various hardware platforms including GPUs, FPGAs, and ASICs. Through comparative analysis, the performance of operators in core power industry tasks, including load forecasting, fault detection, and scheduling optimization, is evaluated. Experimental results show that the optimized operators significantly improve in inference speed, power efficiency, and accuracy, better meeting the power industry's demands for real-time processing, precision, and energy efficiency. Finally, the paper discusses the importance of operator customization and scalability and outlines future directions for operator optimization and application.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Effects and Active Support Capability of Fault Ride-Through Methods for the VSG Under Different Grid Faults
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: With the extensive use of distributed new energy sources, the virtual synchronous generator (VSG) is widely involved in the grid-connected generation of new energy sources due to their inherent inertia and damping capabilities. However, when a voltage drop occurs in the grid due to a short-circuit fault, the VSG can burn out due to a large overcurrent shock. In order to prevent the VSG from being burnt, the VSG needs to have fault ride-through capability and provide certain reactive power support for the grid. Existing studies on the VSG mostly focus on the steady-state without focusing on the dynamic performance of the VSG during grid faults. To solve this problem, this paper focuses on several commonly used fault ride-through control methods. It analyses the current limiting effect and reactive power support capability of these methods through simulation comparison. Finally, based on the simulation results, it is concluded which fault ride-through control method provides better performance regarding the current limiting effect and active grid support capability.

articleTitle: Research on the Optimal Scheduling Model of Virtual Power Plant Considering GCT-CET Interaction Mechanism and CVaR
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Under the dual-carbon policy, virtual power plants (VPPs) optimize multi-energy coordination and renewable integration. This study develops a risk-aware scheduling model integrating green certificate-ladder carbon trading (GCT-CET) and Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) theory to balance economy and sustainability. The framework enhances renewable utilization through GCT mechanisms, employs incentive-based demand response (IDR) for load shifting, and quantifies operational risks via CVaR. An improved quantum particle swarm algorithm minimizes daily costs. The multi-scenario comparison shows that the mechanism can effectively improve the new energy consumption and reduce carbon emissions through source-load collaborative optimization, which confirms its collaborative optimization ability in improving the low carbon and economy of the system.

articleTitle: A Method for Node Importance Evaluation in Power Systems Based on Graph Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Modern power systems are increasingly complex and require accurate evaluation of node importance to ensure grid stability and efficient resource allocation. Traditional methods relying on basic topological metrics often fail to capture dynamic interdependencies among grid components. In this paper, we propose a novel Graph Neural Network (GNN)-based approach that leverages self-supervised learning to integrate topological structure and multi-dimensional node attributes for real-time node importance evaluation without labeled data. Experimental results on real-world power grid data show that our method significantly outperforms traditional approaches in rank accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score, highlighting its potential for smart grid applications.

articleTitle: Distribution Network Dynamic Zoning and Reactive Power Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Distributed power supply has a high access ratio, and its output random superposition load fluctuations make it difficult to adjust reactive power voltage in distribution system, not as simple as the system with fixed output power. Therefore, aiming at these distributed power sources, such as wind power generators and solar photovoltaic power generation, which can change the output capacity at any time, a new method is proposed to dynamically partition and perform reactive power optimization as their output becomes high or low. Based on the tree-like layout of the distribution network, the maximum modularity function value of the whole system is taken as the hard constraint condition, and the sub-regions are adjusted according to the operating value of the system and whether the reactive power margin in each sub-region meets the established standards. Thus, the optimal zoning scheme is formed; And optimize on the basis of completing these tasks. Finally, the IEEE33-node system is taken as an example to verify that the method can solve the partition problem caused by the new energy grid connection with random output to a certain extent. Key innovations include: 1. Dynamic zoning mechanism adapting to renewable energy fluctuations 2. Hybrid optimization combining structural modularity with operational constraints 3. Real-time adjustment capability for voltage regulation precision This methodology provides a viable solution for modern power systems transitioning toward sustainable energy integration,

articleTitle: The Reliability Improvement of Substation Primary Equipment Monitoring Devices and the Research on Lean Technology in Operation and Maintenance
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Substations are pivotal components of power systems, where the reliability of critical equipment such as transformers and circuit breakers deteriorates over time due to various internal and external factors. Managing the maintenance of this equipment is a complex and routine task for power companies. While condition-based maintenance strategies have been increasingly adopted to improve efficiency, the high costs and current limitations of monitoring technologies pose significant challenges. Additionally, maintenance decisions should not only address the reliability of individual equipment but also consider the broader impact on grid reliability. This paper explores an integrated approach that combines equipment reliability theory with power grid reliability assessment methods to enhance maintenance decision-making for key substation equipment. The proposed method is applied to transformers and circuit breakers, providing a more scientific and effective strategy for managing substation maintenance.

articleTitle: Intelligent Operation Head Control Method Based on Fuzzy Active Disturbance Rejection Control
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Aiming at the complex disturbance control problems faced by UAVs in 10kV distribution network insulation spraying operations, this paper proposes a synergistic control architecture that integrates fuzzy self-immunity control and sliding mode PIFOC speed loop. By designing a fuzzy rule base to dynamically compensate the gain parameters of the linear auto-immunity controller (LADRC), the shortcomings of the traditional LADRC with fixed parameters are solved; at the motor drive level, the sliding mode PI control is innovatively introduced to replace the traditional FOC speed loop, which is combined with a hyperbolic tangent function to suppress high-frequency jitter, so as to achieve the synergistic optimisation of dynamic immunity and steady state accuracy. Matlab/Simulink simulation and physical verification of the three-axis gimbal show that the proposed scheme provides an effective technical solution for high-precision spraying operations in a strong electromagnetic interference environment compared with traditional methods.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Filtering Algorithm for Low-Voltage Regulators in Flexible DC Transmission Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: This paper presents an adaptive filtering algorithm for low-voltage regulators based on flexible DC technology, addressing the challenges of noise suppression and voltage stability in DC transmission systems. We enhance the traditional LMS algorithm by incorporating a variable step-size adjustment to dynamically optimize filter parameters in response to real-time conditions. The proposed approach is validated through simulation results, which demonstrate significant improvements in noise suppression and voltage quality compared to conventional fixed-parameter filters. The results underline the algorithm's effectiveness in handling complex, dynamic noise environments and enhancing system reliability.

articleTitle: Contextual Word Distance and Sentiment-Enhanced Dual Graph Convolutional Network for Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis (ABSA) is a fine-grained sentiment classification task that aims to determine the sentiment polarity of specific aspects within a sentence. Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) are widely used in ABSA for capturing dependencies between words. However, GCN relying on semantic and syntactic dependencies face challenges in processing informal or noisy texts due to syntactic parsing errors and the introduction of irrelevant contextual information by attention mechanisms. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Contextual Word Distance and Sentiment-Enhanced Dual Graph Convolutional Network (CWDS-DGCN). Specifically, we propose a contextual word distance matrix to explicitly capture the dependencies between aspect and sentiment words while reducing the impact of irrelevant information. We incorporate external sentiment polarity knowledge into the syntactic dependency tree to enhance its representation. In addition, we design a recurrent feature fusion module to combine information from both semantic and syntactic channels more effectively. Extensive experiments on three datasets show that the CWDS-DGCN model performs better than the most recent baseline approach.

articleTitle: YOLO-CBS: A Model for Fast Object Detection Based on YOLOv7-Tiny
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: This paper proposes YOLO-CBS, a lightweight object detection model enhanced through dual-path optimization for feature representation and cross-layer fusion efficiency. Firstly, the CBS module (Conv-BatchNorm-SiLU) replaces conventional CBL structures, leveraging the smooth gradient properties of SiLU to improve training stability in deep networks. Secondly, a Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) channel attention mechanism is embedded at critical nodes of the feature pyramid, adaptively calibrating channel weights to enhance discriminative multi-scale feature expression. Experiments on the COCO dataset demonstrate that the improved model achieves 56.1% mAP, providing a high-precision lightweight solution for scenarios such as drone inspection and mobile vision analytics.

articleTitle: Analysis of Noise Interference Prediction Methods of Electric Drive System Under Different Conditions
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Since the conduction and radiation noise of the motor drive system of electric vehicles can affect such as the vehicle communication antenna and other on-board electronic equipment, countries around the world have limited the electromagnetic interference noise level of electric vehicles (such as CISPR25). Based on the finite element simulation of electromagnetic field, two methods for predicting the radiated noise of the machine table under different conditions are analyzed and compared in this paper. The main difference between the two methods is that the common mode current return path is different under different environmental conditions.

articleTitle: Transverse Differential Current-Based Pilot Protection Scheme for Flexible DC Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the complex fault transient characteristics of flexible direct distribution network lead to poor reliability of traditional DC protection, this paper proposes a transverse differential current-based pilot protection scheme for flexible DC distribution network. Firstly, the refined model of modular multilevel converter is derived in this paper, and then the fault transient model of flexible direct distribution network is established. The current flowing through the protected line is solved, and the protection criterion of the protected line is constructed by using the difference of transverse differential current under internal and external faults. Finally, a simulation model is built on the RT-LAB platform for verification. The method can correctly identify faults at different fault locations, and has strong ability to withstand transition resistance, with high reliability.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation of Hydrogen Leakage Diffusion Characteristics in Electric-Hydrogen Smart Energy Station
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: In the context of the global development of renewable energy and the increasing importance of hydrogen energy, the study of hydrogen leakage diffusion characteristics in energy stations is crucial for accident prevention because hydrogen is flammable and explosive. In this paper, the electric-hydrogen smart energy station is modeled and hydrogen leakage from different components is simulated using FLUENT. The effects of leak location, wind speed, and wind direction on hydrogen diffusion and combustible cloud distribution are investigated. The research results can support the development of safety prevention and control measures for the energy station.

articleTitle: Research on Energy Storage Configuration and Optimal Scheduling of Cold-Heat-Electricity Coupled Integrated Energy System with Photothermal Power Station
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: In the study, an energy storage scheduling model of integrated energy system (IES) including thermal storage photothermal power station is constructed. Firstly, the photothermal power plant model is tuned, and the electric heater is introduced to recycle a single material that can be both solar energy and wind energy absorber. An optimization model for the thermal energy storage capacity of a photovoltaic power station is developed, considering the expenses associated with fuel, operation, and maintenance in a thermal power plant, as well as the storage costs of the photothermal power station's heat storage system. This model facilitates the optimization of the heat storage capacity, which is then incorporated into the subsequent Integrated Energy System (IES) model. Secondly, based on the optimal heat storage capacity obtained above, a multi-energy complementary integrated energy system model considering electric energy, heat energy and cold energy is established. Again, the scheduling model is established with the system operation cost and carbon emissions as the objective function. Last but not least, an example simulation confirms the established scheduling model's viability and efficacy.

articleTitle: General Human-Machine Architecture and Key Technologies for Centralized Control Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: It is introduced that the current centralized monitoring system of substation is restricted by the system architecture of “man-machine and resource binding”, which is closely bound to the site, and cannot remotely and flexibly access the data resources of specific substation institutions in different places. In order to better support the new construction, reconstruction and expansion of the centralized monitoring system of the new generation of substation, a general man-machine flexible access system architecture of the centralized control system is proposed, and the key technologies such as human-computer interaction network architecture, screen analysis and verification, master-slave mode management, and man-machine seamless switching are designed and implemented, so as to break the binding between man-machine and resources, places and systems, and realize the rapid deployment of man-machine, the local and remote non-differential monitoring of the main and standby commissioning (AB) system, and the analysis and verification functions of substation wiring drawings. The emergency support of the dispatching system and the ability to check the monitoring screen have been improved.

articleTitle: Multi-Feature Detection of Tongue Images Based on Improved YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Tongue feature recognition, as an important component of tongue diagnosis in Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM), has a profound and complex research background, integrating the development of traditional TCM theory with modern science and technology. This paper addresses the characteristics of tongue features and improves upon the YOLOv8 model. By incorporating the ABS module, the model's adaptability to the diversity of tongue shapes and blurred edge features is enhanced. Additionally, the original C2F structure is replaced with the C3STR module, which combines cross-stage spatial attention mechanisms with depthwise separable convolutions. This substitution optimizes feature fusion efficiency while reducing computational redundancy and enhances sensitivity to fine-grained textures. These two improvements complement each other, with the deformable convolution improving spatial modeling capabilities and the C3STR module achieving lightweight feature enhancement. Ultimately, a specialized network architecture tailored for tongue image detection tasks is constructed, providing an efficient solution for multi-target collaborative detection in complex TCM tongue diagnosis scenarios.

articleTitle: Research on the Construction Technology of a Knowledge Base for Large Models in the Power Industry
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Traditional methods for constructing a knowledge base for large models in the power industry primarily rely on general-purpose corpora and simple data augmentation techniques, which struggle to meet the in-depth requirements of the power industry's specialized knowledge. This study significantly enhances the model's ability to understand and apply knowledge in the power domain by constructing a dedicated knowledge graph for the power industry and introducing a chain-of-thought injection mechanism. Experimental results show that, compared to traditional methods, the innovative techniques proposed in this study improve accuracy by 15.3% in power industry knowledge question-answering tasks and increase the F1 score by 12.7% in fault diagnosis tasks. These achievements provide crucial technical support for the construction and application of large models in the power industry.

articleTitle: Optimality Analysis of Reinforcement Learning-based Reactive Power Control
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Data-driven reinforcement learning (RL) methods have shown significant success in various power system applications, particularly in control tasks. However, there is limited research on the optimality of RL methods in voltage control within power systems. This paper addresses this gap by investigating the optimality of RL in reactive power control. We propose a Markov Decision Process (MDP) framework tailored for reactive power control and demonstrate that a tabular RL algorithm can achieve optimal solutions. Furthermore, we examine how the observability of specific state variables affects the optimality of the derived strategy. Simulation results on the IEEE-39 bus system confirm the optimality of the proposed tabular RL method for reactive power control.

articleTitle: Research on the Economic and Safety-Oriented Solutions for Medium Voltage Power Supply End-Use
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: With the rapid development of the power industry, medium voltage power supply systems, as a key component of the power system, have increasingly attracted widespread attention regarding the reliability and economy of their end-use. This paper mainly focuses on the deficiencies in end-use of medium voltage power supply networks, comprehensively considering factors such as economy and safety, and through in-depth analysis of the current power supply schemes and their practical applications, derives the optimal solution for medium voltage power supply end-use. The proposed solution not only considers economic costs but also delves into safety factors, meeting electricity demand and achieving optimal economic benefits and safety standards. The proposed end-use solution will optimize the design of the medium voltage power supply system and provide valuable references.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of a Novel Asymmetric Magnetic Barrier PMa-SynRM for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: This paper presents an optimization design for a novel asymmetric magnetic barrier permanent magnet-assisted synchronous reluctance motor (PMa-SynRM) and analyzes its electromagnetic performance before and after optimization using ANSYS Maxwell simulations. First, a 30 kW, 6-pole symmetric PMa-SynRM was designed based on its operating principles. Then, an asymmetric magnetic barrier structure was introduced by adjusting the opening angle of the magnetic barriers to enhance motor performance. The results show that the peak flux density was reduced from 2.34 T to 2.01 T, the saliency ratio increased, torque ripple decreased by approximately 3%, and the corner speed increased from 983 rpm to 1500 rpm, while the maximum speed rose from 4300 rpm to 5000 rpm. The optimized design significantly improves the electromagnetic performance of the PMa-SynRM, making it more suitable for applications such as new energy vehicles.

articleTitle: Research on Characteristics Simulation Method in Blanket Pebble Beds Based on Percolation Theory
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: The solid tritium breeder blanket is one of the most promising candidates for fusion reactor blankets. However, the simulation of processes such as pebble bed filling and purging is computationally intensive due to the millions of pebbles contained within a single blanket module. Given the structural and physical similarities between pebble beds and porous media, this study develops a simulation program based on percolation theory to characterize the filling and purging behaviors of blanket pebble beds. A percolation network model was constructed through computer programming to simulate fluid flow within the pebble bed, enabling the calculation of pressure drop and velocity distribution under various operating conditions. The simulation results were compared with experimental data, showing excellent agreement and validating the accuracy and reliability of the percolation network model. The results demonstrate that the model based on percolation theory significantly improves computational efficiency while maintaining high accuracy, thereby reducing computational resource requirements. This approach provides a robust theoretical framework and technical support for the rapid modeling and efficient simulation of blanket pebble beds.

articleTitle: A Study on the Differentiated Application of a Generic Scheme for Main Wiring Based on the Whole Life Cycle
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Based on the theory of life cycle cost (LCC), the economic, safety and social benefits of 110kV outdoor HGIS and GIS substation are comprehensively evaluated in order to optimise the selection decision of power distribution equipment. The LCC mathematical model is constructed, and the whole life cycle cost (LCC) of the two options is quantitatively measured and comparatively analysed in terms of initial investment, operation, maintenance, failure and decommissioning disposal. The results show that the initial investment cost of the HGIS scheme is slightly higher than that of the GIS, but its operation cost is basically the same, the maintenance and fault repair cost is significantly lower than that of the GIS, and the decommissioning cost is also more advantageous. Within 40 years of operation, the whole life cycle cost of the HGIS scheme is lower than that of the GIS scheme by about 3 million RMB, which shows a better economic performance. The study shows that the application of LCC calculation method in the optimisation of general design scheme of power distribution equipment is of great value, which can provide a scientific basis for the economic decision-making of electric power engineering projects, improve the investment efficiency and operation efficiency of power grid construction, and promote the sustainable development of the industry.

articleTitle: Research on the Application of XG Boost Based on Quantum Genetic Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: As a major international event, the Olympic Games have an outstanding impact on the sports industry. The quantitative prediction of the number of Olympic medals is a key link in the continuous development of such activities. Firstly, this paper analyzes the influencing factors of Olympic medals, constructing an index system for the number of medals. Secondly, the XG Boost Olympic medal prediction model based on quantum genetic optimization is established. The Olympic medals of 206 countries or regions from 1896 to 2024 are used to predict the medal list of Los Angeles Olympic Games in 2028. It is predicted that the top three of Los Angeles Olympic Games in 2028 are the United States, China and Japan, and the prediction interval of medals is given at 95 % confidence level. After adjusting the hyperparameters of the model by quantum genetic optimization, the prediction accuracy is 87.1 %, providing a scientific reference for the Olympic organizers and participating countries to carry out future events.

articleTitle: Evaluation System of Lithium Battery Energy Storage System from a Safety Perspective
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Energy storage power systems have been widely used due to their multifaceted advantages, and their safety issues have also received extensive attention. A comprehensive performance evaluation method based on a multi-dimensional perspective is proposed to address the current problems in the safe operation of energy storage power plants. The method takes into account the influence of multidimensional factors such as environmental impact, battery health. Moreover, a combined-assignment AHP-GCA evaluation model is constructed to systematically quantify the importance of each indicator, providing a new idea for the safety evaluation of energy storage power systems.

articleTitle: Differential Protection for Collection Lines in Flexible Low-Frequency Transmission Systems Based on Transient High-Frequency Impedance
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: This paper proposes a transient high-frequency impedance-based protection scheme for offshore wind power collection lines with low-frequency AC transmission. By selecting a frequency band that satisfies converter linearization, avoids transient resonance, and reduces noise, the scheme establishes a high-frequency impedance network where both line ends exhibit inductive impedance. This enables simplified calculations of operating and braking impedances, with internal faults showing operating impedance larger than braking impedance, and external faults the opposite. Simulations on PSCAD/EMTDC confirm the scheme's ability to accurately identify internal and external faults with high sensitivity, strong resistance to synchronization errors, and robustness against transition resistance.

articleTitle: Research on MPPT Control Strategy for Photovoltaic Integration into Traction Power Supply Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Amidst the swift expansion of electrified railway networks, the proportion of railway energy consumption in overall power usage has gradually increased. Integrating clean energy sources such as photovoltaic (PV) systems into traction power supply systems has become a significant trend in the development of electrified railways. In the integration of PV systems into traction power supply systems, paying attention to energy transmission efficiency is critical. Therefore, photovoltaic cells necessitate the application of control techniques for achieving maximum power point tracking (MPPT), Factoring in how environmental variables affect the power generation of photovoltaic systems, this paper proposes a Simulated Annealing Perturb and Observe (SA-P&O) method, an MPPT control algorithm that combines the Simulated Annealing (SA) algorithm with the Perturb and Observe (P&O) method. This approach enables rapid localization of the maximum power point while avoiding being trapped in local optima.

articleTitle: Unit Commitment Warm-Start Decision Method Based on Similarity Computation via Graph Convolutional Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: With the rapid development of AI, the ability to make fast and accurate unit commitment (UC) decisions is of great significance. This paper proposes a hybrid UC decision model based on both physical and data-driven approaches, and develops a UC warm-start decision method based on Similarity Computation via Graph Convolutional Networks (SIMGCN). Firstly, we design the labels for UC scheme similarity scores considering the weighted rated capacity of units. Then, we construct a graph similarity evaluation model based on Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN). Leveraging the advantages of GCN in establishing power grid topology and utilizing bus-level information, we train a mapping model between bus load and graph similarity scores using historical data. Finally, we input the decision scheme with the highest historical similarity as the initial feasible solution into the physical model to obtain the optimal UC solution for the day to be predicted through warm-start. Simulation results based on the IEEE-118 bus system show that compared to traditional physical-driven decision methods, the proposed method has superior solving time while ensuring decision accuracy.

articleTitle: Optimization of Operation for Tourism-Oriented Island Microgrid with Combined Wind-Wave Energy and Electricity-Heat Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: To address the prominent issues of high operating costs, low renewable energy utilization, and acute supply-demand imbalance of thermal loads during peak tourist seasons in tourism-oriented island microgrids, this paper proposes a wind-wave-electrothermal co-generation coordinated optimization model. By integrating wind energy, wave energy, and combined heat and power (CHP) systems, a multi-energy coupled system is constructed, incorporating micro gas turbines (MTs), fuel cells, and electrical/thermal energy storage. A multi-objective optimization model is established, focusing on economic objectives (minimizing operating costs) and energy utilization objectives (maximizing primary energy efficiency), while considering constraints such as power balance, equipment operational boundaries, and renewable energy fluctuations. Case studies on a typical tourism-oriented island in southeastern China demonstrate that the proposed system reduces daily operating costs by 24.2% (¥1,156.53/day vs. ¥1,524.81/day), transforms grid interaction from net consumption to net revenue generation, and significantly improves thermal load supply stability. The model effectively enhances renewable energy accommodation capacity and provides theoretical support for multi-energy coordinated dispatch in island microgrids.

articleTitle: Research on the Abnormal Analysis Model of Electricity Selling Price Based on Clustering
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: With the accelerated construction of a modern high-quality economic system, the power sales market presents a diversified competitive pattern. However, since the opening of the power sales market, the profits of power sales companies have been rising month by month, and the electricity costs of some users have increased significantly, making it impossible for the dividends of supply-side market competition to be transmitted to the user side. This paper takes the intelligent analysis of the abnormal average price of power sales by power sales companies as the entry point, builds an abnormal analysis model of the market-based average price for the retail users of power sales companies, uses the DBSCAN clustering analysis algorithm to locate the retail users with abnormal electricity prices, intelligently divides different groups of abnormal users and conducts traceability analysis, and excavates and analyzes the abnormal points of the settlement electricity price, thereby accurately judging the users with abnormal electricity consumption costs, facilitating power companies to proactively serve users to reduce costs and resume production.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of SPICE Model for Circuit Simulation of Cold-Cathode Trigger Tubes
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: A spark-gap switch possesses unique characteristics that cannot be replaced by other devices. It has a multitude of applications and primarily protects high-voltage equipment and components by serving as a high-voltage pulse switch in various high-voltage pulse generators and aviation engine ignition systems. However, a complete and simple Simulation Program with Integrated Circuit Emphasis (SPICE) model for this device is not yet available. This study proposes a cold-cathode trigger tube SPICE model. Under set parameters, the self-breakdown voltage is 15.51 kV, minimum trigger voltage is 3.00 kV, working voltage range is 7.03-10.00 kV, and the operational current is less than 7.14 kA. All characteristic parameters fulfill the detailed specifications of the RQ-10 cold-cathode trigger tube. Model parameters can be modified to satisfy the needs of different scenarios.

Author Keywords: Simulation Program with Integrated Circuit Emphasis

articleTitle: Torque Coordinated Control of Dual-Stator Hybrid Excitation Motor Based on Virtual Motors
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: The dual-stator hybrid exciting vernier motor (DSHEVM) has advantages of higher space utilization and larger output torque, and is especially suitable for the direct drive equipment with low-speed and high- torque. Considering the capability mismatch of the inner and outer stators to output torque on rotor caused by the structure and parameters, the active-disturbance rejection collaborative control (ADRCC) based on the virtual motors was carried out, and the corresponding simulink simulation model was established. The results show that the ADRCC based on the virtual motors can realized the higher phase response speed when the start and load change.

articleTitle: Simulation Study on Discharge Current Characteristics of Gapped Line Arresters
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: For line arresters with series gaps, leakage current monitoring is generally infeasible due to the isolation by the gaps. Current fault detection methods primarily rely on monitoring discharge counts, which alone are inadequate for condition assessment. Research indicates that analyzing discharge current characteristics under lightning impulses is a viable approach to assess arrester conditions. This study constructs a model of a gapped line arrester and validates its feasibility. Using this model, lightning current impulse simulations are conducted to investigate discharge current characteristics and residual voltages. The work in this paper is of great significance for improving the state evaluation and fault diagnosis technology of gapped line arresters.

articleTitle: Prediction of Lithium Battery SOC Based on Extended Kalman Filter Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Accurate parameter identification and state of charge prediction of lithium battery model are the guarantees for the healthy operation of batteries. This paper presents a state of charge prediction method of lithium battery based on extended Kalman filter algorithm. Firstly, the equivalent circuit model of the second-stage RC lithium battery is established and the parameters of the model are identified by the discharge experiment of the hybrid power pulse characteristics. The reliability of the model is verified by comparing the simulation model with the discharge condition. Then the state space modeling of lithium battery is established. The MATLAB simulation experiment is carried out by comparing the extended Kalman filter algorithm and the state of charge prediction of coulomb counting method. The results show that the average prediction error of extended Kalman filter algorithm is 0.9%, which is far lower than 4.4% of coulomb counting method. The prediction accuracy is high, which can effectively improve the utilization rate of lithium battery.

articleTitle: The Calculation of Static Voltage Stability Limits Based on Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: In the context of large-scale wind power integration, traditional methods for calculating static voltage stability limits suffer from low computational efficiency and poor adaptability. To address these issues, this paper proposes a fast calculation method for static voltage stability limits based on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN). The Random Forest algorithm is used to select feature attributes that are strongly correlated with the static stability limits of the transmission sections. These key feature attributes are then input into the CNN for training, establishing a nonlinear mapping relationship between the transmission section limits and the key features. Case studies show that the proposed method significantly improves computation speed compared to traditional continuation power flow algorithms, with prediction errors for static voltage stability limits of less than 5%. This method is suitable for calculating static voltage stability limits of transmission sections in large-scale wind power aggregation systems.

articleTitle: Research on Synergistic Interaction Between Electric Vehicles and Distributed Photovoltaics Under the Background of New Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: This paper systematically analyzes the synergistic interaction between electric vehicles (EVs) and distributed photovoltaics (PV) within the context of emerging power systems. We propose a multi-level coordinated dispatch strategy and introduce innovative business models designed to enhance renewable energy consumption while maintaining grid stability. Our work explicitly considers the impact of dynamic grid topology changes on dispatch strategies and investigates the coupling between business model innovations and grid technology implementation, including the feedback effects that evolving market mechanisms exert on grid operations. In addition, we conduct robustness analyses under extreme operational scenarios to assess the practical applicability of our strategies. The outcomes provide both a theoretical basis and practical guidelines for the efficient coordination of sources, grids, loads, and storage, thereby supporting the development of next-generation power systems.

articleTitle: Neutral line break fault identification for low-voltage power supply lines based on adaptive inspection
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of low efficiency of traditional broken line fault detection methods, this paper proposes a neutral line break identification method for low-voltage power supply lines based on adaptive inspection. According to the neutral line current criterion, adaptive inspection strategy, measured data update scheme, load impedance measurement technology, and the broken line fault detection criterion that takes into account manual experience threshold and adaptive inspection data, the neutral line break fault is accurately identified. Simulation results show that the method can effectively detect the neutral line break fault, and has high reliability and engineering adaptability. Compared with the traditional method, the proposed method reduces the hardware equipment requirements, facilitates engineering implementation, and provides a new solution for the safe and stable operation of the low-voltage power supply system.

articleTitle: Research on Safety Risk Assessment in the Development of the Photovoltaic Industry
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Photovoltaics (PV) is a crucial component of new energy sources, and its vigorous development will effectively address the increasingly severe environmental and energy crises. However, the growth of the PV industry necessitates the resolution of numerous safety risks. In this paper, the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) is employed to classify the safety risks in the development of the PV industry into 5 first-level risk indicators and 18 secondary risk indicators. A risk matrix is calculated to determine the corresponding weights, and risk analysis is conducted. The results reveal that the primary safety risks currently faced are equipment safety and system design.

articleTitle: Improved Antlion Algorithm for UAV 3D Based on Multi-Strategy Path Planning
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Path planning is a fundamental and practical function for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), especially when performing 3D operations in field environments. However, traditional path planning solutions have disadvantages, including local optimization, low convergence accuracy, and poor robustness. This paper proposes an improved Antlion algorithm (SLGCALO) to solve the above problems. We firstly construct flight trajectory model, field terrain model and constraint function for UAV kinematics. Based on this, an improved Sine chaotic mapping is used to generate task path points, while Levy flight is employed to update the UAV trajectories. Along with this, the Gauss-Cauchy hybrid mutation mechanism is introduced to avoid local optimization and improve convergence accuracy. Finally, simulation results are both presented, demonstrating that our proposed solution improves optimization accuracy and path quality compared to traditional algorithms such as the Ant Lion Optimizer (ALO).

articleTitle: Optimization of Distributed Photovoltaic and Wind Turbine Capacity Optimization Allocation Based on Improved Spider Monkey Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: This research advances a refined computational intelligence framework for coordinating sustainable energy assimilation in modern power grids. Leveraging the IEEE 33-bus radial network benchmark, the methodology demonstrates enhanced convergence characteristics when resolving multivariate renewable coordination challenges, particularly in photovoltaic-wind hybrid configurations. Experimental validation confirms that optimized deployment of three wind conversion units (2.1-2.4 MW) or dual photovoltaic clusters (1.2-1.5 MW) achieves concurrent technical enhancements: 17.9-19.2% voltage stabilization, 22.4% mean energy loss reduction, and 14.3% network operational efficiency improvement. The algorithm exhibits superior parametric stability (variation coefficient < 0.12) against conventional swarm intelligence methods, effectively harmonizing intermittent generation profiles with nodal demand characteristics in decentralized architectures.

articleTitle: Text Recognition of Measurement Experiment Detection Table Based on Feature Extraction and Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: The text data for quantitative testing contains a large number of tables, and the main information is stored in the tables. This article proposes an improved feature extraction and fusion model for identifying the complex and diverse table structures, as well as a large number of merged and blank cells, in the text of power metering test detection. By using CVT for feature extraction, we can better detect blank cells and merged cells, improve model accuracy, and use fully connected layers instead of semantic segmentation layers for row and column detection. At the same time, we remove the complex post-processing steps based on semantic segmentation methods, which improves model speed. In order to improve the effect of cell merging, the proposed model uses quadratic ROI+CVT+SCNN to enhance the information exchange ability between adj acent cells. The final experimental results indicate that the proposed model has certain advantages in speed and accuracy compared to existing models, and can solve problems such as blank cells.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Regulating Capacity of Power System Nodes and Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: The large-scale access of renewable energy to the power grid leads to a sharp increase in the demand for power system regulation capacity. In order to solve this problem, this paper explores the mechanism of supply and demand balance of power system regulation capacity, analyzes the transmission characteristics of regulation capacity, and proposes the adequacy index of node regulation capacity and the adequacy index of network transmission regulation capacity. The Garver-6 node system is used to verify the effectiveness and practicability of the proposed method. The example shows that the proposed evaluation method can accurately identify the weak links of regulation ability and clarify the causes of insufficient regulation ability.

Author Keywords: regulate the capacity flow network transmission adjustment ability

articleTitle: Capacity Allocation Method of Hybrid Energy Storage System for Photovoltaic Power Leveling
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: In order to improve the economy and reliability of the hybrid energy storage system, it is very important to select an appropriate capacity allocation method. Starting from the internal power division of the energy storage system, this paper proposes a capacity allocation method of the hybrid energy storage system based on adaptive decomposition. First, weighted moving average method is adopted to make the photovoltaic power meet the grid-connected standards. Then, the Marine Predator algorithm is used to optimize variational mode decomposition (MPA-VMD) to adaptively determine the number of modes K and the quadratic penalty term factor, and VMD-Hilbert is used to allocate HESS power to lithium batteries and supercapacitors, and then the optimal configuration model of hybrid energy storage system is established. The experimental results show that the PV power fluctuation is reduced from 20% to 8%, and the average annual cost is reduced by 34.6% compared with the single configuration energy storage scheme, and the average annual cost is reduced by 15% compared with the single variational mode decomposition (VMD) due to the optimization of the number of modes and the quadratic penalty term factor.

articleTitle: Research on Optimal Dispatch and Operation for Power Quality Improvement in Wind Farms
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: The wind generator installed capacity increases, the power quality issues arising from large-scale wind power integration, particularly focusing on voltage deviation, voltage fluctuations, flicker, and harmonics. It proposes a method to optimize the power quality output of wind farms under load-limiting operating conditions. Firstly, the paper analyzes the main factors affecting wind power quality, including wind speed and turbulence intensity, and highlights the close relationship between voltage flicker and the output power fluctuations of wind turbines. Secondly, it introduces an operational strategy to optimize the overall power quality output by adjusting the power output of different turbines within the wind farm. This method is based on the steady-state analysis theory of power systems and incorporates actual operational data from wind turbines to calculate voltage fluctuations and flicker values under various wind conditions. The effectiveness of the’ method is validated through data fitting and surface rendering using MATLAB. Finally, the paper concludes that under load-limiting operating conditions, rational adjustment of the power output of turbines within the wind farm can effectively improve the overall power quality output, ensuring the safe and economic operation of the power grid. This approach can also be integrated with wind power prediction systems to further optimize wind farm operation and scheduling, providing support for the stable operation of power grids with large-scale wind power integration.

articleTitle: Multi-Source Distributed Photovoltaic Anti-Islanding Protection Device Based on Impedance Angle Measurement
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: With the increasing penetration of distributed generators (DGs) in distribution networks, the issue of unintentional islanding caused by grid outages has become increasingly severe. Impedance-based anti-islanding protection methods, which offer advantages such as small detection blind zones, low false operation rates, and minimal impact on power quality, have attracted significant attention. However, in multi-source distribution networks, variations in DG numbers and mutual interference among injected signals can lead to protection failure. This paper first designs an islanding identification criterion based on impedance angle measurement. Then, a “one-point multi-address” encoding scheme is adopted, where the tripping of any phase simultaneously acts on all receivers in the same district to disconnect photovoltaic (PV) stations. Field experiments demonstrate that the proposed method effectively avoids misoperation and refusal-to-operate issues in existing protections, eliminates potential risks of “islanding operation,” and resolves the long-standing “islanding” hazard in power systems.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Multi-Lead ECG Classification with Short-Time Fourier Transform Attention
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: ECG classification is critical for diagnosing cardiovascular diseases. This study introduces a novel multi-lead ECG classification model incorporating Short-Time Fourier Transform Attention (STFTA) to enhance performance under complex conditions. STFTA effectively integrates information across both the frequency and time domains, significantly improving classification accuracy. The model was evaluated on the PTB-XL and CPSC2018 datasets. On the PTB-XL dataset, it achieved an F1 score of 0.784 and an AUC of 0.941, outperforming existing methods. On the CPSC2018 dataset, the model obtained an F1 score of 0.862, surpassing other advanced models. These results demonstrate the model's excellent performance in ECG classification, improving accuracy and generalization in cardiac disease diagnosis, and confirming the potential of STFTA in ECG signal processing.

articleTitle: A Local Search Algorithm Leveraging the Reasoning Abilities of Large Language Models for Solving Urban Charging Station Location Problem
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: To enhance the charging experience for electric vehicle users and facilitate the widespread adoption of electric vehicles, the paper introduces the urban charging station location problem (UCSLP), which has significant practical implications in the field of electric power. The UCSLP involves two conflicting objective functions: minimizing user waiting time and maximizing the revenue of charging stations. To comprehensively evaluate the solution quality in this multi-objective context, we propose a local search algorithm that leverages the reasoning abilities of large language models. Experimental results demonstrate that large language models can effectively understand the multiple objective functions of the problem and thoroughly assess solution quality. The reasoning abilities of the large language model improve the effectiveness of the local search algorithm in solving the UCSLP and have potential applications for other multi-objective optimization problems.

articleTitle: Research on Loss Reduction Technology for 10kV Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Line loss is an important indicator of the economic operation of the power grid, and energy conservation and loss reduction are important ways to achieve the dual carbon goals. Line loss is an important indicator of the economic operation of the power grid, and energy conservation and loss reduction are important ways to achieve the dual carbon goals. Based on the analysis of the models of various components and power losses in the power grid, this article proposes technical loss reduction methods, and combines them with the example of 10kV high loss lines. Through electrical simulation methods, a mathematical model is established to deeply calculate and analyze the loss composition and high loss reasons of each component under various working conditions, and practical and feasible loss reduction measures are proposed. This provides reference value for the loss reduction work of 10kV transmission lines and has important practical significance.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Optimization for China's Power System Planning with High Proportion of Renewable Energy
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: This study combines power sources, power grids and energy storage infrastructure to construct a new high-resolution long-term planning model for power system, in order to research the layout and configuration of future power systems. The results show that China's power generation structure has significant provincial differences, and renewable energy will become the main source of electricity. The transmission capacity will increase by 210.68<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> and the energy storage capacity will increase by 140.82% in the next 20 years. Our research results also provide valuable reference suggestions for energy planners.

articleTitle: Distribution Cable Fault Location Method Based on ICEEDMAN-NTEO
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: With the acceleration of urbanization, fault location in power distribution cables has become increasingly challenging due to their concealed nature and complex operating environments. Traditional dual-terminal traveling wave ranging methods suffer from inaccuracies in wave velocity calibration and fault occurrence time estimation. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a fault location method for distribution cables based on an improved ICEEMDAN (Improved Complete Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition with Adaptive Noise) combined with a Novel High-order Time-frequency Energy Operator (NHTEO). First, the dual-terminal traveling wave ranging method is enhanced by analyzing the reflection and refraction characteristics of traveling waves during propagation. This modification eliminates the dependency on wave velocity and fault timing, enabling high-precision localization using only four key parameters. Second, to mitigate noise interference and modal aliasing in fault signals, an improved ICEEMDAN algorithm integrating Kernel Principal Component Analysis (KPCA) and fractal dimension fusion is proposed. Coupled with the NHTEO, this approach effectively suppresses high-frequency noise and improves the detection accuracy of wavefront arrival times. Validation through PSCAD simulations under diverse fault conditions-including varying fault locations, transition resistances, and fault types-demonstrates that the proposed method achieves a maximum ranging error of 0.165 km. Compared to conventional approaches, the method exhibits significantly enhanced precision and robust performance. This technique provides an effective solution for rapid fault localization in distribution networks.

articleTitle: Identification of Pipeline Resistance Coefficient Based on Intelligent Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: For network modeling, resistance coefficients in pipes can deviate from their theoretical design values due to long-term usage, wear, blockages, and other factors. This paper proposes a method for identifying pipeline resistance coefficients using the Crested Porcupine Optimizer (CPO) algorithm. This approach transforms the model parameter identification problem into a multi-objective nonlinear optimization problem with complex constraints. It allows for the calculation and accuracy analysis of resistance coefficients in the network using a limited number of observation nodes and measurement values. The identified resistance coefficients closely match the actual parameters under network operation, reduced the influence of the deviation of the drag coefficient on the ac-curacy of the simulation.

articleTitle: Analysis and Recommended Strategies for Load Demand of Docking Ships and Capacity Selection of Shore Power Construction
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: This study explores the impact of the load demand of moored vessels on the capacity planning of shore power infrastructure, with the aim of proposing a scientific capacity selection strategy. By estimating the power demand of port vessels and analyzing the mainstream ship types of typical docks, the shore power capacity demand was studied and evaluated. The results indicate that the capacity of shore power construction should prioritize the actual electricity consumption of ships, while balancing economic feasibility and system adaptability. This article proposes optimization strategies, including demand driven capacity estimation and phased implementation, to reduce capacity redundancy, provide decision support for port managers and policy makers, and promote the economic, safe, and efficient operation of shore power technology.

articleTitle: Co-Optimization Strategy of Static and Dynamic Reactive Power Compensation Devices for Reducing Reactive Power Fluctuation at Switching Moment
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: As the proportion of new energy in the power grid increases, maintaining voltage stability becomes an increasingly challenging task. To ensure the reliable operation of the grid, additional reactive power compensation devices are needed. Among these, the Static Var Generator (SVG) plays a critical role. While extensive research has focused on the co-control of SVGs with other dynamic reactive power compensation devices, fewer studies have explored the coordination between SVGs and static reactive power devices. The paper aims to enhance grid stability by replacing part of the reactive power output of the SVG with static reactive power devices during steady-state conditions. This, in turn, allows the SVG to provide more reactive power support during transient grid events. To achieve this, the study utilizes the PSCAD/EMTDC simulation platform to model a wind farm equipped with SVG. Capacitors are used to replace the reactive power output of SVGs in steady state, and the precise switching moments of static reactive devices are calculated to minimize reactive power fluctuations during the replacement process. The results offer a novel solution to voltage stability in grids with a high share of new energy integration and provide significant engineering applications for the coordinated use of SVGs and static reactive power compensation devices.

articleTitle: A Typical Day-iTransformer Based Method for Power Load Breakpoint Fitting
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Amid the continuous advancement of China's electricity market reform, accurate user - side power load aggregation monitoring is of great significance. This paper focuses on the breakpoint issue in load aggregation curves. By leveraging the Typical Day - iTransformer algorithm, a feature set is constructed, data features are mined, and breakpoint fitting is effectively achieved. Comparative analysis reveals that this algorithm outperforms other methods, ensuring data integrity and offering strong support for subsequent power - related applications. Through the verification of single - point and multi - point missing scenarios, it is found that the Typical Day - iTransformer algorithm exhibits significantly better fitting results than the Newton interpolation algorithm when there are missing values in the load curve, providing a new solution for optimizing curve numerical fitting.

articleTitle: Study on Constant Current Characteristics of LCC-S-S Wireless Energy Transfer System
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: LCC-S-S type compensation structure is a common compensation structure in single trunk coil radio energy transmission system. Due to the influence of high frequency parasitic resistance, its constant current characteristics change with the change of load, which is difficult to meet the needs of practical design. In this paper, the influence of high frequency parasitic resistance parameters on the constant current characteristics of LCC-S-S radio energy transmission system is studied. Through the analysis of grey correlation degree, the influence degree of different parameters on the constant current characteristics of the system is compared, and the simulation model is established to analyze the influence of the parasitic resistance parameter with the highest grey correlation degree on the constant current effect of the system and the joint influence of multiple high-frequency parasitic resistance parameters on the system in turn. The design requirement of system current fluctuation under different high frequency parasitic resistance parameters is given, and the simulation results are consistent with the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Analysis and Suppression of DC-Side Oscillations in MMC Grid-Connected Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: With the increasing penetration of power electronic devices in power systems, oscillations resulting from dynamic interactions between devices have become increasingly prominent. This paper investigates DC-side oscillation issues arising from grid-connected Modular Multilevel Converters (MMC). Firstly, an MMC impedance model is developed to analyze the mechanisms behind DC-side oscillations. Subsequently, a DC-side oscillation suppression strategy based on impedance phase optimization control is proposed, in which an impedance phase correction module is integrated with the conventional notch filter to compensate for MMC impedance phase deviations specifically. This effectively enhances the phase margin and suppresses oscillations in the system. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, demonstrating that it significantly improves system stability and provides rapid dynamic response.

articleTitle: Wind Power Prediction Based on Chaotic Time Series Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: According to the analysis based on short term load forecasting, the author analyze wind power data, knowing that meteorological factor is the greatest impact on wind power. This article refers to the knowledge of chaos, wind power has the random and irregular trajectory, the meanwhile, chaos is very sensitive to initial conditions of periodic motion. Applying MATLAB toolbox of time series to analyze wind power, we achieve the changing trends and relationship between wind speed and wind power. Drawing support of SPSS software for wind power spectral analysis, data from the DT70 meters tower, we get wind power spectral density, wind speed, area spectrum, phase spectrum, gain, cospectrum density, coherence and cross-piece. We know that the disorder, intermittent and random characters result in challenging prediction of wind power. We obtain in this study that wind power and wind speed shows very close correlation between their obviously similar trends.

articleTitle: Automatic Differential Protection of Distribution Network Line Current Based on DTW Algorithm and Phase Features
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Aiming at the inefficiency of traditional protection systems in distribution network line faults, a distribution network line current automatic differential protection method based on DTW algorithm and phase characteristics is proposed. Firstly, a device framework integrating data acquisition, digital processing, and protection algorithms was designed to achieve precise processing and discrimination of fault currents and voltages. In terms of fault detection mechanism, differential protection criterion is introduced, which extracts current amplitude and phase characteristics, and uses line fault direction diagram to accurately locate the fault location and evaluate its severity. Innovatively applying the DTW algorithm allows for adaptive adjustment of the timeline length based on data features, thereby optimizing the similarity between data collection points and significantly improving the accuracy of fault feature recognition. By using the DTW distance as the objective function, this method can accurately calculate the position of short-circuit points, grounding resistance value, and fault phase current amplitude, effectively improving the reliability and efficiency of distribution network line protection. The simulation results have verified the improved protection effect of this method in terms of amplitude and phase difference, demonstrating the characteristics of rapid response and efficient action. Even in the case of frequent faults, its efficient performance can still be maintained.

articleTitle: Medium and Short-Term Wind Power Prediction Based on ARIMA and LSTM Models
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: With the significant growth of green electricity trading globally, research on wind power generation has become particularly important. Wind power generation is characterized by its volatility and intermittency, which can affect the stability of the power system when connected in large scales. By achieving high-precision wind power forecasting, it is possible to optimize grid dispatching plans, reduce the phenomenon of wind curtailment, and ensure the safe and stable operation of the power grid. This study employs a hybrid method combining the Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) model and the Long Short-term Memory (LSTM) model for wind power output prediction. Initially, the ARIMA model was used for preliminary forecasting, followed by further modeling of the ARIMA forecast results and original data using the LSTM model. Combining the linear modeling capability of ARIMA model with the LSTM model's ability to capture long-term dependencies enhances the forecasting performance, and the method was tested on wind power data from 50Hertz Energy Company in Germany.

articleTitle: The Impact of Higher-Order Motifs on Interdependent Power-Communication Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: The interdependent power-communication network is one of the most important infrastructures in modern society. Modern power systems rely heavily on communication networks for real-time monitoring and control, and communication networks require stable power supplies. This complex interdependence brings significant risks, especially in the case of cascading failures, which may spread rapidly in interconnected systems. Since power grids are exposed to the wild for a long time, they are highly susceptible to natural disasters and trigger cascading failures. However current researches mainly focus on studying the robustness of complex systems from low-dimensional nodes or edges and ignore the interaction between local structures. Motifs are a higher-order structures, providing a new view for studying complex systems. In this paper, we study the impact of the robustness of interdependent power-communication networks based on motifs. Firstly, we construct a realistic model of interdependent power-communication networks by combining electrical properties and network delays. Then, we study the impact of motifs on the power grid. Through numerical simulations, we find that when about 20% of the power grid lines are removed, the motif concentration of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M_{42}$</tex> is close to 0, and the same is true when the communication network lines are removed, which indicates that motif <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M_{42}$</tex> is of great significance to maintaining the power grid topology. We think that this paper is helpful for designing more robust interdependent power-communication networks.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning-Based Intelligent Control Algorithm for Flexible DC Low-Voltage Stabilizers
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: This paper presents an intelligent regulation algorithm for flexible DC low-voltage stabilizers based on reinforcement learning (RL). By incorporating Deep Q-Learning (DQN) into the voltage regulation process, this algorithm enables the stabilizer to adaptively learn optimal control strategies, dynamically adjusting voltage parameters in response to variations in load and grid conditions. The algorithm leverages a self-optimizing mechanism with experience replay and a multi-objective reward function to balance voltage stability and energy efficiency. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm enhances response speed, maintains voltage stability, and reduces energy consumption, surpassing traditional PID and fuzzy control methods in complex grid environments.
