The results show that with the addition of the notch filter, the system can effectively suppress the interference of the second harmonic and ensure the dynamic response speed of the voltage loop without affecting the harmonic content of the input current. The dynamic performance of the system against load disturbances is significantly improved by the load current feed-forward control strategy. The application of second-order sliding mode observer simplifies the hardware design, reduces the system cost, and has a good performance in load current estimation. Simulation experimental results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Correlation-Driven Multi-Level Multimodal Learning for Anomaly Detection on Smart Electric Grid
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: In multi-energy systems, the continuous expansion of sensor networks and the rapid growth of data dimensions make the traditional single-modality-based anomaly detection strategy difficult to adapt to the challenges of multi-source heterogeneity and potential correlation brought by complex energy consumption scenarios. According to the theory of multimodal fusion algorithms, the Correlation-Driven Multi-Level Multimodal model in this work deeply executes cross-modal collaborative learning and multi-level semantics representation for the data feature of multiple energy sources: Firstly, utilize the multi-channel attention mechanism to mine the correlation between energy consumption data in different modals to realize the implementation of the weight attention of key features. Then, the hierarchical embedding network was used to map the multi-modal features to the high-dimensional unified semantic space, the temporal information and spatial relations were captured through different levels. Moreover, we construct a composite graph relationship which covers multi-source data and the potential interaction in between by combining graph structure learning and adversarial training, to enhance the accuracy and robustness of abnormal features capturing, to realize accurate detection of complex anomalous patterns in multi-energy systems. The experiment results demonstrate that, compared to the previous mainstream methods, the proposed model has a higher detection accuracy and a stronger generalization ability on the multi-source energy datasets.

articleTitle: Virtual Power Plant Bidding Strategy from the Power Demand Side Perspective
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: With the development of the new power system and the continuous deepening of the power market reform, the participation modes of power demand - side resources in the market have become diversified. Virtual power plants integrate distributed demand resources and play dual roles of both buyers and sellers in the market, enabling the optimization of power resource allocation. In order to comprehensively optimize power trading, this study starts from the perspective of the power demand side and constructs a bidding model for virtual power plants participating in the day-ahead power market. It focuses on electric vehicle scheduling and demand response strategies, and analyzes their impacts on the economic performance of virtual power plants as well as the internal action mechanisms of operation strategies on the cost structure. Through case studies to optimize the bidding electricity volume and combined with flexible scheduling and demand response measures, the results show that the power trading cost can be precisely controlled. This indicates that virtual power plants have great potential in promoting the efficient and sustainable development of the power market.

articleTitle: Optimization Algorithm for Photovoltaic Distribution Network Based on Improved Multi-Objective Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of distribution networks containing a high percentage of distributed power sources in terms of source-load uncertainty and coordination of multiple reactive power compensation devices. In this paper, we propose an optimization strategy based on an improved multi-objective particle swarm technique. The strategy firstly targets on-load regulator transformers and capacitor banks with discrete outputs, takes the active fluctuation of the distribution network and the voltage deviation of the PV grid-connected points as the objectives, introduces the miniature habitat technique to improve the particle swarm algorithm, and adopts the algorithm to solve the model. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed strategy is verified by the IEEE 33-node example. The optimization strategy ensures the security of the whole network and accurately controls the weak nodes in the distribution network, which provides an important guarantee for the economic and reliable operation of the distribution network.

articleTitle: Defect Detection Method for 10kV Column Equipment Based on Superposition Segmentation and Improved YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: To address the challenges of small recognition targets and significant background interference in the detection of defects in 10kV column equipment, a novel defect detection method based on superposition segmentation and an improved YOLOv8 model is proposed. To tackle the issue of small target detection, the proposed method introduces a superposition segmentation approach, which divides the detection image into four equal parts and incorporates the golden section ratio. This strategy effectively enlarges the recognition targets and enhances detection accuracy. Furthermore, to mitigate the limitations of the original YOLOv8 model, which is prone to background interference and inaccurate target localization, the proposed method integrates the GAM attention mechanism and replaces the original loss function. These modifications increase the weighting ratio of the target, thereby improving detection performance. The method was evaluated on a self-constructed dataset, named the CCDD (Column Equipment Detection Dataset). Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an average detection accuracy of 86.7% and a recall rate of 83.2% for defect detection. Compared to the original YOLOv8 model, the accuracy is improved by 9.2%, and the mAP@0.5 is increased by 15.5%. This approach provides a promising solution for defect detection in 10kV column equipment.

articleTitle: Calculation and Analysis of Solar Irradiance of Small Fresnel Fixed Line-Focus Collector
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: The sliding polar axis tracking mode of a small Fresnel fixed-focus line collector is introduced in this paper, and a calculation model is presented for determining the amount of solar radiation absorbed by the collector's absorber. The impact of geographic factors on the sliding polar tracking performance of small Fresnel fixed-focus line collectors is analyzed, and environmental and economic evaluations are conducted using Guangzhou as a case study. It is found that the solar collector's annual adjustment interval ranges from 20 to 48 days, and the cumulative total absorbed solar radiation throughout the day follows a “bimodal” distribution with an increasing number of days in a year. Moreover, the negative impact of high geographical latitude on solar radiation can be offset by the high altitude factor. It is calculated that carbon dioxide emissions can be reduced by 250.37 kg/year, sulfur dioxide emissions by 2.03 kg/year, and dust emissions by 1.01 kg/year in the Guangzhou area using small Fresnel fixed-focus line collectors, highlighting their potential as a conventional energy substitution for reducing greenhouse gas emissions.

articleTitle: Research on Charging and Storage Trading Mechanism of Park Source Network Based on Multi-Agent Cooperative Game
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: With the continuous expansion of energy marketization, the demand of users to participate in energy marketization transactions continues to increase, which puts forward new requirements for the development of Integrated energy system. In order to solve the problem of conflict of interests of different decision-making bodies in IES, this paper first constructs a typical IES source network load and storage equipment model. Based on the operation mode of IES participating in the power market, a multi-agent transaction model of the park in the power market is constructed and solved. Finally, the proposed multi-agent cooperative game method is verified by simulation examples. The results show that after adjusting the market energy price for many times, all the aggregators can save about 30% of the cost. The proposed optimization scheme can effectively promote the multi-body cooperative alliance of source network load and storage in the park, and improve energy utilization efficiency and economic benefit.

articleTitle: Wind Power Smoothing with Genetic Algorithm Based Fuzzy Control of Energy Storage in Wind Farm
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: To achieve the smoothing and grid connection of wind power, an energy storage system is used to mitigate wind power fluctuations. Firstly, based on the adaptive improved complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition with adaptive noise (ICEEMDAN), wind power is adaptively decomposed and reconstructed to obtain the power instructions for wind power grid connection and energy storage charge and discharge. Secondly, according to the output requirements of the energy storage system and considering the state of charge (SOC) of the energy storage, a fuzzy control method is employed to adjust the power instructions for the energy storage, obtaining optimized power instructions. Finally, genetic algorithms are utilized to optimize the fuzzy membership parameters, reducing the impact on grid-connected power while optimizing the SOC. Case studies demonstrate that the proposed control strategy can achieve the smoothing and grid connection of wind power, ensuring that the energy storage SOC operates within a reasonable range.

articleTitle: Research on Ordered Power Usage Strategy for Decentralized Electric Heating Considering User Behavior Differences
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: The large-scale integration of electric heating devices under the “coal-to-electricity” policy can cause peak loads, affecting grid stability and power quality. To address this, this paper proposes a leader-follower game optimization for a “Photovoltaic + Thermal Storage Electric Heating” system, led by a Virtual Power Plant (VPP) and considering user behavior. Using a building thermal load model and K-Means clustering, users are grouped for better management. The bilevel model optimizes VPP pricing and user electricity plans, which is then solved as a Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) problem. Case studies show that the optimized pricing strategy reduces user costs, increases VPP profits, and improves photovoltaic utilization while ensuring orderly electricity use.

articleTitle: Optimal Operation of Virtual Power Plant Considering Electricity Carbon-Green Card Transaction and Its Income Distribution
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: A virtual power plant (VPP) facilitates the utilization of renewable energy by consolidating numerous distributed wind power sources and energy storage systems to engage in electricity market transactions. Simultaneously, it can yield the environmental advantages of VPP by engaging in the carbon trading market and the green certificate market. This paper establishes an optimal operation model for VPP in the spot power market, carbon trading market, and green certificate market, addressing the uncertainties associated with wind power and photovoltaic output income risk, as well as the interconnections between power market trading, carbon emission trading, and green certificate trading. It also provides the optimal bidding strategy for VPP in the power market. Subsequently, utilizing the Shapley value from cooperative game theory, a quantitative analysis is conducted on the contributions of various distributed resources within the virtual power plant to the total income. The validity of the proposed bidding technique and income distribution system is demonstrated through an example.

articleTitle: Research on Intelligent Traction Control Method of Hydraulic Grinder Based on Fuzzy PID
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: In this paper, a new modular hydraulic grinding traction method is proposed to improve the stability and accuracy of grinding process. This method combines modular design, hydraulic technology and traction system, and can accurately pull and grind wires and cables. Firstly, the paper analyzes the shortcomings of traditional grinding methods. Then, the optimal control parameters of PID are calculated by using BP neural network, based on the deviation between actual and expected traction speed; At the same time, through fuzzy control, the accurate update of PID parameters is obtained by taking the deviation between actual and target traction force and its change rate as input. The control results of these two aspects are applied to the actuator to adjust the parameters of hydraulic grinding and realize the precise control of traction speed and force. Experimental results showed that the performance parameters of the hydraulic grinder met the target values. The system demonstrated stable dynamic performance, and the balancing control effect was remarkable.

articleTitle: Multi-Time-Scale Optimal Voltage Control in Microgrids with Distributed Generations
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of network loss increase, voltage deviation, and voltage exceeding specified limits when large-scale distributed generations (DGs) are connected to a microgrid (MG), this paper proposes a multi-time scale coordinated control method considering different types and response speeds of reactive power regulation equipment. In the day-ahead stage, an optimization model is established to minimize the network loss and voltage deviation by controlling traditional equipment like tap changers and capacitor banks, which is efficiently solved by linearization and a second-order cone algorithm. In the real-time stage, a reactive power-voltage control model based on the voltage sensitivity principle is proposed, which considers the differences in the adjustment costs of different DGs. The simulation example shows that the proposed method reduces the voltage deviation and network loss (by 34.73<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>). For voltage regulation, it can optimize the regulation target according to the voltage sensitivity and the regulation costs of each DG, thus resulting in better economic performance while adjusting voltages.

articleTitle: Parameter Optimization Analysis of Cold Source System Based on Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: With the rapid development of urban modernization and industrialization, the global energy shortage and the increasing degree of environmental damage, the problems represented by building energy consumption, especially the energy consumption of central air-conditioning system, have attracted widespread attention. As the main part of building energy consumption, the optimization of the central air-conditioning cooling system is of great significance for achieving energy conservation and emission reduction. However, there are still many deficiencies in the modeling technology and energy consumption optimization of the central air conditioning cold source system, including the low accuracy of the model and the inaccurate prediction of energy consumption. In order to solve these problems, this paper proposes an optimization scheme of chilled water system of central air conditioning based on genetic algorithm to improve the parameters of the cooling source system, so as to improve the accuracy of energy consumption prediction and the effectiveness of system optimization.

articleTitle: Optimization Analysis of Overvoltage Protection Setting for Parallel Capacitor Banks
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: The parallel capacitor group in the substation is usually put into operation when the grid voltage drops, and is promptly disconnected when the grid voltage rises. If the disconnection is unsuccessful, there will be a delay in overvoltage protection disconnection. This article focuses on the accident of parallel capacitor banks in a 500kV substation. During the analysis of the causes, it was found that there were problems with overvoltage protection, which could not effectively protect the capacitor banks. Taking into account the effects of transformer impedance, harmonic current, and capacitor manufacturing tolerances, the reason for the high overvoltage protection setting was identified and verified through PSCAD simulation. Corresponding measures and suggestions were proposed for control strategy and overvoltage protection setting of parallel capacitor devices, providing reference for current design and operation personnel.

articleTitle: Optimal Scheduling Strategy of Renewable Energy Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: The coordinated operation of microgrid units is crucial for the society. Since the system output power is full of uncertainties, it is crucial to propose reliable optimal scheduling strategies for microgrids. In this paper, a multi-objective scheduling structure is established based on the output power allocation of each operating unit in the grid-connected mode of the microgrid and solved by the improved multi-objective particle swarm algorithm (MOPSO). Through the simulation model data verification, the proposed method can not only deal with the complex multi-objective microgrid system but also can effectively give the real-time active output of different operating units in one day. Therefore, the optimal scheduling strategy proposed in this paper has high practical value and helps to improve the power supply reliability and economy of renewable energy microgrids.

articleTitle: Research on Fine-Tuning and Optimization Techniques of Language Models in the Field of Electric Power Customer Service
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: With the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence technology, the demand for intelligent services in the power customer service sector is growing. Large language models, as a core technology in natural language processing, have shown significant potential in the application within the power customer service field. However, directly applying general-purpose language models falls short of meeting the professional, timely, and personalized needs of the power customer service domain. This paper aims to investigate the fine-tuning optimization techniques of language models for the power customer service sector. By constructing high-quality instructions through human-machine collaboration, low-rank adaptive fine-tuning, reinforcement learning based on human feedback, and the distillation of reasoning capabilities in small-sample learning contexts, we enhance the model's performance and fine-tuning efficiency, as well as its ability to understand and respond to user intents. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed methods significantly improve the accuracy of power customer service Q&A by 12.7%, increase the BLEU score of response generation by 9.3%, and enhance training efficiency by 3.2 times.

articleTitle: Research on the Improved Control Algorithm of Virtual Synchronous Generator Based on T-Type Three-Level Inverter
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: This paper investigates the control strategy of the grid-connected T-type three-level inverter, aiming to enhance the power angle stability of the inverter system under large grid disturbances. The study first establishes the mathematical model of the grid-connected T-type three-level inverter, employing Virtual Synchronous Generator (VSG) control, and proposes a power angle stability control strategy in grid-connected mode, improving the power angle stability after large grid disturbances. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, providing theoretical support and practical guidance for the stability of inverter systems based on grid-connected control strategies.

Author Keywords: Large disturbances in the power grid

articleTitle: Load Voltage Control Operation Method for Hybrid Distribution Transformers Based on Improved Voltage Detection Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: The changes in the distribution network load will affect the distribution network voltage, so the hybrid distribution transformer (HDT) needs to start or stop the load voltage compensation equipment according to the specific load situation. Due to the disadvantage of commonly used voltage rise and fall detection algorithms, this paper proposes a novel dq0 transformation detection algorithm, which takes the derivative of each phase voltage to construct a virtual three-phase voltage, and then performs dq0 transformation on three sets of virtual three-phase voltages. Finally, through simple logical judgment, the detection of single-phase power supply voltage drops and other conditions can be achieved. The advantage of this algorithm is that it only requires the addition of a filter with a smaller time constant to filter out higher-order harmonics, effectively avoiding the delay caused by the larger filter time constant in traditional detection algorithms, thereby improving the real-time and accuracy of detection. The simulation verification of the improved detection algorithm is implemented with the Saber simulation platform about the start and stop of the load voltage compensation device based on the detection signal.

articleTitle: Research on Measures to Improve the Multiple Renewable Energy Stations Short Circuit Ratio Based on an Actual Photovoltaic Integration System
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: This paper analyzes the effectiveness of synchronous condensers and grid-forming devices in improving the multiple renewable energy stations short circuit ratio (MRSCR), based on a practical project involving a 90MW photovoltaic (PV) station connected to the 330kV HR substation in Ningxia power grid. The study shows that configuring a 50Mvar synchronous condenser, 50MW grid-forming energy storage, or 40Mvar static synchronous compensator can increase the SCR to above 1.5, meeting Chinese National Standard. Additionally, a hybrid configuration of 20Mvar static synchronous compensator and 25MW grid-forming energy storage is also effective. The research provides practical engineering references for improving the MRSCR.

Author Keywords: renewable energy stations short circuit ratio

articleTitle: Power Inspection Text NER: Integrating BERT with Matrix LSTM
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Online monitoring and power inspection are essential tools for ensuring the stability and reliability of power systems. However, current intelligent operation and maintenance analysis predominantly relies on online monitoring data, largely overlooking the vast potential of inspection text data. Named Entity Recognition can extract critical information from such texts, optimizing maintenance processes and enhancing grid stability. This paper proposes a BERT-mLSTM NER model. The model enriches contextual semantic information by incorporating perturbations generated by the FGM algorithm into BERT's input embeddings. It also employs multiple mLSTM modules to capture long-range dependencies, improving contextual recognition. Furthermore, a contrastive noise module is introduced to enhance the model's noise resistance. These enhancements significantly improve the model's robustness and recognition performance. Experiments demonstrate that the BERT-mLSTM model performs excellently on both domain-specific and general-domain datasets, showcasing strong adaptability and generalization capabilities, and providing an effective solution for power inspection text analysis.

articleTitle: Analysis of Text Generation System Design Combining Retrieval Augmented Generation and Fine-Tuning Strategy
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Text generation technology based on Pre-trained Language Model (PLM) has made significant progress in recent years, but it still faces many challenges such as semantic inconsistency and insufficient computing power. In view of this phenomenon, Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) and Fine-tuning strategy is studied, the general framework design for the text generation system of fusion strategy is put forward, several typical systems in specific fields are analyzed. The discussion of the realization and development direction of technology provides a reference for studying fusion strategy, which can improve the quality of text generation system design.

articleTitle: Analysis and Evaluation of Battery Pack Inconsistency Based on PSO-Level Difference Maximization Combination Weighting
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: In this paper, a new method of inconsistency evaluation is proposed, which combines subjective and objective weights. The improved subjective weight of AHP and the objective weight of E-Critic are synthesized by using the level difference maximization method based on PSO optimization, and the comprehensive weight is obtained. Finally, the score standard deviation is used as the threshold to evaluate the inconsistency. This paper selects the data of decommissioned lithium iron phosphate battery pack, extracts several characteristic indexes, and evaluates the consistency with this method. It is proved that this method of fusion weight is reasonable compared with each single-weight method. Finally, the validity of this method is verified by another battery cycle data.

articleTitle: A Two-Stage Optimization Strategy for Hybrid Power Systems with Dominated-Hydropower
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: This study proposes a two-stage optimization scheduling strategy for hybrid energy systems dominated by hydropower, aiming to address the coordination of hydro, wind, solar, and energy storage in the context of energy transition. The first-stage model focuses on resolving the current challenges in coordinating hydro, wind, and solar power, while the second-stage model explores the effect of energy storage in reducing the gap between power generation and demand with increased penetration of wind and solar power in the electrical grid. The findings emphasize that the key to grid-side energy storage deployment is achieving a balance between economic efficiency and system stability. Additionally, improving the accuracy of wind and solar power forecasting is essential for enhancing the reliability of day-ahead scheduling.

articleTitle: Lightweight and Secure Encryption of Sensitive Data in Power Communication Transmission Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Data privacy and security are becoming more and more the focus of users' attention, while data face serious leakage risks during network transmission and storage. Moreover, in edge networks, due to the limited computing and communication resources, it is difficult to protect data privacy while efficiently computing and processing the data. Therefore, this paper proposes a lightweight security encryption technique for sensitive data in power communication transmission networks. Firstly, the services carried on the power communication transmission network are classified, and the principles and processes of service configuration are clarified; then, for the problem of incomplete consideration of factors in the current traditional service configuration algorithm, combined with the principles of service configuration of the power communication transmission network, a multi-constraints-based service routing optimisation model for the power communication transmission network is designed. On this basis, a service routing optimization algorithm suitable for power communication transmission networks is proposed Finally, deep learning algorithms are compared and analysed to demonstrate the superiority of deep learning algorithms in service configuration application scenarios. Through actual cases, the proposed algorithm is compared and analysed with related typical algorithms, and it is verified that the proposed algorithm has obvious advantages in balancing the network load, reducing the risk of the whole network, and computing efficiency.

articleTitle: Research on Inertia Estimation of New Energy Power System Based on Parameter Identification
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Accurate inertia estimation is the premise of evaluating the frequency security and stability of power system. In this paper, an inertia estimation method for new energy power system based on parameter identification is proposed. Firstly, the expression of equivalent inertia time constant of new energy power system is analyzed. Then, taking the region as the research object, the principle of inertia estimation is clarified. Then, based on the active-frequency data, the identification process of the controlled autoregressive model and the recursive least squares algorithm with forgetting factor is introduced in detail. Finally, the feasibility and accuracy of the proposed method under large / small disturbances are verified by the improved IEEE 39 system.

articleTitle: Research and Application of Knowledge Driven Safety Supervision and Control System for Electric Power Production Operation
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: In view of the insufficient application of intelligence in power production, the technology such as big model and knowledge map is used to integrate UAV key violation evidence search and multimodal data of power production, develop a safety management and control system for power production and operation, build a new mode of UAV omni-directional safety supervision and control, assist in supporting the intelligent analysis and control of safety risks at various stages before, during and after power field operation, promote the transformation and upgrading of intelligent field operation safety management and control, and improve the efficiency of safety management and control in power production and operation.

articleTitle: Research on Carbon Emission Prediction Model Based on Power Load Data
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: In the context of the global active response to climate change, China has firmly put forward the “dual carbon” goals. However, there are many problems in the current field of carbon emission research. Traditional carbon emission prediction methods have low accuracy and struggle to comprehensively and accurately capture the nonlinear relationship between carbon emissions and numerous complex influencing factors, resulting in a large deviation between the prediction results and the actual situation; the stability is also not good. Facing external environmental changes or data fluctuations, the output results fluctuate significantly and cannot provide continuous and reliable data; in addition, it is difficult to obtain input data. Its influencing factors cover many fields such as economy, energy and industrial production. Data sources are widely distributed, and the collection, collation and integration work is challenging, limiting the accuracy and practicality of the prediction model. The power industry is a key area for carbon emissions. This paper focuses on studying the relationship between power data and carbon emissions, optimizes and improves the BP neural network, and builds an electricity-carbon prediction model for carbon emission prediction on this basis. Finally, through the data of a certain province, the proposed electricity-carbon prediction model is simulated, and the electricity-carbon prediction model constructed in this paper is comprehensively compared and deeply analyzed with other prediction models. The research results clearly show that the carbon emission prediction model proposed in this paper can effectively achieve carbon emission prediction in the power field.

articleTitle: Energy Efficiency Optimal Control of Multi-Unit Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: This paper presents several energy efficiency optimization cases of multi-unit systems composed of equipment with the same efficiency, equipment with similar efficiency, and equipment with different efficiency. For a multi-unit system composed of equipment with the same or similar energy efficiency, the optimal load distribution method between equipment is to keep the load rate of each operating equipment equal; for a multi-unit system composed of equipment with different energy efficiency, the optimal load distribution method between equipment is to keep the load rate of each operating equipment approximately equal, that is, Yao's Theorem 1. When the number of equipment is switched, the overall operating efficiency of the multi-unit system is equal or the equipment is at the maximum load point, that is, Yao's Theorem 2. Yao's Theorem 1 and Yao's Theorem 2 are both proposed by the author for the first time.

articleTitle: Research on Power Information Digital Intelligent Integrated Network
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: With the intelligent upgrading of power system, the cybersecurity problems are becoming increasingly prominent, seriously threatening the national security and social stability. Therefore, in this study, through power information network modeling based on a network topology model, vulnerability analysis and state assessment of power information system, and software design of power information digital intelligence range based on PyQt5 and DeepSeek, we constructed a power information digital intelligence integrated network range to simulate cyber-attacks and defense drills, which helps the power system to develop efficiently, securely and sustainably.

articleTitle: Double Layer Optimization of Grid Connected Microgrids Considering Demand Side Response
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Microgrids have become the optimal solution to the problems of grid-connected distributed power sources and power supply in remote areas, but the current research lacks a holistic planning scheme. According to this problem, this paper establishes a grid-connected microgrid model containing wind turbine-PV-diesel and energy storage and proposes a two-layer configuration method for microgrids considering demand-side response. Among them, the upper-layer optimization model takes the lowest total cost as the goal for capacity allocation, and the lower-layer model takes the highest user satisfaction as the goal for operation optimization, and at the same time, the influence brought by the demand-side response is considered in the lower-layer optimization. Finally, the two-layer optimization model is simulated and analyzed, and the overall optimal configuration scheme is obtained by solving the two-layer optimization model using the Gray Wolf Algorithm (GWO), and the simulation results show that the cost of electricity consumption of the users in 24h is reduced by 13.3% and the overall revenue of the microgrid is improved by 1.7 times after considering the demand-side response and the two-layer optimization.

articleTitle: Research on Robot Path Planning Algorithm Based on Improved TD3
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: This paper is a research on robot path planning based on Improve Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic policy gradient (I-TD3) algorithm. Aiming at the problems of sparse rewards and waste of experience data in complex environments, the TD3 algorithm proposes to use the robot's explored experience as a reference point to guide the robot in path planning, which effectively improves the robot's action selection strategy in path planning in complex environments; meanwhile, it combines the reference point with the idea of artificial potential field to design a combined reward function, which mitigates the problem of sparse rewards; and it integrates the preferred hierarchical experience playback mechanism to reduce the waste of experience and improve the training efficiency of the algorithm. Experiments show that I-TD3 effectively improves the convergence speed of the network and its effectiveness in the path planning task.

articleTitle: Strategies to Improve the Resilience of Power Distribution Networks Under the Influence of Combined Extreme Weather
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: In recent years, the increasing frequency of typhoons and urban flooding incidents has significantly jeopardized the power supply security of distribution networks in coastal metropolitan areas. Given this critical situation, the strategic allocation of pre-disaster preparedness resources and post-disaster recovery resources has become paramount in enhancing the resilience of distribution networks. This study presents a comprehensive methodology for improving distribution network resilience through optimized pre-disaster resource deployment and post-disaster recovery scheduling. The proposed approach focuses on achieving efficient coordination among drainage systems, repair operations, and mobile energy storage system scheduling under complex extreme weather conditions, including typhoons, torrential rainfall, and urban inundation. The research methodology encompasses three main components: first, the development of a distribution network fault model that accounts for the compounded effects of typhoons and urban flooding; second, the formulation of an integrated model for pre-disaster resource deployment and post-disaster recovery operations, considering the distinctive characteristics of various recovery resources; and finally, the validation of the proposed strategy's efficacy through empirical case analysis. The findings demonstrate the effectiveness of this integrated approach in strengthening distribution network resilience against extreme weather events.

articleTitle: Research on Coordinated Control Strategy for Photovoltaic-Storage-EV Charging of Local Power Network
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: With the improvement of distribution network reliability requirements and the increase in the penetration rate of distributed adjustable source-load resources, traditional centralized control methods have issues like long scheduling cycles, slow response speeds, and difficulty in efficiently controlling complex power grids. This paper proposes a collaborative model, a dual-objective optimization control model, to reduce the load fluctuation degree of distribution transformers and increase the consumption of distributed photovoltaic power in distribution station areas. By comparing pre- and post-optimization results, it's concluded that accessing an appropriate capacity of energy storage and controllable charging piles is a prerequisite for collaborative control of distribution station areas to increase new energy consumption and reduce transformer load fluctuations. A reasonable collaborative control strategy for the distribution network can still change the load situation to some extent, achieve peak shaving and valley filling, and improve the load condition of distribution transformers.

articleTitle: Stability Control of Off-grid Photovoltaic Systems Using DC-DC Converters with MPPT Strategy
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: The paper discusses the design and optimization of a maximum power point tracking (MPPT) photovoltaic controller based on the STM32G431 microcontroller for off-grid solar power systems. Key features include the use of a DC-DC Buck converter, PI regulation, and the FreeRTOS operating system for real-time control. Experimental results highlight improved system efficiency, stability, and power output under varying sunlight conditions, thus making the controller effective for renewable energy applications.

articleTitle: Multi-Load Condition Grid Energy Storage Multi-Temporal and Spatial Scale Coordinated Optimization Control Method Based on GBO Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: In response to the difficulty of effectively ensuring the operational stability of the power grid under different load conditions, this paper proposes a multi-load condition power grid energy storage multi-temporal and spatial scale coordinated optimization control method based on the Gradient-based Optimizer (GBO) algorithm. Firstly, a multi-temporal and spatial scale model of power grid load and energy storage system was constructed. Then, the objective function for coordinated optimization control of energy storage in multi-load power grids at multiple time and space scales was constructed, and the constraints were determined. Finally, the GBO algorithm was used to optimize the capacity configuration, charging and discharging strategies, and scheduling of the energy storage system at different time scales, in order to achieve coordinated control of the energy storage system at multiple time scales. Through simulation verification and case analysis, the effectiveness of the proposed method in improving the flexibility, reliability, and economy of power grid operation has been demonstrated. This method provides a new approach and solution for the coordinated optimization control of multi-temporal and spatial scales in power grid energy storage systems.

articleTitle: Study on Evolution Mechanism of Single-Phase-to-Ground Fault Characteristics in Multi-Mode Neutral Grounding Mode of Large Generators
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: This study develops fault analysis models for three generator neutral grounding configurations: arc suppression coil, high-resistance, and ungrounded systems. The models establish fault current distribution principles and grounding parameter criteria. Using MATLAB simulations, we quantify characteristic evolution patterns of zero-sequence voltage and neutral current under varying transition resistances, elucidating grounding-mode-dependent fault characteristics. Multi-scenario comparisons demonstrate distinct amplitude and phase characteristics of fault signals across various grounding configurations. Finally, through the actual action case on site, the correctness of the simulation results is serious, which provides theoretical support for the grounding protection configuration and fault diagnosis of generator stator winding.

articleTitle: An Innovative Method for the State of Charge Estimation Utilizing an Enhanced Firework Algorithm and Levenberg-Marquardt Optimization Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: The state of charge (SOC) denotes a fundamental aspect of battery management systems (BMS). Reliable SOC calculation is vital to guarantee the optimal performance and risk-free use of electrical instruments. This research presents an advanced method for SOC estimation, utilizing a Backpropagation Neural Network refinement using the Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm (LMBPNN) for preliminary estimation. Building upon the LMBPNN, this study employs an enhanced Fireworks Algorithm (IFWA) for further optimization, conducting a comparative analysis with Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and the conventional Fireworks Algorithm (FWA). Comparative experiments were conducted using three typical driving conditions for cross-validation. The proposed intelligent SOC estimation method demonstrated high accuracy under the New European Driving Cycle (NEDC), as evidenced by the lessening of the average absolute error (AAE) to 1.4% and the root mean square error (RMSE) to 1.7%.

articleTitle: Optimization Method of Incentive Demand Response Strategy Considering User Participation Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: In view of the significant impact of the uncertainty of user participation on the implementation effect of grid demand response dispatching strategy, this paper designs an incentive demand response (DR) contract, which combines the enthusiasm advantage of user independent participation. The contract aims to deal with the randomness of residents' response behavior, and constructs an uncertainty model to characterize the relationship between user participation and grid incentives. The simulation results show that the demand response optimization strategy considering user participation uncertainty shows significant advantages and effectiveness.

articleTitle: Optimized Operation of the CCHP System based on MSCOA Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: This paper introduces an optimized energy management framework for scheduling CCHP operations, incorporating key components such as a gas-driven turbine, an absorption chiller, and an electric air conditioner To minimize operating costs, a Multi-Strategy Improved Coati Optimization Algorithm (MSCOA) is developed, considering system constraints and time-of-use tariffs. Case studies demonstrate that, compared to MSBWO, MSCOA reduces operating costs by 2.24% in summer and 4.55% in winter, and by 1.31% and 1.92%, respectively, compared to MSPSO.

articleTitle: A Non-Intrusive Household Load Monitoring Algorithm for High Frequency Based on Multi-Source Data
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: This paper proposes a high-frequency, non-intrusive household load monitoring algorithm using multi-source data. By constructing a multi-source time series data set with time as the coordinate axis, combining the adaptive splitting module, the multi-source analysis architecture model and the variable convolution module, the algorithm realizes the accurate decomposition of the household load. The algorithm considers environmental impact on electricity habits and performs dynamic high-frequency data analysis, enhancing load monitoring accuracy and efficiency.

articleTitle: Multi-Energy User Interactive Response Model Based on Dynamic Incentive Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: With the deepening of the energy revolution and the rapid development of new types of adjustable loads, the energy consumption and load characteristics of users are undergoing changes. Their energy consumption structures and method are more complex and diverse, and the adjustability of users has been greatly enhanced. Under the traditional dispatch operation mode, users are mostly receivers of market prices, and their own demand response potential has not been fully exploited. Therefore, a multi-energy user interactive response model based on a dynamic incentive mechanism is proposed in this paper. Considering users' satisfaction, comfort, and cost-benefit, an upper-layer users' comprehensive utility model is constructed; considering the energy purchase cost and sales revenue of the service provider, a lower-layer revenue model is constructed; in addition, considering the dual influencing factors of real-time yield rate and comprehensive energy efficiency, a dynamic incentive factor is constructed to dynamically update the retail contract price and demand response price of the service provider, effectively guiding users to actively participate in demand response and actively change their energy consumption demands. The example shows that the proposed method can increase the service provider's revenue by about 0.74% and the user's comprehensive utility by about 3%.

articleTitle: Research on Flexible Job Shop Scheduling Problem Based on Improved Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: On the basis of solving FJSP, this article designs an improved genetic algorithm using the idea of single chain integer encoding. It adopts encoding and decoding operations of single chain integer encoding, initializes population individuals, sets fitness functions, and uses the widely used “round robin” method in selection operations. In the crossover operation, the pre adopted multi-point crossover method was analyzed and improved. Finally, the multi-point crossover method will be applied to the machining sequence of workpieces and chromosome segments of machining machines. In the mutation operation, the processing sequence of the workpiece and the chromosome fragments of the processing machine are respectively subjected to reverse mutation and multi-point mutation, and iteration termination conditions are set. The proposed algorithm can not only divide the production task into multiple sub batches with flexible batches according to the production line capacity limit, but also optimize the processing sorting and production line selection. Simulation experiments have verified the effectiveness and feasibility of the improved genetic algorithm in solving FJSP.

articleTitle: Modeling and Adaptive Robust Control for an Electric Power Insurance Damage Claim Robot Joint Module
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: This paper studies the trajectory tracking control problem of robot joint modules. Based on the framework of constraint-following control, an adaptive robust controller is proposed. The controller is composed of two components: a nominal control term, derived from an accurate model, to stabilize the nominal system, and a robust control term to reduce the effect of uncertainties on tracking performance. Theoretical analysis and numerical simulation illustrate that the proposed control scheme ensures a satisfactory performance of the system.

articleTitle: Research on Fault and Protection Technology of PEDF System
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: DC circuit breakers are key equipment for the safe operation and protection of DC distribution networks. This paper studies the inter-pole short-circuit fault and protection of the PEDF system, and proposes a control and protection scheme based on a new all-solid-state DC circuit breaker. Firstly, a simulation model of the PEDF system is established in the PSCAD/EMTDC platform, and the fault response mechanism of the grid-connected converter when an inter-pole short-circuit fault occurs is analyzed and simulated and verified. At the same time, the topological structure and working principle of the new all-solid-state circuit breaker are briefly described. On this basis, a protection scheme for the PEDF system is designed, and relevant tests are carried out to verify the correctness of the circuit breaker design and protection scheme.

articleTitle: Dynamic Simulation of Compressed Air Energy Storage System in Energy Storage Phase Under Different Ambient Temperatures Based on Modelica Software
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: The compressed air energy storage (CAES) system represents a large-scale technology for electrical energy storage and conversion, which holds significant importance in integrating renewable energy into grids and balancing power grid loads. To enhance understanding of the CAES system's operational characteristics under diverse conditions, this study employs Open Modelica software to construct models of the energy storage phase and simulate parameter variation patterns of system components across different ambient temperatures. Analysis reveals that elevating ambient temperature shortens energy storage duration while reducing thermal dissipation from the air storage tank. Concurrently, the final temperature of the thermal storage tank rises, and although compressor power output increases, overall energy consumption by the compressor decreases.

articleTitle: Active Distribution Network Management System for the New Power System
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: With the progress of technology and the decrease in cost, the advantages of distributed energy in efficiency, environmental protection, and flexible deployment have become increasingly prominent, and the transformation of energy supply from centralized to distributed has become the trend of energy system evolution. The traditional passive distribution network management mode is no longer adapted to the increasingly complex operating environment. In order to improve the safety, reliability, and economy of the distribution network operation, the research on active management strategy has become a hot spot and frontier field. Based on the above background, this paper studies the new strategy of hierarchical optimization of active distribution network of multiple distributed energy, and proposes the platform architecture based on cloud side management for active distribution network, so as to promote the development of distributed energy and the consumption of high proportion of renewable energy.

articleTitle: Distribution Influence of Pump Sources on the Cooling Performance of the Cold Plate for a 4kW Laser Device
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: In the field of heat dissipation for fiber laser device, the pump source, as the core heat source of the fiber laser device, directly affects the diffusion path and efficiency of heat on the cold plate. This paper focuses on the pump source arrangement design for a 4kW fiber laser system, proposing three arrangement methods: linear, array, and hybrid configurations. Numerical simulation analyses were conducted using ANSYS FLUENT to evaluate the cooling performance of different arrangements. The results show that, with the hybrid arrangement, the maximum surface temperature of the cold plate is 30.57°C, a 15.32% decrease compared to the linear arrangement. Additionally, the hybrid arrangement offers better temperature uniformity on the cold plate, significantly improving the overall heat dissipation performance.

articleTitle: Research on Power Prediction of Distributed Photovoltaic Power Stations Based on TCN-GCN
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: In recent years, with the rapid growth of distributed photovoltaic installed capacity, the safety and economy of distribution networks are facing increasing challenges. The existing methods for predicting photovoltaic power generation typically rely on fine physical modeling or high-quality meteorological data, but this is often difficult to achieve in distributed photovoltaic systems. Therefore, this article proposes a ultra short term photovoltaic power generation prediction method based on TCN-GCN hybrid neural network, which can effectively extract spatiotemporal features from historical power generation data. This article uses the publicly available dataset provided by the National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL) to train the model, and compares the predicted results with four mainstream neural network models. The experimental results show that the TCN-GCN network performs excellently in prediction accuracy, with significantly reduced absolute mean error and square root error, proving that this method has important application value in the scheduling and management of distribution networks with distributed photovoltaic access.

articleTitle: Prediction of Slope Deformation at the Dam Inlet Based on GA-BP Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: The stability of dam intake slopes is critical to ensuring the safe and reliable operation of hydropower projects. Although backpropagation (BP) neural networks have been widely applied in slope deformation forecasting, they inherently exhibit limitations such as slow convergence and potential local minima issues. This study focuses on the left-bank intake slope of the Longtan Hydropower Station in Guangxi Province, where a hybrid genetic algorithm-BP (GA-BP) neural network model was developed to improve deformation prediction accuracy. Monitoring data collected from two distinct rock mass zones were meticulously selected and partitioned into training, validation, and test datasets for systematic analysis. Results demonstrate that the GA-BP model achieved high consistency with field-measured deformation trends. Specifically, the average prediction errors for measuring points M(4)1 and M(4)4 were 0.027 mm and 0.0070 mm respectively, representing significant improvements compared to the conventional BP model. In terms of computational efficiency, the GA-BP model converged to a precision of 2.46×10-6 within 12 iterations, whereas the BP model required 161 iterations to reach a lower precision of 2.3713×10-5. These findings highlight the GA-BP model's advantages in achieving faster convergence and higher prediction accuracy for dam slope deformation analysis.

articleTitle: Long-Term Reversible Hydropower System Operation Optimization Based on Fast Unit Commitment
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: To address the urgent demand for large-scale energy storage in renewable energy transition of China, this study proposes a schematic of reversible hydropower system and its long-term operation optimization model. By employing Fast Unit Commitment (FUC) algorithm, the model effectively reduces computational complexity while maintaining accuracy. Case studies demonstrate that the proposed method takes 1,000 times less time compared to nonlinear programming methods. With cascade reservoirs retrofitted into reversible hydropower stations, wind and solar curtailment rates decrease by 93.83% and 88.72<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, respectively, leading an annual profit increase of 0.47 billion CNY. These results show the algorithm's efficiency and the retrofit's economic benefit, providing critical insights for enhancing renewable integration in high-penetration grids.

articleTitle: Research on the Impact of Distribution Network Loop Closing Operation Based on the Random Forest Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: In order to accurately evaluate the influence degree of each influencing factor on the loop closing current, this paper adopts the random forest algorithm to analyze the influence degree of each influencing factor on the loop closing operation of the 10kV distribution network. Firstly, the loop closing current of the distribution network is calculated and the factors influencing the loop closing current are analyzed. Secondly, each factor is taken as a variable, calculate the loop closing current under the condition of changing these variables for 500 times. The values of each variable and the calculation results of the loop closing current are recorded and used as the data analysis samples for the random forest algorithm. Finally, the random forest algorithm is used to train each sample to obtain the influence degree of each influencing factor on the loop closing current. According to the results, the influence degree of each influencing factor on the loop closing current of the distribution network in descending order is: voltage phase angle, loop closing path impedance, output of distributed generators, load magnitude, voltage amplitude, and load distribution.

articleTitle: A Method for Detecting Insulator Defects in Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Aerial Photography Based on Improved YOLOv5
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: The background of insulator defects in transmission lines captured by drones is complex, and existing deep learning algorithms have low detection accuracy and usually require significant computational resources. To address this issue, we propose an improved YOLOv5 insulator defect detection algorithm in this paper. First, we introduce the GhostConv structure, and a G-C3 module is further designed to reduce the computational complexity. Then, we utilize a mobile attention mechanism and build a CA-S attention fusion module to improve the feature extraction capability of the network. Experimental results show that compared with the traditional YOLOv5 model, the average detection accuracy of the improved YOLOv5 proposed in the paper is increased by 1.9%, and the number of parameters is reduced by 12.5%. It is proved that the proposed algorithm has better performance than other popular algorithms in insulator defect detection of transmission lines.

articleTitle: Design Method for Finite Control Set Model Predictive Controller of Bilinear Converters with Stability Guarantees
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: In recent years, Finite Control Set Model Predictive Control (FCS-MPC) has attracted considerable attention in the field of power electronic converter control, resulting in numerous research achievements. However, the stability issues of FCS-MPC systems have not been thoroughly investigated to date, and traditional FCS-MPC controller design methods struggle to provide stability guarantees for the system. To address this issue, this paper proposes an FCS-MPC controller design method that ensures practical stability for a class of power electronic converters that can be modeled as bilinear systems. The proposed method theoretically guarantees system stability and steady-state performance. Therefore, compared to traditional design methods, it achieves good performance without the need for cumbersome parameter tuning. To verify the correctness of the theoretical results, simulations were conducted based on the mathematical model of a boost converter.

articleTitle: Analysis and Study of Excitation Inrush Current Characteritics of High-Impedance Power Transformer
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: With the development of economy and society, the problems of decreasing system impedance and serious excessive short-circuit current have generally occurred in the backbone network of large power grid interconnection and the urban power grid with large load concentration. The cost of circuit breakers will rise sharply with the growth of the demand for breaking capacity. In order to limit the short-circuit current on the low-voltage side of the transformer, the application rate of high-impedance transformers with low cost, small additional floor space and strong ability to limit the short-circuit current of the system is increasing. The high impedance transformer can increase the short circuit impedance to reduce the short circuit current without increasing the primary device, and has been widely used. This paper first introduces the definition and design principle of high-impedance transformer, and summarizes the realization methods of different high-impedance transformers; Secondly, the inrush current characteristics of the most widely used high-voltage built-in high-impedance transformer are analyzed, and the transformer model is established by Maxwell finite element simulation software. Finally, the inrush current of the high-voltage built-in high-impedance transformer is theoretically analyzed and summarized.

articleTitle: Research on ARC Discharge Detection in Switchgear Based on Improved YOLOv11
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Arc discharge faults in switchgear cabinets present critical challenges to power systems due to their stochastic occurrence, concealed characteristics, and complex physical mechanisms. To address the limitations of conventional detection methods in feature ambiguity and response latency, this paper proposes an enhanced YOLOv11-based intelligent detection framework. Three core innovations are implemented: 1) A deformable convolutional network (DCNv4) is integrated into the backbone, dynamically adapting receptive fields to capture irregular discharge morphologies; 2) A hybrid CNN-Transformer architecture synergistically fuses local spatial features with global contextual dependencies; 3) An adaptive bounding box regression strategy with parametric IoU loss optimization enhances multi-scale detection robustness. Experimental validation demonstrates superior performance, achieving 3.94% and 3.67% improvements over YOLOv8 and YOLOv10 respectively, confirming practical applicability in complex grid scenarios.

articleTitle: Gearbox Fault Early Warning for Wind Turbines Based on Mutual Information Recurrent Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: The damage and failure of the gearbox can directly or indirectly lead to the fault or shutdown of wind turbines, resulting in significant economic losses. To enable early warning of gearbox fault conditions, this paper proposes a fault early warning model for wind turbine gearboxes based on the mutual information recurrent network. Firstly, the maximal information coefficient is utilized to analyze the correlation between the operating parameters and the temperature of the gearbox output shaft. Highly correlated parameters are then extracted as input features for a recurrent neural network with memory capabilities. Following this, the residual distribution of the gearbox temperature under normal conditions is constructed, and a warning threshold is defined to realize early warning of the fault state of the wind turbine gearbox.

articleTitle: Loss Calculation of High Voltage DC Transformers Based on the Principle of Capacitive Transfer
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: A precise calculation method for system losses is proposed to address the power loss issue generated during the operation of DC transformers based on the principle of capacitive energy transfer (CET). Firstly, determine the functional relationship between bridge arm voltage and bridge arm current. Based on the relationship between the capacitor voltage of the submodule and the bridge arm voltage, determine the input quantity function of the single-phase bridge arm submodule using a rounding function. Establish a loss mathematical model by comprehensively considering the on state loss, switch loss, and converter valve on state loss types of the bridge arm submodule. The system loss can be accurately calculated by multiplying the number of submodules, bridge arm current, and conduction voltage drop. Analyze the distribution pattern of losses during bidirectional power transmission. Finally, the effectiveness of the loss calculation method proposed in this paper was verified through simulation.

Author Keywords: DC transformer based on CET principle

articleTitle: A Method for Identifying Multiple Interference Sources in Complex New Energy Grid Connection Based on Deep Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Due to the sub synchronous oscillation characteristics of complex new energy grid connection, the stability of power output cannot be guaranteed, resulting in low accuracy in identifying multiple interference sources. Therefore, a complex new energy grid connected multi interference source identification method based on deep learning algorithms is proposed. Using singular value decomposition (SVD) to remove interference source noise, extract interference source features, and obtain complex new energy grid connected multiple interference factors based on artificial intelligence models. Integrating attention mechanisms into deep attention networks to calculate the probability of interference source anomalies, achieving identification of multiple interference sources. The experimental results show that the deep learning algorithm proposed by the research method has very ideal convergence, and the AUC index under the research method is high, with a lower error rate, always remaining below 2%.

articleTitle: Fault Self Balancing Control Method for Medium and Low Voltage Distribution Equipment Based on Improved DQN Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: The faults of medium and low voltage distribution equipment have modular high-frequency chain conduction characteristics in the state space. If the chain influence degree of different fault modes is not considered and the faults are directly randomly controlled, the control resources will be unbalanced, and the number of faults cannot be effectively reduced. To reduce the frequency of power grid failures, a fault self balancing control method for medium and low voltage distribution equipment based on an improved DQN algorithm is proposed. Enhanced operator based on CEEMD algorithm to capture transient fluctuations in operating frequency in equipment operation data. Extract the features of multiple device operating status data, calculate their feature entropy values, and identify different device failure modes. Introduce a priority experience replay mechanism to improve the DQN algorithm, and determine the control priority of different fault modes based on the degree of chain influence in different fault state spaces. By calculating the reward value for executing control actions through loss and reward functions, the action with the optimal reward value is selected as the final fault execution action to achieve equipment fault control. The experimental results show that the designed fault control method effectively reduces the frequency of faults and the load rate affected by different equipment faults in practical applications, and can effectively control the losses caused by faults in distribution equipment.

Author Keywords: Medium and low voltage power grid

articleTitle: A Real-Time Single-Phase Ground Fault Localization Method based on Improved Attention Mechanism Graph Neural Network for Multi-Source Data Fusion
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: In this paper, a real-time single-phase ground fault localization method for multi-source data fusion based on an improved attention mechanism graph neural network (AM-GNN) is proposed. The method introduces an adaptive attention mechanism based on graph neural network (GNN), which enhances the ability to recognize key nodes and edges. Meanwhile, the accuracy and real-time fault localization are improved by integrating multi-source data and dynamically adjusting the importance of different data sources by using the attention weights. In addition, this paper adopts the spatio-temporal attention mechanism (STAM) to effectively handle multi-source temporal data, utilizing temporal convolutional networks and multi-head self-attention mechanism to capture the spatio-temporal characteristics of the data. The deep integration of AM-GNN and STAM is realized through an innovative two-way information flow and attention-guided feature fusion mechanism. Compared with traditional GNN methods, the method proposed in this paper better captures complex interactions in the system and demonstrates greater scalability when dealing with large-scale power grids. Experimental results show that the method outperforms existing methods in terms of fault localization accuracy and response time. This study provides a new solution for real-time monitoring and localization of single-phase ground faults in power systems, which is of great significance for improving the safety of power grid operation.

articleTitle: Research on Feature Size Recognition and Measurement of High Voltage Cable Joints Based on 3D Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: This paper presents a method for recognizing and measuring feature sizes at critical process nodes to enhance the installation quality of high-voltage cable accessories and address the issues of imprecise, inefficient, and poorly defined inspection techniques. The method leverages three-dimensional reconstruction, employing a normal vector condition segmentation approach integrated with principal component analysis, which enables precise point cloud segmentation of critical nodes, such as stripping, conductor crimping, and stress cone installation. Additionally, it facilitates point cloud acquisition at installation sites and non-contact measurement of key feature dimensions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can rapidly and autonomously identify key feature sizes with a measurement error of less than 1%, meeting field application requirements.

articleTitle: Influence of Power-Synchronization Grid-Forming Energy Storage on Short-Circuit Current
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: With the continuous expansion of the grid-connected capacity of power-synchronization grid-forming energy storage (PSGFES), its impact on the short-circuit current (SC Current) is increasing. The SC Current of the PSGFES under different limiting strategies are analyzed in detail. The variation of SC Current in the near area under different operating conditions of the PSGFES and different fault modes is analyzed by simulation. The influence law of PSGFES on the SC Current in the near bus is revealed from multiple angles, and the contribution amplitude of the energy storage to the SC Current of the grid-connected bus is quantified.

articleTitle: Fault Section Location in Active Distribution Networks Based on Traveling Wave and Graph Convolutional Network
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: The large-scale integration of distributed power sources has transformed the power flow structure of traditional distribution networks from unidirectional to multidirectional, increasing system complexity and posing challenges for fault location. Traditional methods struggle to handle the complex network topology and bidirectional power flow structure introduced by multiple power sources, resulting in reduced accuracy and robustness in fault location. Although deep learning techniques hold great potential for fault location, existing studies primarily focus on analyzing the features of individual nodes, neglecting the importance of the complex topological information in distribution networks, which is crucial for improving location accuracy. To address this, this paper proposes a fault location method based on Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN) and voltage traveling wave signals. Voltage traveling wave signals can rapidly transmit fault information when a fault occurs, while GCN can perform deep feature extraction considering the topological structure of the distribution network. By integrating voltage traveling wave signals and GCN, this method achieves precise fault section location in active distribution networks, and experimental results validate its effectiveness in such networks.

articleTitle: A Study of Parallel Configurable Collection Methods for Grid Data Information Containing Imbalance Samples
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: The current implementation of data synchronization mining and verification for configurable collection, processing, and sorting is mainly based on single cycles, resulting in low efficiency in data sorting. It is difficult to parallelize configurable collection in power grid data information containing imbalanced samples. Therefore, a parallel configurable collection method for power grid data information containing imbalanced samples is proposed. Using a multi-level approach, complete the multi-level sorting of parallel configurable data information. Based on this, a parallel configurable collection model for unbalanced sample power grid data information is constructed, and data synchronization mining and verification are used to achieve configurable collection and processing. The test results show that the relative error obtained by this design method is relatively small, which can improve the efficiency of data collection in complex background environments.

articleTitle: Edge-Optimized Defect Detection for Substation Insulators
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Insulator self-detonation defect detection is of great significance to ensure the stable operation of power system and prevent large-scale power outage.
