Traditional manual inspection and helicopter inspection methods have the limitations of high cost, low efficiency and strong environmental dependence. In this paper, a lightweight edge-optimized insulator self-detonation detection algorithm is proposed. By replacing the backbone network of YOLOv4 with MobileNetv3, depth separable convolution is used to reduce the number of parameters, and an improved loss function is designed to improve the detection performance. The DE-BiFPN module is further introduced to enhance the multi-scale feature fusion capability, and the C3TR module is combined to capture global information. Experimental results show that the detection accuracy of the improved model on the test set (mAP@0.5) is 1.65% higher than that of the original YOLOv4, the loss value converges to 0.71%, and the improved model exhibits strong robustness under complex background and small-target scenarios. Compared with Mobilenet-SSD, the proposed model reduces overfitting problems and significantly improves defect detection accuracy, which verifies its high efficiency and practicability on edge devices.

articleTitle: Approach on the Applicability of Leader Progression Flashover Criterion to the Simulation of Streamer Development Process in Long Gap Discharges
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Lightning is the main cause of power system line tripping. Studying gap discharge mechanisms under lightning impulses and establishing accurate flashover criterion models are crucial for evaluating transmission line lightning protection performance. The leader progression method has been widely recognized for its comprehensive consideration of the physical process of long gap discharges. The streamer and leader development are included in the model, but there is no research on the accuracy and applicability of the simulation of streamer development for this model. Therefore, this article calculates the streamer development time of various leader progression models proposed by different scholars under different rod-plate gaps, and compares and analyzes the accuracy and applicability of different leader progression models in simulating the streamer development process in rod-plate gaps. Finally, based on the results of the comparison and analysis, this article points out the deficiencies of existing models in simulating the streamer development process. The aforesaid research provides an important basis for subsequent research on adding models that conform to the physical process of streamer discharge development to the leader development flashover criterion.

articleTitle: Research on Key Technology of Photovoltaic-Energy Storage-Charging-Discharging Integrated System based on Electric Energy Metering
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: With the wide application of new energy generation methods such as photovoltaic power generation and the popularization of electric vehicles, how to integrate and plan the distribution of electric energy resources is the main problem facing the use and consumption of new energy. The PV-energy storage-charging-discharging integrated system aims to optimize resource allocation, and unify the planning and coordination of energy flow among PV power generation, energy storage, charging piles, and power-using equipment. This paper proposes an integrated PV-energy storage-charging-discharging system, analyzes the system structure and the functions of each system part, constructs a system optimization operation model, and finally simulates and analyzes the impact of optimization strategy on the peak and valley values of loads by taking electric vehicle loads as an example.

articleTitle: Fault Ride-Through Strategy for Grid-Forming Photovoltaic Systems under Unbalanced Voltage
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: This paper investigates the grid-forming control strategy for two-stage photovoltaic (PV) systems, focusing on addressing current imbalance and low-voltage ride-through (LVRT) challenges under grid asymmetric faults. An enhanced dual closed-loop positive/negative sequence decoupling control method is proposed: the positive- and negative-sequence components of grid voltage are separated using a real-time sequence decomposition algorithm, and reverse compensation currents are actively injected into the current control loop to suppress negative-sequence current components. Combined with virtual impedance technology, this method achieves rapid fault current limiting for inverter output. Simulation results demonstrate that under single-phase or two-phase short-circuit faults, the proposed strategy confines the PV inverter's fault current within safe limits while ensuring balanced three-phase operation and maintaining voltage-source characteristics to provide active voltage support. This method offers a reliable solution for renewable energy power stations to address extreme voltage imbalance scenarios, holding significant engineering value for the stable operation of integrated wind-PV-storage grids.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of Intelligent Thermal Insulation Protection System
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: To address the challenges of electronic components malfunctioning in high-temperature and hypersonic flow environments, the high cost of heat-resistant components, and the expensive research and development process, this study proposes a thermal protection system composed of air-cooling protection, cooling air ducts, and a data acquisition and control system. The system is established through model simplification and grid meshing, constructs a thermal protection layer using novel insulation materials, and employs an intelligent control system to optimize key influencing factors (e.g., air flow rate, wind speed) in real time. This enables precise control of internal temperatures for test motors, sensors, and air inlet/outlet temperatures within the system. Experimental results indicate that the average temperature of the motor and the average temperature of the air threshold in this system do not exceed 50°C, meeting the normal operating temperature range for electronic components.

articleTitle: Cyber Risk Detection for IEC 60870-5-104 Operation Commands in Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: To address the increasing cybersecurity challenges in distribution automation systems, this paper proposes a modeling method for International Electrotechnical Commission (IE C) 60870-5-104 protocol that integrates network layer traffic features and application layer protocol features. Through improved ARIMA (Auto-Regressive Integrated Moving Average) time series modeling and wavelet packet analysis, precise modeling of communication traffic is achieved. Based on information entropy theory, a protocol field correlation model is constructed, and combined with random forest and improved deep autoencoder to achieve efficient monitoring of remote control command anomalies. Experimental results demonstrate that this method shows significant advantages in both accuracy and real-time performance of anomaly detection.

articleTitle: A CMA-ES and LightGBM-Based Misoperation Prevention Method for Secondary Systems in Smart Substations
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: With the widespread adoption of smart substations, the secure operation of power systems imposes stricter requirements on secondary system maintenance. Addressing the issue of potential misoperations during state transitions of secondary equipment, this paper proposes a misoperation prevention method for secondary systems in smart substations based on the LightGBM model, with parameters optimized using the CMA-ES algorithm. Considering that the original signals of smart substation secondary systems are predominantly binary {O, 1} state quantities, this paper employs switch quantity encoding to define data groups. The CMA-ES algorithm is then applied to optimize the hyperparameter combinations of the LightGBM model, enhancing the efficiency of parameter tuning in an automated manner and overcoming the limitations of manual tuning. Finally, a misoperation prevention model for secondary systems in smart substations is constructed based on station-end information. Simulation tests using historical operational data demonstrate a misoperation prevention accuracy rate of 98.34%, thereby validating the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: A Distributed Photovoltaic Cluster Partitioning Method Based on Spatiotemporal Scalability and Feature Correlation Minimization (SSFCM)
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: We proposed a distributed photovoltaic (PV) cluster partitioning method based on spatiotemporal scalability and feature correlation minimization. By considering the temporal and spatial characteristics of distributed PV output curves, we introduced the capacity factor and dynamic time windows into the Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) calculation process, decomposing the output curves into multiple time windows. Building on the K-Means algorithm, we proposed a feature correlation minimization principle to guide the initialization of cluster centers, grouping distributed PV systems with similar output characteristics into the same cluster. Finally, by integrating meteorological data and historical PV output data, we constructed a MQ-RNN prediction model to effectively forecast PV output. The case study results demonstrated that the proposed method in this paper is capable of handling scenarios with inconsistent data, such as long-term intermittent missing data. It can reduce the clustering error of distributed photovoltaic systems, thereby improving the accuracy of power prediction for distributed photovoltaics.

articleTitle: Optimization of Energy Structure: The Role and Development Trend of Pumped Storage Power Stations in the Consumption of Renewable Energy
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: This paper discusses the important role of pumped storage power station (PSPS) in promoting the utilization of renewable energy. Firstly, the operating principle and advantages of PSPS are introduced, including peak load and valley filling, energy storage, frequency and phase regulation, black start and emergency backup. Secondly, it analyzes the influence of new energy and energy storage on the power grid, points out the challenges brought by the randomness, intermittency and volatility of new energy to the stable operation of the power system, and expounds the importance of the cooperation between energy storage facilities and renewable energy sources. Finally, the paper summarizes the energy efficiency and future development of PSPS, emphasizes its positive impact on augmenting the power system's flexibility, ensuring safety and reliability, and driving the adoption of renewable energy. On this basis, the future development trend is forecasted.

articleTitle: Control Parameter Identification of Photovoltaic Power Generation System Based on Grid Related Test Data
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: The modeling and Simulation of photovoltaic power generation system is an important means to verify its security and stability. However, the confidentiality of equipment control parameters and the complexity of control logic limit the accuracy of parameter identification. In this paper, a control parameter identification method of photovoltaic power generation system based on PSO algorithm is established, and the key information in the targeted network related test data is extracted to improve the accuracy of parameter identification. Finally, a practical example is given to verify the reliability and applicability of the method under various working conditions.

articleTitle: Frequency Regulation Reserve Optimization Considering Flexible Resource Complementary Aggregation
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: This paper proposes a fast-solving strategy that uses the complementarity of flexible resources to aggregate and participate in frequency regulation. Firstly, this paper proposes a frequency regulation performance index which can consider the adjustment rate, response delay time, adjustable capacity and adjustment cost of flexible resources. Then, based on the index, this paper uses the K-means algorithm to cluster the resources with similar performance. Then, this paper proposes an aggregation strategy considering the complementary of multiple flexible resources. Finally, this paper improves the unit combination optimization model, so that flexible resources can participate in the optimization in the form of aggregation, and the ratio of resources can be determined in advance, reducing the number of optimization parameters and improve the efficiency of solution. In this paper, the simulation is carried out on the IEEE-118 node. The results show that the proposed scheme can effectively improve the rate of optimization solution and effectively avoid the curse of dimensionality in the face of a large number of flexible resources.

articleTitle: Based on Improvement Immunity Algorithm Electrical Power System Optimal Power Flow Computation
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: This study presents an enhanced artificial immune algorithm specifically developed to address optimal power flow (OPF) problems in power systems. The algorithm is inspired by the immunological mechanisms of human and higher vertebrate immune systems, where the objective function and inequality constraints are conceptualized as antigens, while potential solutions within the search space are represented as antibodies. Solution evaluation and selection are performed based on affinity measures derived from antigen-antibody and antibody-antibody interactions. To maintain the comprehensive search capabilities of the foundational immune algorithm and ensure theoretical diversity, the concept of vector distance is incorporated into the algorithm's design. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through computational experiments conducted on the IEEE 30-bus test system, and a comparative analysis with conventional evolutionary algorithms, specifically genetic algorithms, indicates that the proposed algorithm exhibits superior global search capabilities and enhanced convergence properties.

articleTitle: Resource Potential Feature Extraction Method for Flexible Response of Power System Considering Uncertain Demand
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: To alleviate peak shaving pressure, a flexible resource potential feature extraction method based on uncertain demand is proposed for power systems, focusing on air conditioning, electric vehicles, and energy storage batteries. Build an uncertain demand response model and use set pair and fuzzy set algorithms to extract features. Simulation shows that the result error is controllable, showing a periodic positive correlation, and as the temperature rises, the response demand, resource potential, and system uncertainty all increase.

articleTitle: Research on Investment Decision Optimization Considering Power Grid Carrying Capacity
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: In the context of global energy transition, photovoltaic, wind power-based new energy scale, extensive access is the inevitable trend of grid energy transition development, with the new energy in the various voltage levels of distribution grid scale continues to rise, the grid presents new energy multi-level access, integrated consumption characteristics, in order to protect the new energy consumption and realize the precise investment, it is necessary to carry out the optimization of the investment decision considering the carrying capacity of the power grid research. This paper firstly establishes a grid carrying capacity assessment model to measure the carrying capacity of each voltage level for new energy, then considers the grid carrying capacity and other influencing factors to build an investment demand model, and coordinates the investment capacity of grid enterprises to establish a dynamic balance optimization model, by adjusting the investment capacity and the range of adjustable indicators in the investment demand model, and taking the minimum difference between investment demand and investment capacity as the target, and adopts the particle swarm algorithm to solve the problem, and uses the particle swarm algorithm to solve the problem. By adjusting the range of adjustable indexes in the investment capacity and investment demand measurement model, and taking the minimum difference between investment demand and investment capacity as the goal, the particle swarm algorithm is used to solve the model, and a regional power grid is used as an example to simulate and optimize the model to verify the feasibility.

articleTitle: Relay Protection Method for Medium and Low Voltage Distribution Network Considering Distributed New Energy Access
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: This article proposes a new method for relay protection in medium and low voltage distribution networks, targeting distributed new energy access while balancing reliability, adaptability, and economy. By constructing an objective function, analyzing the impact of new energy grounding, setting compensation coefficients, calculating protection delay and distance, establishing protection constraint intervals, and generating protection schemes. The experiment shows that this method has accurate setting values, high efficiency, and excellent protection performance.

Author Keywords: Medium and low voltage distribution network

articleTitle: Image Inpainting Algorithms for Drone-Containing Images based on GAN Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Image inpainting has become a crucial area in image processing, allowing for the automatic restoration of missing or damaged portions of images. This paper focuses on image inpainting techniques specifically for images containing drones. Using a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN)-based model, we propose a novel approach to restore drone images that may have missing sections due to occlusions, noise, or transmission errors. By leveraging the strengths of Variational Autoencoders (VAE) and GANs, our model learns to reconstruct the lost parts of the drone and its surrounding environment with high fidelity. The VAE captures the latent features of the drone, while the GAN enhances the realism of the generated image. We also incorporate an attention mechanism to ensure that fine details of the drone, such as propellers and body structure, are accurately restored. The proposed model is validated on a dataset of drone-containing images, showing significant improvements in inpainting quality compared to traditional methods.

articleTitle: An Improved Particle Swarm Optimization-Based Method for Assessing Distributed Photovoltaic Hosting Capacity in Power Grids
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: The phenomenon of power backflow caused by large-scale distributed photovoltaic integration has led to critical safety issues in medium-voltage distribution networks, including node voltage violations and reverse overload of distribution transformers. To address these challenges, this study establishes a distributed PV hosting capacity assessment model based on multiple constraints, such as power flow balance, voltage deviation, transformer load rate, and line current capacity. Furthermore, an improved particle swarm optimization algorithm is proposed to solve the model. Tests conducted on the IEEE 33 system and a real-world power grid demonstrate that the model effectively evaluates the safety and stability of the grid. Compared to traditional methods, the improved algorithm exhibits superior convergence speed and optimization capability. Under the same constraints, it achieves a higher PV hosting capacity and lower network losses.

articleTitle: Lithium Battery State Estimation and Life Prediction Based on Multi-Model Fusion
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: An approach to estimating the state of lithium battery and predicting its lifetime based on multi-model fusion is presented. The electrochemical behavior model is combined with data-driven model, and adaptive weighted PSO is introduced in order to improve prediction precision. Through multi-model weighted fusion, it can fully capture the multiple levels of battery state, which improves accurate prediction of battery aging process. This paper is experimentally verified on the MATLAB/Simulink simulation platform, using a lithium battery data set from actual tests. Experimental results show that the multi-model fusion method is better than traditional single-model method both in capacity forecast and residual life prediction. The MAE of capacity prediction is O.008Ah and the RMSE is O.012Ah, which is about 15% lower than the traditional method; the RMSE of remaining life prediction is 22.5 hours, which is about 25% less than the traditional method. This method not only maintains a high prediction accuracy under various usage conditions, but also shows strong robustness and adaptability.

articleTitle: Graph-Aided Teacher-Student Framework for Semi-Supervised Object Detection in Transformer Bench Inspection
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: This paper proposes a semi-supervised object detection method applied to transformer bench inspection, using a teacher-student framework enhanced by a Graph Neural Network (GNN)-based Teacher Assistant. By leveraging spatial dependencies between objects commonly found in transformer bench settings, the GNN refines pseudo-labels to improve detection performance with limited labeled data. Experiments demonstrate significant improvements in mean Average Precision (mAP) and F1-score compared to traditional semi-supervised methods, highlighting the effectiveness of the GNN-based Teacher Assistant in refining pseudo-labels and enhancing model robustness in this specific industrial application.

articleTitle: Intelligent Mobile Trash can Based on Speech Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: This paper designs a smart home device with TMS320F2812 to achieve the purpose of voice control of garbage can movement. This paper introduces the overall scheme design, car body driving design, program design, speech recognition design, function module design, etc., and finally expounds the production and debugging process. For the recognition of specific speech, the system uses SPCE061A voice chip to process the collected voice; With the pickup as the sound sensor, the source orientation is detected in real time by using the delay estimation method, and the sound source location is carried out. In order to avoid the complexity of the circuit board brought by discrete components, the H-bridge driving component L298N chip is used in the design. Through this system, we can realize the intelligent garbage can, humanization, and make our daily life more convenient.

articleTitle: Development of a GaN HEMT Type in Cascode Structure and Its Application to the Power Module used in the EEAT
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: With the New-type Power System construction progress of China, stricter requirements for the functionality and performance of the electricity energy acquisition terminal (EEAT) were proposed by the power grid designers. At present, there are sorts of EEATs using in the power grid such as DTU, the intelligent terminal and the distribution concentrator. The traditional power supply module of the EEAT was based on Si MOSFET, which had low operation efficiency and caused high electricity energy consumption. The power supply module in the new generation EEAT was required to be based on GaN HEMT (High Electron Mobility Transistor) to improve power supply efficiency, reduce operation temperature, achieve better stability and extend lifespan of the module, and it also could save more power during the usage process. In this article, a type of GaN HEMT device, which had 1100V+ voltage resistance capability was developed. A Cascode structure was introduced to design the GaN HEMT. Moreover, a power module based on the newly developed GaN HEMT was applicated. The efficiency of the GaN HEMT-based module was compared in specifications with a Si MOSFET-based module. The test results showed that the efficiency of power modules based on GaN HEMT was generally higher than that of Si MOSFET-based module. At present, the power modules based on GaN HEMT have implemented for batch application in the EEATs.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Economic Dispatch for Energy Internet Based on Price Quota Curves
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: This paper addresses the evolving role of the energy internet in the electricity market and the conflicts of interest arising from distributed energy sources. It proposes a hierarchical economic dispatch strategy for the energy internet, based on price quota curves. Utilizing Internet of Things technology, the distribution network is modeled as a regional energy internet, with the price quota curve facilitating the clearing process between the regional network and the public grid. The local energy internet aggregates distributed energy resources according to their attribution rights and incentivizes synergies between these resources and the distribution grid through dynamic pricing mechanisms. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through simulation.

articleTitle: Parameter Design and Optimization of Long-distance Multi-relay Wireless Power Transfer Systems at High Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: This paper presents a design and optimization methodology for a high-frequency long-distance multi-relay wireless power transmission system based on equidistant arrangement of relay coils. To obtain an accurate equivalent circuit model under high-frequency conditions, the study constructs frequency-dependent parasitic resistance fitting functions for both coils and capacitors, establishing a theoretical correlation model between transmission power and frequency. By formulating the objective of maximizing system output power, a systematic sweep analysis is conducted over the frequency range of 0.9-2.0 MHz to determine the optimal operating frequency. Furthermore, the research investigates the impact of relay coil parameter deviations and mutual inductance variations on transmitter coil current characteristics, offering improved design insights for system optimization. Simulation results substantiate the validity of the theoretical analysis, demonstrating the proposed framework's effectiveness in achieving desired performance metrics.

articleTitle: Defect Detection Method for Substation Equipment Based on Infrared Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: The long-term stable operation of substation equipment is very important for power supply reliability. Equipment faults often show abnormal heating, so the monitoring and diagnosis of thermal state is very important. Infrared thermal imaging technology can effectively carry out non-contact online detection, identify abnormal heating and prevent power failure. However, the current manual analysis method is inefficient and error prone, and the intelligent inspection platform still needs to manually process massive images. The existing defect identification methods have low accuracy and poor generalization ability. This study proposes a defect detection method based on infrared detection, using yolov7 to detect the target, decode the thermal sensor data, accurately locate the three-phase equipment, detect the defect based on the improved temperature difference identification method, realize automatic diagnosis, and improve the intelligent level of the substation.

articleTitle: Intelligent Enhancement of Distribution Networks Based on Swarm Intelligence Control in Complex Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: In response to the demand for intelligent enhancement of distribution networks, and to ensure the safety, stability, and efficiency of their operation, scheduling, and maintenance, we address the challenges posed by the low efficiency and accuracy of large-scale autonomous inspection applications. We have conducted research and applied key technologies for the intelligent enhancement of distribution networks based on swarm intelligence control in complex systems. Our work includes the investigation of situation awareness and risk assessment techniques, employing time-series early warning models to achieve precise control over the operational states of distribution networks. Additionally, we have explored grid-based deployment optimization techniques, utilizing intelligent analysis of digital grid topologies to optimize the placement of distribution network equipment. Furthermore, we have delved into attention mechanisms using graph neural networks as the carrier, effectively solving the problem of fault section localization in distribution networks with topological changes and multiple topological configurations.

articleTitle: Quantitative Analysis of Factors Affecting Transient Overvoltage of Wind Turbines
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: With the continuous increase in the proportion of new energy in the power system, the grid strength in wind power integration areas is relatively weak. The transient overvoltage after an AC short-circuit fault can trigger cascading faults, and in severe cases, it may lead to the disconnection of wind turbines from the grid. Existing literatures have conducted detailed analyses on the generation mechanism and suppression measures of transient overvoltage. However, few literatures have carried out a quantitative analysis of the impact of the internal control system of wind turbines on transient overvoltage. Based on the grid-connected model of the Doubly Fed Induction Generator (DFIG) and combined with the MATLAB/Simulink simulation model, this paper uses a mathematical analytical method to derive the analytical expressions of the transient overvoltage with respect to the control parameters, so as to solve for the maximum value of the transient overvoltage. The correctness of the conclusions is verified through MATLAB/Simulink simulations.

articleTitle: Online Error Evaluation of CVT Based on Memory and Prediction Enhanced Temporal Convolutional Autoencoder
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Capacitor voltage transformers (CVTs) are critical components in high-voltage energy metering, and their measurement accuracy directly impacts the fairness of energy billing. However, environmental factors can cause CVTs to degrade over time, leading to measurement errors and potential system instability. This paper proposes an online evaluation method for CVTs using the Memory and Prediction Enhanced Temporal Convolutional Autoencoder (MPE- TCA). The model incorporates memory and prediction modules to enhance anomaly detection and improve data reconstruction accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that the model outperforms other models in terms of accuracy, precision, and recall, effectively capturing normal data patterns and detecting anomalies. The proposed method provides a reliable solution for real-time CVT monitoring in modern power systems.

articleTitle: Understanding Safety Risk Warning Technologies for Lithium-Ion Battery Energy Storage Power Stations from an Engineering Perspective
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: As an important part of the new power system, the safety of lithium-ion battery energy storage power station may pose a potential threat to personnel, environment and equipment. At present, there are a variety of safe operation risk early warning technologies, but the concepts of “early warning” and “alarm” are often confused and difficult to distinguish. In this paper, firstly, the connotation of safety protection of lithium-ion battery energy storage power station is deeply analyzed, the development map of safe operation risk is constructed, and the characteristic signals and technical measures at each stage are determined. Then, different early warning technologies are compared, and the adaptability of early warning technology based on battery external signal and operation data is analyzed. Finally, the application of early warning technology in engineering is counted, and based on the risk early warning technology developed by the team, the occurrence probability of common risks is analyzed to provide reference for research and application.

articleTitle: Improved CGAN for Short-Term Wind Power Forecasting based on Heat Maps and LSTM-CNN
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Wind power generation plays a crucial role in maintaining grid stability and achieving sustainable energy goals, making accurate forecasting of electricity generation capacity essential for efficient power system operation. Traditional Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks (CGAN) face limitations in condition selection and spatiotemporal feature extraction, affecting their forecasting accuracy. This paper presents a modified model that addresses these challenges through an innovative integration of deep learning architectures. The proposed model employs a data-driven approach to select weather conditions with the highest correlation as conditional information, utilizing heat map analysis to identify the most significant predictive factors. Temporal characteristics are captured through Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, while spatial features are extracted using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), creating a comprehensive framework for feature analysis. The model's effectiveness is validated through extensive experiments across different seasons using real-world data from operational wind farms. Results demonstrate superior forecasting precision compared to conventional methods, with significant improvements in Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE). The enhanced generalization capability and robust performance make this model particularly suitable for power grid scheduling applications, contributing to more reliable and efficient renewable energy integration.

articleTitle: The Thermal Simulation Analysis of Air Cooling Performance of 18650-Type Lithium-Ion Batteries
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: This paper conducts a simulation study on the air cooling performance of 18650-type lithium-ion batteries using COMSOL<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1]</sup>. The research findings indicate that air cooling significantly enhances the thermal management performance of the batteries. Detailed analyses were performed on the temperature distribution under different wind speeds. This study provides valuable references for optimizing the design of lithiumion battery cooling systems.

articleTitle: Scheduling of the DC Microgrid Group Integrating Mobile Energy Storages Under Power Rationing
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Direct current microgrids (DCMGs) may face power rationings in the case of power shortage, resulting in significant load interruptions and economic losses. To address the problem, mobile energy storage (MES) is used to realize energy sharing between multiple DC microgrids in this paper. First, a new spatiotemporal transfer model of the MES based on travel frequency is established. MES's flexible charging and discharging constraints are also developed. On this basis, an energy scheduling strategy of the DC microgrid group integrating MESs under power rationing is designed, where the battery operational limit and the power balance constraint are considered. This scheduling model is directly solved using commercial solvers. Finally, the case study validates the superiority of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Knee Osteoarthritis MRI Image Classification Method
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: In the classification of knee osteoarthritis (KOA) using MRI images, the application of end-to-end deep learning techniques holds significant importance. The raw knee joint images contain multiple complex attributes, including shape, size, and spatial position, all of which critically influence the performance of neural networks in KOA classification. However, knee joint imaging often exhibits intricate anatomical structures and subtle variations, particularly when different categories share high similarities. Traditional methods face limitations in extracting fine-grained features, making it challenging to distinguish key discriminative patterns among different classes and increasing classification difficulty. Moreover, conventional convolutional neural networks (CNNs) primarily rely on a hierarchical stacking of layers, where single convolutional kernels focus on capturing local features at the input stage. This approach frequently results in the loss of critical fine details within images, leading to suboptimal classification performance. To address the challenges of inadequate local feature extraction and class imbalance in KOA MRI classification, this study introduces a classification network based on the Swin Transformer. By integrating multiple novel modules and optimization strategies, the proposed model aims to enhance classification accuracy and improve generalization performance.

articleTitle: Dynamic Simulation Technology Research of Variable-Velocity Pumped Hydro-Storage Unit
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: This paper focuses on the research of dynamic simulation technology of Variable - velocity pumped hydro - storage unit. It elaborates on the development status and key technologies of Variable - velocity pumped hydro - storage unit, including their structural characteristics, operation modes, and advantages. The dynamic simulation technology of Variable - velocity pumped hydro - storage unit is introduced in detail, such as the methods and processes of establishing mathematical models and building dynamic simulation test systems. Through the research of these technologies, important support is provided for the safe and stable operation of Variable - velocity pumped hydro - storage unit.

Author Keywords: Variable - velocity pumped hydro - storage unit

articleTitle: Research on the Network Security Protection Model of the New Power System
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: In the process of promoting the construction of the new power system, in view of the current situation that the network structure of the power system is becoming increasingly complex and the network's closed nature is gradually being broken, this paper proposes a terminal network security protection model based on the zero-trust concept. Starting from six aspects: policy, isolation, identification, protection, detection, and response, this model realizes controlled and secure access to resources through the all-round closed-loop management of the users, hardware, software and behaviors of network entities. Through this model, not only has the protection ability of the new power system against network threats been significantly enhanced, but it also provides new ideas and practical references for the research and design of network security protection in future power systems.

articleTitle: Research and Design of Home Photovoltaic Storage Monitoring System Based on Microcontroller Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: With the rapid development of the global economy, energy shortage and environmental pollution have become severe problems facing the current situation, which has promoted the development of renewable power generation. Among many renewable energies, photovoltaic power generation occupies an extremely important position. However, there is a feature intermittent power generation in the photovoltaic power generation process, and the application of the battery energy storage system in the photovoltaic power generation system store surplus electricity in the peak period of electricity generation, and release the electricity stored in the energy storage system in the valley period of electricity generation, suppress the fluctuation of, adjust the output power of the system, and improve the stability and safety of the system operation. At the same time, due to the instability of the battery energy system and the delay of the system, the whole system may have the phenomenon of overcharging and discharging of the battery, the voltage is too high to form a circuit inside the battery and other safety hazards. In view of the above problems, this paper designs a home photovoltaic storage monitoring system based on single chipcomputer technology. The system realizes the storage and output of energy through the combination of photovoltaic and storage, and at the same time, it monitors and the battery storage system in real time, effectively avoiding the occurrence of accidents, reducing losses, and making the home photovoltaic storage system operate more efficiently, safely and reliably.

articleTitle: Study on the Breakeven Point of Human Transportation Distance in Mechanized Construction of 220kV and 500kV Overhead Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Mechanized construction is an important part of State Grid Corporation, and mechanized construction of overhead transmission lines in mountainous areas is a major challenge. The breakeven point of human transportation distance is an important indicator for selecting tower locations for mechanized construction in mountainous areas. This paper is based on a survey of the foundation types of mechanized construction in mountainous areas, discussed the cost calculation differences between mechanized construction of overhead transmission lines and conventional construction and analysis the breakeven point for typical terrain conditions of 220kV and 500kV lines, the results show that: (1) the breakeven points are between 63-125m on 220kV transmission line, and that of 500kV transmission line is 233-421m which is higher than that of 220kV and 110kV. (2) The breakeven point of rock anchor foundation is greater than that of mechanized pile foundations on same condition, indicating that the economic benefits of rock anchor foundations are relatively high.

articleTitle: Continued Research of Interleaved Parallel and Secondary Coupled Switched Inductance Boost Converter
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: This paper is a further Study on the basis of the previous paper “Study on interleaved parallel and secondary coupled switched inductance Boost converter”. The former only analyzes the working mode, voltage gain and simple voltage stress. In this paper, the voltage, current stress and critical inductance values of each component are analyzed in detail. Finally, simulation experiments are carried out to verify the correctness of the analysis.

articleTitle: Modal Identification of External Vibration Signals of Transmission Lines Based on TDM-MIMO Millimeter Wave Radar
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: After external impact, the frequency component of the vibration signal undergoes transient attenuation, which may be mixed with low-frequency electromagnetic interference, leading to misjudgment. To this end, a modal identification method for transmission line vibration signals based on TDM-MIMO radar is proposed. High quality signals are captured using sparse transmit and dense receive antenna arrays, decomposed into multiple eigenmode function components, and classified using an extremum learning machine. Experimental results have shown that this method achieves an accuracy of 99.04% in separating frequency components and identifying vibration modes, which is accurate and effective.

articleTitle: Research on Zero-Sequence Transfer Suppression in Non-isolated Medium Voltage Flexible DC Interconnected System
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: In order to realize the fault ride-through of non-isolated medium-voltage flexible-direct interconnected system under single-phase-to-ground fault, the fault characteristics and the generation and transmission mechanism of zero-sequence component are analyzed: the zero-sequence component generated by the fault side will be transmitted to the non-fault network through the DC side, resulting in voltage imbalance in the non-fault network. Aiming at the shortcomings of other suppression strategies, such as low economy and complex control, this paper proposes a method to suppress the fluctuation of DC bus voltage by configuring a series compensation circuit on the DC side. The corresponding control algorithm is designed to suppress the transmission of zero-sequence components and ensure the voltage balance of non-fault network. Finally, the simulation model is established in Matlab/Simulink to verify the theoretical analysis and the proposed fault control.

articleTitle: Dynamic Modelling of Multiple Faults in Tidal Stream Turbines
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Tidal stream turbines (TSTs) operate in complex seabed environment, rendering them highly susceptible to various faults, including impact faults, biofouling, and demagnetization. Additionally, the high energy density of the seabed, combined with the TSTs' small rotational inertia, increases their sensitivity to variations in tidal velocity. To reduce the impact of tidal velocity variations on fault detection and improve detection precision, a fault model incorporating multiple faults based on the TST's dynamic characteristics has been developed. The impact of tidal velocity is minimized through system decoupling and linearization. Simulation experiments demonstrate that additive faults in the TST can be effectively detected using the constructed model.

articleTitle: Research on Lightning Trip Risk Assessment Method of Overhead Transmission Line Based on Multi-Dimensional Information Fusion
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: The risk assessment of lightning strike trip rate of overhead transmission lines is an important factor for the safe operation of power grids. Aiming at the existing risk assessment methods of lightning strike trip rate of overhead transmission lines, which have problems such as low precision and large artificial influence of assessment factors, this paper proposes an improved evidence theory method for lightning strike trip risk assessment on the basis of multidimensional information fusion. The weights of different characteristic factors are given by entropy weighting method, the distribution functions of different characteristic factors are determined by gray correlation theory, and then fused and the risk level is determined by evidence theory. The feasibility of the method is proved by analyzing the lightning strike trip rate of towers and lines through tests. The results show that the assessment results of the proposed method are basically consistent with the actual situation. The calculated line lightning strike trip rate is 2.3309 times/year per 100 kilometers, and the relative error with the actual value is 0.034, and the accuracy of the lightning strike trip risk of the whole grid overhead transmission line is 96.8%. This study provides a certain reference for transmission line disaster early warning analysis.

articleTitle: Modeling and Overvoltage Simulation Analysis of ±800kV UHVDC Transmission System
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Based on PSCAD simulation platform and practical engineering parameters of ±800kV Hami - Zhengzhou Project, a system model of ±800kV UHVDC transmission system including DC filters, DC lines and other key equipment is established. The main components of the model are introduced. Based on the established system model, the time domain simulation of AC side and pole grounding faults under bipolar full voltage conditions is carried out, and the operating characteristics of the simulation model under the above faults are analyzed. The simulation results show that the model can accurately simulate the steady-state and transient operating characteristics of UHVDC transmission systems, and can be used as an effective tool to study UHVDC transmission systems.

articleTitle: Optimization of Economic Dispatch for AC-DC Hybrid Microgrid with Electric Vehicle Participation
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Under the dual-carbon background, the sudden increase in the number of electric vehicles (EVs) entering the grid poses a challenge to the safe and economic operation of microgrids. In this paper, the dispatchable capacity models of private electric vehicle cluster (PEVC) connected to the grid at night and network-connected electric vehicle cluster (NEVC) connected to the grid during daytime are developed based on Monte Carlo sampling, Minkowski summation method and LSTM neural network algorithm. On this basis, a mixed-integer second-order cone planning (MISOCP) model for AC-DC microgrids is constructed with the objective of cost optimization and taking into account the solution efficiency and accuracy. The example results demonstrate that implementing time-of-day tariffs leads to a 15.05% reduction in the cost of microgrid operation compared to disordered charging. This is achieved through an orderly charging and discharging strategy that considers the load and storage characteristics of electric vehicles (EVs).

articleTitle: Design and Experimental Study of a Small Concentrating Solar Distillation Device
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: This paper uses a linear Fresnel lens as a concentrator and a solar vacuum tube as a receiver to form a small collector distillation device using a polar axis tracking method. The experiment was carried out under sunny conditions, and the concentrating system, heat collecting system and device performance of the distillation device were analyzed respectively. The results show that the fluctuation range of the geometric concentration ratio of the concentrating system is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{0.0867}\sim \mathbf{0.1067}$</tex> at low wind speed, and the concentrating situation is relatively stable. Although the heat collection efficiency of the concentrating collector is mostly slightly smaller than that of the non-concentrating collector, the temperature in the concentrating collector rises rapidly at the same time. In the test time range of 12:18 to 14:00, the total water production was 0.21 L, and the gained output ratio of the device was calculated to be 0.5. The device has the advantages of cheap materials, stable light concentration, and light structure. It can be applied to areas such as poverty, lack of water resources, and complex terrain.

articleTitle: Secure Transmission Method of Power Communication Network based on Illegal Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Based on the security problem in electric power communication network, this paper studies the safe transmission method of electric power communication network based on illegal intelligent reflective surface. We studied IRIS-assisted eavesdropping scenarios, and jointly optimized transmitted beamforming and illegal beamforming to maximize the overall safety rate. We combine model-free meta-reinforcement learning with strategy gradient method to solve the problem of slow convergence and poor generalization. The simulation results show that the meta-reinforcement learning method proposed in this paper can effectively reduce the harm of IRIS, and compared with the traditional reinforcement learning algorithm, the algorithm can improve the total safety rate.

articleTitle: Operational Risk Assessment and Configuration of a Novel Urban Distribution Grid Accounting for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Currently, the widespread use of distributed energy and electric vehicles (EVs) poses operational risks to distribution networks, particularly due to the uncertainties introduced by the output of photovoltaic (PV) and wind power, as well as the random charging loads of EVs. This paper focuses on voltage excursion risk, treating it as a critical indicator of distribution network operation. A Frank-Copula function-based model is constructed to represent the correlation between PV and wind power generation, and further developed with historical data to refine the stochastic charging model for EVs. Utilizing Monte Carlo simulation, the operational risk of the distribution network under various scenarios is evaluated, including situations without EV charging loads and with EV charging loads at different nodes. The study reveals that the integration of distributed energy into the distribution network may lead to issues such as voltage excursions. However, by adjusting the point of EV access, the impact of distributed energy and EV charging loads on the distribution network can be effectively balanced, thereby reducing operational risks to some extent.

articleTitle: AoI-Based Delay Analysis of PLC Relay Metering Network
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Power line communication (PLC) is widely used in metering communication networks, and it is necessary to solve the problem of delay performance analysis under relay conditions. Therefore, aiming at the power line communication metering network based on multi-hop relay, this paper establishes the power line multi-hop relay model based on lognormal distribution fading. Taking two-hop relay model as an example, the closed expression of the average age of information (AAoI) of the system under automatic retransmission is derived by using M/G/1 queuing system and P-K formula. Monte Carlo simulation is used to verify the validity and reliability of the system model, and the effects of distance between nodes and arrival rate on the age of information performance are compared and analyzed. It provides theoretical and technical support for practical application.

articleTitle: Numerical Study on Free Cooling and Mass Distribution in a Pump-Driven Two-Phase Cooling Loop for Data Centers
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Generally, the integrated cooling system in data centers consists of a vapor compression (VC) loop and a pump-driven two-phase cooling (PDTPC) loop. The PDTPC loop, utilizing free cooling without compressor operation, is a promising energy-saving technology for data center cooling. However, research on the factors influencing the upper limit of free cooling temperature and refrigerant mass distribution in the PDTPC loop remains limited. This study developed a steady-state numerical model to investigate the effects of pipe pressure drop and vapor quality on these parameters. Results show that reducing the pressure drop between the evaporators and condenser significantly increases the upper limit of free cooling temperature. Additionally, reducing the pressure drop between the condenser and reservoir substantially decreases the refrigerant mass in the condenser. Operating at high vapor quality is beneficial to increase the upper limit of free cooling temperature and reduce refrigerant mass in the pipes, evaporators, and condenser. A reservoir is essential to manage changes in refrigerant mass distribution. This work provides theoretical guidance for extending the annual utilization of free cooling and reducing refrigerant charge in the practical application of the PDTPC loop in data centers, thereby improving energy efficiency and reducing overall costs.

articleTitle: Optimization of Equalizing Ring Attachment Angle Based on COMSOL Simulation
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: The evolution of ultra-high voltage (UHV) transmission technologies has rendered difficulties such as electric field distortion and corona discharge increasingly significant. Contemporary research primarily emphasizes the dimensional attributes of voltage equalizing rings, although little attention has been directed into the impact of the attachment angle of these rings on electric field modulation. This research employs COMSOL Multiphysics simulations to investigate the influence of the attachment angle of the voltage equalizing ring on the electric field distribution along a 500 kV transmission line. The findings indicate that an ideal attachment angle of 50° to 60° markedly decreases the electric field intensity adjacent to the insulator edges, offering critical insights for the construction of high-voltage transmission lines.

articleTitle: Research on Optimized Operation of Regional Integrated Energy System Based on SAPSO Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Achieving efficient use of energy by optimizing the regional integrated energy system is conducive to further attaining the goal of carbon neutrality and carbon peaking. This paper takes a foreign park as the research object and its annual operating cost as the optimization target, establishes an optimization model, and uses the SAPSO algorithm to solve the model. The results show that the annual operating cost can be effectively reduced, and the economic optimization of the park's integrated energy system can be realized.

articleTitle: Optimal Design of LLCL Parameters Based on APSO
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: For the novel LLCL structure, current research primarily focuses on damping strategies. For instance, [4] developed a biquad filter-based active damping method combined with a proportional-integral multiresonant repetitive controller. However, the control strategy must be adjusted accordingly, increasing the complexity of the control algorithm and reducing system reliability and robustness. In contrast, research on LLCL filter parameter design is limited. [5] determined the parameters of each filter component through iterative calculations under various constraints, but this method is complex and often relies on empirical tuning, leading to imprecision.

articleTitle: The Energy Management Optimization Algorithm for User-Side AC Voltage Stabilizers Based on Flexible DC Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: This paper proposes an energy management optimization algorithm for user-side AC voltage stabilizers based on flexible DC technology. The algorithm combines real-time load forecasting and electricity price data analysis, using Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to optimize energy scheduling. Experimental results show that the proposed algorithm effectively reduces system operation costs and improves the stability and economy of the power system, especially in a time-of-use pricing environment.

articleTitle: Data Analysis and Intelligent Scheduling of Power Customer Service Based on Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: With the increasing complexity of power demand forecasting, traditional methods face challenges in handling multiple influencing factors. This paper proposes a power load forecasting model based on the Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT) to improve the accuracy and stability of power demand forecasting. By introducing a variable self-attention mechanism and gating mechanism, the TFT model effectively captures long-and short-term dependencies, while considering external factors such as weather and holidays that affect power demand. The study further enhances the model's forecasting capability and robustness through optimization strategies like multi-step forecasting, deep feature crossing, and model fusion. Experimental results show that the optimized TFT model demonstrates outstanding performance in power load forecasting, providing strong support for intelligent power scheduling.

articleTitle: Circulating Current Control in Underground Cables with Distributed Sheath Compensation
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Underground power cables, commonly laid using duct banks or cable trenches, face significant challenges due to high groundwater levels that lead to submerged manholes. This not only complicates the installation of diagnostic devices like partial discharge detectors and fault locators but also threatens cable integrity. To manage these issues, cable sheath transposition boxes and grounding boxes are connected via coaxial cables and installed above ground. However, frequent changes in road planning often necessitate relocating these boxes, causing the coaxial cable lengths to exceed the standard 10-meter limit. This results in faults, such as damaged sheath protectors and partial discharges at neighboring joints. Addressing issues like excessive sheath grounding currents and defect detection in cable sheaths is vital to extending cable life, reducing maintenance costs, and ensuring reliable operation of high-voltage cable systems. This paper proposes a Distributed Cable Sheath Compensation (DCSC) controller that aims to reduce sheath grounding currents and enhance system stability by optimizing compensation reactance.

articleTitle: Improving Intelligent Substation Communication Network Fault Location with Multi-view Contrastive Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: The occurrence of communication network failures in intelligent substations lead to communication interruptions and abnormal operation of the power system. Accurate fault location is crucial for timely restoration of normal network operation. The traditional fault location methods for communication networks in intelligent substations often focus on static network structure analysis, which is difficult to adapt to the dynamic changes in the network. This article proposes an intelligent substation communication network fault localization method based on multi view contrastive learning. This method does not rely on additional temporal network parameters and can effectively achieve representation learning and fault localization of dynamic networks. Treating dynamic network snapshots as multiple views eliminates the dependence of contrastive learning on data augmentation. By constructing a comparative learning objective function that includes three views: network structure, node evolution, and topology evolution, we can deeply explore the evolution patterns of network structure within snapshots, nodes between snapshots, and higher-order network structures to learn node representations and complete fault localization tasks. The experimental results of multi class dynamic fault location on multiple real data sets show that this method is significantly better than all baseline methods, which strongly verifies the effectiveness and progressiveness of the proposed method in fault location of intelligent substation communication network.

articleTitle: Enhancement of CIGS Solar Cell Performance Parameters Using Zn2P3 as Back Surface Field and SnS2 as Buffer Layer
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Copper indium gallium selenide (CIGS) thin-film solar cells with high conversion efficiency, high light absorption coefficient, high stability, tunable forbidden bandwidth, and strong radiation immunity are the main reason for the high interest of researchers. Cadmium sulfide (CdS) is commonly used as a buffer layer in some CIGS-based solar cells. However, CdS is hazardous and can adversely affect the environment. In this work, we propose to use non-toxic tin sulfide (SnS2) as a buffer layer for CIGS cells because it has good optical transparency and electrical conductivity, which makes it an ideal buffer layer material. Secondly, we recommend inserting Zn2P3 as the back surface field (BSF) between the absorber layer and the back contact layer of the cell to enhance the cell performance. By simulating the Al-ZnO/SnS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/CIGS/Zn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/Mo solar cell structure utilizing SCAPS-1D software, we explored and analysed the effects of absorber layer thickness, buffer layer concentration and defect density on photovoltaic parameters. The efficiency of the optimized device structure can reach 30.45% (under AM 1.5 G illumination). This helps to improve our understanding of CIGS solar cells for better performance of solar cells.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Early Warning Method for High Voltage Power Equipment Risks Based on Cloud Modeling and Random Forest
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: The conventional risk intelligent early warning method for high-voltage power equipment mainly uses the WebService interface to calculate the similarity of risk early warning characteristics, which is vulnerable to the impact of spatio-temporal correlation fluctuations, leading to abnormal early warning in some states. Therefore, a risk intelligent early warning method for high-voltage power equipment based on cloud model and random forest is proposed. That is, the cloud model and random forest are used to extract the operation characteristics of high-voltage power equipment, and the intelligent risk early warning algorithm of high-voltage power equipment is designed, thus completing the intelligent risk early warning of high-voltage power equipment. The experimental results show that the average warning delay of the design method is 1.1ms, and the root mean square error of the warning does not exceed 0.05, which has certain application value.

articleTitle: Multi-Label Image Recognition Algorithm Based on Convolutional Block Attention Module
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: This paper proposes a multi label image recognition algorithm based on CBAM (Convolutional Block Attention Module) to address the issue of partial feature neglect in multi label images. The algorithm constructs a co-occurrence matrix between labels using a graph convolutional neural network, and uses a ResNet-34 network based on CBAM as an improved convolutional neural network to form a new recognition network.

articleTitle: Two-Stage Bi-Level Multi-Objective Optimization Model for Equilibrium Analysis of Electricity and Carbon Markets
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Under the influence of the carbon market, the coupling between the medium- and long-term (MLT) market and the spot market becomes increasingly complex. Generation companies (Gencos) face high-dimensional decision-making problems, leading to diverse market equilibrium outcomes. To address this issue, a two-stage bi-level modeling framework is established. In the upper level, the bidding strategies of Gencos are modeled. In the lower level, the electricity and carbon markets clearing are modeled in two stages. The MLT market is cleared first, and its clearing results are passed to the spot market and carbon market clearing models. To solve the model, the diagonalization method (DM) algorithm is employed. Finally, based on the cases of physical delivery and financial delivery, different carbon reduction targets and new energy output scenarios are analyzed. The results show that, compared to financial delivery, transitional delivery can lower market electricity prices and reduce the impact of new energy output fluctuations on the market. However, it also reduces the revenue of Gencos. The carbon reduction cost is on average 25.34% higher than under financial delivery.

articleTitle: Optimal Design of Heat Dissipation Structure and Experimental Verification of MFT Considering Insulation Performance
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Although the increase in frequency improves the transmission efficiency of medium-frequency transformers (MFTs), the heating problems of MFTs are more serious than those of conventional power transformers due to the increase in core losses and winding losses. After testing the insulation properties of insulating materials at 1~20 kHz, the internal insulation structures of the medium frequency transformer (MFT) were designed to avoid breakdown or flashover occurring during long-term operation. Subsequently, heat dissipation methods were proposed for MFT models with different volume requirements. Finally, a natural air-cooled MFT prototype with the rated parameters of 200 kVA and 10 kHz was developed. The simulation results show that the natural air-cooling method with heat sink fins on the upper and lower sides can limit the temperature rise of MFT to the allowable range for a 200 kVA, 10kHz MFT. While if a smaller volume is required, the forced air-cooling method with an air velocity of 1.6 m/s needs to be used. Finally, the rationality of the above design was verified by the temperature rise test of the MFT prototype.

articleTitle: Multi-objective Day-ahead Optimal Scheduling of Wind-solar-storage Microgrids Considering V2G and P2G Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Aiming at the energy crisis and environmental pollution problems, this paper proposes a multi-objective day-ahead optimal scheduling model for wind-solar-storage microgrids integrating V2G and P2G technologies. The model aims to achieve both economic and environmental objectives of the microgrid by integrating the modelling of devices such as wind, photovoltaic, micro gas turbine, P2G devices and PV loads. An improved multi-objective grey wolf algorithm is used in the study, and the results of the arithmetic analysis demonstrate the effectiveness of the scheduling strategy in both the economic and environmental optimal cases.

articleTitle: Access Control Model of Decentralized Power System Based on zk-SNARKs
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: This paper presents an innovative access control model for decentralized power systems by integrating zero-knowledge succinct non-interactive arguments of knowledge (zk-SNARKs). The proposed model addresses the growing need for secure, privacy-preserving management of access rights within distributed energy infrastructures. By leveraging zk-SNARKs, the system ensures that authorization can be validated without disclosing sensitive information, thereby enhancing both security and operational transparency. The model is rigorously analyzed through a combination of theoretical proofs and simulation experiments, demonstrating its effectiveness in mitigating unauthorized access and reducing computational overhead. Our findings indicate that the zk-SNARK-based approach not only fortifies the security framework of decentralized power systems but also facilitates scalable and efficient access management. This work provides a critical step towards the realization of robust, privacy-aware energy networks in the era of smart grids and distributed generation.

articleTitle: Towards Green Airports: Integrated Energy System Optimization and Renewable Energy Utilization
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Airport integrated energy systems typically encompass electricity, thermal energy, cooling energy, and other auxiliary energy forms. These systems extensively adopt renewable energy generation, distributed energy resources, and energy storage technologies to enhance energy efficiency and reliability. This study focuses on the multi-energy coupling and complementary characteristics of airport integrated energy systems, developing an optimization model that balances economic benefits, environmental friendliness, and energy security. Key aspects such as the share of renewable energy, energy storage configurations, and demand-side responses are analyzed to evaluate their impact on system performance and operational costs. By employing multi-objective optimization algorithms and simulation methods, the study optimizes the structure, operational strategies, and critical parameters of airport integrated energy systems, providing optimal energy scheduling solutions across different time periods and operating conditions.

articleTitle: Efficient Distributed PV Power Prediction via Blockchain-Driven Personalized Federated Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Accurate prediction of distributed photovoltaic (PV) power generation is crucial for efficient grid integration and energy management. Traditional centralized models often face challenges related to data privacy, heterogeneity, and transparency. This paper proposes an innovative framework that integrates blockchain technology with personalized federated learning (PFL) to address these issues in PV power prediction. In our approach, each participating node trains a local model on its dataset, preserving data privacy. Model updates are then securely aggregated using blockchain, ensuring transparency and immutability. This decentralized methodology accommodates the unique characteristics of each node's data, leading to improved predictin accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework outperforms traditional centralized and non-personalized federated learning models. The integration of blockchain enhances data security and fosters trust among stakeholders. These findings underscore the potential of combining blockchain-driven personalized federated learning to advance distributed PV power prediction systems.

articleTitle: China-U.S. Relations and Cybersecurity: A Study of Bilateral Cyberattack Patterns Based on Big Data Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: This paper explores the dynamics of China-U.S. relations in cyberspace, with a focus on the competition and cooperation between the two countries in the era of big data. As two major cyber powers, China and the United States engage in a complex interaction within cyberspace, influencing global cybersecurity, geopolitics, and economic trends. The study utilizes big data analysis to examine the characteristics and trends of cyberattacks, specifically focusing on the bilateral cyberattack patterns between China and the U.S. The research analyzes data from 2017 to 2024, including policy scores, policy effectiveness, and cybercrime rates, to predict the occurrence and severity of future cyberattacks. The findings emphasize the critical role of cybersecurity policy in shaping cyberattack trends and provide a deeper understanding of how policy changes affect cyber threat landscapes. Furthermore, the paper discusses the importance of China-U.S. cooperation in cyberspace, particularly in the context of big data technologies, to enhance mutual understanding and global cybersecurity governance. By utilizing big data and predictive models, the study provides valuable insights into the strategies that both nations can employ to mitigate cyber risks and promote a secure digital future.

articleTitle: Optimization of Coordinated Operation of Multi-Microgrid System Based on Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Method
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: With the advancement of renewable energy and distributed power generation technology, microgrids, as a platform for efficient resource integration and management, play a key role in improving energy efficiency, reducing transmission losses and supporting grid stability. Microgrids can not only optimize energy utilization, reduce transmission losses, and improve energy efficiency at the local level, but also support stable operation and reliable power supply through interactions with other power grids.
