This interaction involves multiple levels such as two-way flow of energy, information exchange, and operational coordination, and has an important impact on enhancing the resilience and disaster prevention capabilities of the power grid. Therefore, studying the optimal operation control of microgrids and the interaction mechanism of microgrids is extremely important to formulate strategies to promote the sustainable development of energy systems. This article discusses the application of SAC algorithm in multi-microgrid systems and highlights its advantages in system performance optimization. Through a series of experiments and analysis, the effectiveness of the SAC algorithm in improving energy utilization efficiency, reducing operating costs, and enhancing system power supply reliability was verified. Especially in dealing with renewable energy supply volatility and load demand uncertainty, the SAC method shows excellent adaptability and flexibility.

articleTitle: Dynamic Modeling of pH in a Dual-Tower Desulfurization System Based on an Improved Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: The dual-tower desulfurization system exhibits characteristics of significant delay and hysteresis in slurry concentration and pH value, which leads to certain deficiencies in the identification of slurry pH value. This paper analyzes the structure of a dual-tower desulfurization system in a power plant, taking the operational data under 590MW condition as an example, to conduct data analysis on factors affecting the slurry pH value. A closed-loop identification method is employed, utilizing an improved particle swarm optimization algorithm for parameter optimization, to establish the transfer functions of inlet SO2 concentration, inlet flue gas flow, slurry supply volume, and slurry pH value. Simulation analysis is carried out through MATLAB, and the results show that the identification error of the front tower is controlled within 2.5%, while the identification accuracy of the rear tower is relatively higher, controlled below 0.4%. The identification function can closely follow the changes in the actual curve, proving the reliability of the identification model.

articleTitle: Knowledge-Based False Information Detection Model
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: In response to the problem of insufficient attention given by traditional detection methods to text structure, this article proposes four text relation graphs: sentence-entity graphs, syntax dependency-based graphs, semantic dependency-based graphs, and graphs that combine syntax and semantic dependency. Furthermore, the constructed text relation graphs are analyzed for their features, and it is found that the graph density of real texts is relatively high, indicating that the text structure in real texts is denser, and the number of entities and relationships is also richer. The analysis suggests a close correlation between text structure and false information, and considering text structure relations can help improve the accuracy of false information detection. To effectively aggregate the semantic features of text with multiple relations, this article proposes a graph neural network false information detection model based on multiple relation semantic aggregation. From the perspective of spatial topology and sequence relationships, GCN-LSTM and GAT-LSTM and other models with multiple relation semantic aggregation are constructed. Experiments compare different networks and topologies, different models, model fusion analysis, and the results of each experiment are compared. Finally, the experimental results show that the GAT-LSTM training model with a syntax-semantic relation graph as the text feature input performs best, with an accuracy rate of 80.060%, recall rate of 81.843%, and F1 value of 82.520%.

articleTitle: The Comprehensive Evaluation Method for Residential Integrated Energy Systems Considering Thermal Comfort, Combining Both Subjective and Objective Approaches
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Integrated energy systems (IES) can enhance the economy, environmental friendliness, and reliability of energy systems through the coordinated integration of multiple energy sources. Considering the comprehensive evaluation of multiple indicators in IES is of great significance for its implementation and application in practice. This paper proposes a combined subjective and objective comprehensive evaluation method that incorporates thermal comfort as a key indicator. By constructing an evaluation index system that includes economic efficiency, energy consumption, environmental protection, comfort, and reliability, the proposed method integrates Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) with an improved entropy weight method for weight assignment. This approach ranks and analyzes various operation schemes of household integrated energy systems, providing users with meaningful guidance for selecting suitable application schemes tailored to their needs.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation of Cooling Plates with Different Channel Structures
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Current research on the performance of liquid cooling plates has predominantly emphasized the simulation method for a single flow channel structure. Consequently, systematic analysis of different flow channel structures based on experimental data remains limited. This study investigated the cooling characteristics of plates with six different channel structures, providing some experimental data references for related applications and studies. By comparing the consistency between the simulation results and the experimental data, the comparative experiment verified the reliability of the experimental process. Then, range analysis was used in the orthogonal test to reveal the variation patterns of three general performance metrics: maximum temperature of the heat source, temperature difference, and pressure drop under the combined influence of the cooling plate channel structure, thermal load, and flow rate. Furthermore, a comprehensive cooling performance metric was constructed using the entropy weight method and the Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) to evaluate the integrated cooling performance of different channel structures. The results demonstrate significant differences in the cooling performance between channel structures, with the grid-type channel exhibiting the best performance. Furthermore, a faster flow rate reduces the duration and efficiency of heat transfer, recommending an optimal flow rate of approximately 6 L/min under similar thermal conditions.

articleTitle: Energy Management Technologies for Hypersonic Vehicles: Current Status, Challenges, and Future Exploration
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: With the rapid advancement of technology, hypersonic vehicle technology has gradually become a focal point of global research, demonstrating significant military and commercial application potential. Energy management technologies are crucial for ensuring reliable flight operations of hypersonic vehicles while meeting the high energy demands in extreme environments. This paper reviews the current research status of energy management technologies for hypersonic vehicles, focusing on key technologies such as the Brayton cycle, thermoelectric conversion and hybrid power generation systems. By analyzing the potential applications and limitations of these technologies in optimizing vehicle performance and adapting to extreme operating conditions, this study examines their advantages and challenges in improving energy utilization efficiency. Building on this foundation, the paper discusses potential future directions for energy management in hypersonic vehicles, aiming to guide further innovation and the practical applications of energy management technologies.

articleTitle: Real-Time Mechanical Intrusion and Avian Nest Detection in Transmission Corridors Using Enhanced YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: The reliable operation of power grids faces significant threats from both avian nests and mechanical intrusions within transmission corridors, impacting safety and stability. To address these challenges, this paper presents a real-time detection system for identifying both bird nests and mechanical intrusions like cranes and excavators on power transmission lines, leveraging an enhanced YOLOv8 model. First, the model's backbone is enhanced using the EFC2F module to improve feature extraction capabilities relevant to both types of disturbances. Second, a small-object detection head is added to increase the accuracy of detecting smaller avian nests and intrusion-related objects. Finally, an improved ECBAM attention module is incorporated before the detection head. This module separately strengthens location and category features, refining the model's ability to distinguish between targets and the surrounding environment. These improvements allow the model to maintain a stable inference speed while achieving enhanced accuracy in identifying bird nests and potential mechanical intrusions under diverse and challenging conditions. The model efficiently identifies target objects under normal conditions and performs well in challenging scenarios, including long-distance shooting, varying lighting, different angles, occlusions, and concealment. Experimental results demonstrate that the improved YOLOv8 model achieves significant improvements across multiple key metrics, validating the effectiveness of these enhancements for both avian nest and mechanical intrusion detection.

Author Keywords: Real-Time Mechanical Intrusion and Avian Nest Detection

articleTitle: Research on Lightning Overvoltage Simulation and Protection Measures of Low-Tolerance Facilities of New Power System
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: In order to implement the “double carbon” goal, China proposes to vigorously develop a new power system with new energy as the main body. Lightning disasters occur from time to time, so the technical requirements for lightning protection of new power systems are getting higher and higher. Compared with a single wind farm or photovoltaic power generation system, the wind-solar hybrid system has more lightning intrusion into key nodes, low tolerance facilities and a larger lightning receiving area. The ATP-EMTP was used to build a transient model of lightning strikes in a wind-solar hybrid system constructed by various subsystems, and the lightning overvoltage distribution of the wind-solar hybrid system was calculated, and the influence of lightning strike location, lightning protection configuration and overhead line length on the overvoltage level of the wind-solar hybrid system was analyzed. The results show that the installation of SPD on the DC side of the PV field inverter achieves the best lightning protection effect for the PV field combiner box, inverter and transformer. The installation of lightning arresters on the high-voltage side of the box transformer of the wind farm can effectively suppress the propagation of the lightning overvoltage at the outlet of the wind turbine to the box transformer; When adopting the single-circuit transmission inlet section, the lightning overvoltage attenuation speed of the photovoltaic farm into the substation bus section is slightly faster than that of the wind farm, and the lightning overvoltage level of the photovoltaic farm inlet section is higher than that of the wind farm inlet section as a whole; The overall lightning overvoltage amplitude of the double-return line section of the same tower is higher than that of the single-return overhead line section. Therefore, when the single-circuit transmission line is adopted, the insulation level of the incoming line of the photovoltaic farm can be appropriately improved, and the length of the bus connecting the wind farm into the substation can be appropriately extended compared with the photovoltaic farm. When the double-circuit transmission line of the same tower is used to integrate into the substation, compared with the single-circuit transmission line, the lightning protection performance of the transmission line can be appropriately improved to reduce the lightning overvoltage amplitude in the intrusion station.)

articleTitle: Research on Intelligent Management Architecture for Power Grid Data Catalog Based on Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: With the digital transformation of the power grid, the scale and complexity of power grid data have significantly increased, encompassing various types such as SCADA systems, GIS data, and dispatch operation logs. This necessitates efficient and intelligent management methods. This paper proposes an intelligent classification method for power grid data catalogs based on the Transformer model. Specifically, the T5 model is employed to convert the classification task into a text generation task, while table embedding techniques are integrated to enhance data representation. To address the issue of class imbalance, Focal Loss is introduced to optimize classification performance, and soft prompt learning is incorporated to improve the training effectiveness for small sample data. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms traditional approaches in power grid data classification, achieving higher classification accuracy and better generalization capability. Furthermore, intelligent retrieval and knowledge graph construction enable efficient data management and intelligent querying. This research provides a novel technological approach to power grid data management, contributing to the enhancement of intelligent power grid operations.

articleTitle: Decision-Making and Market Service Optimization for Agency-Based Electricity Procurement User
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: With the ongoing advancement of electricity market reforms, unqualified electricity users and small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) encounter substantial barriers to direct participation in market transactions. The demand of these users is typically fulfilled through agency-based electricity procurement or intermediary services. Power supply companies face various challenges in balancing market fairness, economic efficiency, service innovation, and risk management. This paper examines the key decision points encountered by power supply companies in addressing unqualified and SME users, integrating policy requirements with market realities. Additionally, it proposes recommendations for optimizing service models, with the aim of providing insights into building a fair and efficient electricity market.

articleTitle: Active Disturbance Rejection Control for the Pump-Controlled Reach Stacker of a New Energy Rubber-Tired Gantry Crane
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: This paper addresses the position control requirements of the lifting cylinder of a new energy straddle carrier and proposes a pump control system design scheme based on Active Disturbance Rejection Control (ADRC). The new energy straddle carrier uses a servo motor as the power source and achieves efficient cargo handling operations through precisely controlled pump-controlled hydraulic cylinders. The mathematical modeling of the lifting cylinder pump control system, including the modeling of the servo motor, fixed displacement pump, and hydraulic cylinder, is elaborated in this paper. Additionally, an ADRC controller designed using an RBF neural network for parameter optimization is introduced. Simulation results show that the proposed ADRC controller outperforms traditional PID controllers in terms of control accuracy and dynamic response performance across different target positions and loads. Specifically, it resolves issues related to increasing response speed with stroke length, enhancing system robustness and stability. Particularly, it resolves the issue of the response speed increasing with the stroke length, enhancing the robustness and stability of the system.

articleTitle: Research on the Scheduling Optimization Model of the Virtual Power Plants Participate in the Electricity Spot Market
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: With the construction of the new power system, the rapid development of new energy and the prominent contradictions in the short-term supply and demand balance of the power grid, virtual power plants can fully tap into decentralized resources to better achieve optimal resource allocation through market mechanisms, and realize energy conservation and efficiency enhancement. However, the current market mechanism is not perfect and cannot ensure effective participation in market scheduling operations to obtain reasonable returns. Considering the establishment of a unified national electricity market, this paper studies the resource scheduling model of virtual power plants in the context of the electricity spot market, including dispatchable units, new energy units, energy storage devices, and adjustable loads. It proposes an optimization control strategy for virtual power plants to participate in the spot market, adapting to the fluctuations in new energy output, utilizing dispatchable units, energy storage devices, and adjustable loads to smooth out the volatility of new energy unit output. Through case analysis, the effectiveness of the proposed model and control strategy is verified.

articleTitle: Optimisation of PV PEM Power for Hydrogen Production based on Multi-Strategy Cuckoo Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: To address the detrimental effects of recurring photovoltaic (PV) output fluctuations, which are influenced by environmental conditions, on the efficiency of electrolyzers and the hydrogen yield in a PV-PEM hydrogen production system, a model that incorporates actual fluctuation scenarios has been developed. Furthermore, an in-depth analysis of the relationship between the electrolyzer's electrolysis efficiency, its power input, and hydrogen production is conducted. A power optimization strategy for PV hydrogen production system based on the multi-strategy improved cuckoo algorithm is proposed. This approach successfully enhances the algorithm's responsiveness and tracking precision in dealing with operational disturbances of the PV hydrogen production system, achieved by augmenting population diversity, incorporating adaptive control elements, and employing a Gaussian perturbation tactic. Results from the simulation experiments indicate that the electrolysis efficiency is enhanced by 2.01%, 1.53%, and 5.11%, and the monthly hydrogen output of the system is increased by 24.42%, 9.56%, and 100.71% when compared to the strategies of CS, P&Q, and no-power optimization, respectively.

articleTitle: Multi-objective Planning of Thermal Power Plant Energy Systems Based on “Power + Ecology” Big Data and Carbon Emissions
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: To reduce the carbon emissions and operating costs of thermal power plants, a multi-objective planning method for the energy system of thermal power plants based on the big data of “power+ecology” and carbon emissions is proposed. Based on the big data of “power+ecology” of thermal power plants, this method calculates the carbon emissions of the energy system of thermal power plants and the carbon emissions increment under various influencing factors; According to the calculation results, a multi-objective programming model for the energy system of thermal power plants is constructed, and the upper and lower objective functions of the model and the corresponding constraints are set; The fast non dominated sorting genetic algorithm (SA-NSGA-II) based on the successive approximation method is used to solve the multi-objective planning model of the energy system of thermal power plants and obtain the multi-objective planning results. The test results show that the algorithm has good solution performance, the distance results of the inversion generation are all below 0.022, the spacing index results are all below 0.019, and the index diversity results are all above 0.942; The carbon emission increment results of the system can be determined based on the big data of power+ecology; The maximum operation cost after the planning is 1.68X 107 yuan, and the maximum carbon emission is 4.36X107 kg. The external power transmission rate is lower than 12.28%, which is significantly lower than the results before planning.

articleTitle: Voltage Sag Localization Method Based on Message Passing Graph Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Voltage sags have become the most severe power quality issue, attracting significant attention from power grids and users. To address the existing voltage sag localization methods, which struggle to cope with network topology changes, have low data utilization rates, and exhibit low localization accuracy, this paper proposes a voltage sag localization method based on Message Passing Graph Neural Networks (MP-GNNs). Initially, the method analyzes the factors influencing the characteristics of voltage sag source localization based on the propagation characteristics of voltage sags, and constructs a voltage sag localization feature graph that includes data such as network topology. A Message Passing Graph Neural Network is built to perform feature extraction and updates on the power grid busbars and branches, while utilizing the Differential Evolution algorithm to optimize the hyperparameter combinations of the network model. This approach avoids falling into local optimal solutions from manual selection of hyperparameters, thereby achieving accurate localization of voltage sag sources.

articleTitle: Research on the Optimal Wiring Method of Distribution Network Lines Adapting to Multi-Level Dynamic Networking of Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: With the deepening of power system reform, most existing distribution network planning methods struggle to adapt to the increasingly large network scale and complex wiring patterns under the current multi-microgrid and multi-level grid system. At the same time, with the progress of the times, people's requirements for distribution networks are also increasing. Therefore, issues such as the fragile structure of the distribution network and the convoluted and intersecting power supply lines are becoming increasingly prominent, posing risks to social and economic development and affecting the construction and operation maintenance of distribution networks. This paper studies the optimal selection of wiring methods for distribution networks that adapt to dynamic networking of multi-level microgrids. It analyzes the impact of different networking scenarios on distribution networks, focusing on the wiring methods and line capacities of distribution networks, and proposes relevant optimization methods. The aim is to address the existing problems in current distribution network planning and to propose a planning index system for distribution networks that adapts to flexible networking of hybrid energy microgrids. This paper will provide reference for the planning and construction of microgrids for the GS power grid.

articleTitle: Multi-Resource and Multi-Objective Peak Shaving Optimization Dispatch of Large Power Grids Considering Efficient Utilization of Multiple Energy Storage and Demand Response
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: With the increasing proportion of clean energy in power systems, the curtailment of wind and solar power has intensified during periods of high clean energy generation. Meanwhile, the high penetration of clean energy installed capacity has further compressed the operating capacity of traditional power generation units, weakening the grid's peak shaving and supply security regulation capabilities. Energy storage, as a key means of smoothing the fluctuations of renewable energy and alleviating supply-demand contradictions, is crucial for ensuring the safe, stable, and flexible operation of the power grid. Demand-side response, as a means of optimizing the load curve, can also reduce the impact of the counter-peak characteristics and intermittency of wind and solar power on grid optimization scheduling. This paper addresses the challenges of ensuring power supply and peak shaving in power systems with a high proportion of clean energy penetration, as well as the difficulties in new energy consumption. It proposes a multi-resource, multi-objective peak shaving optimization scheduling method for large power grids that considers the efficient utilization of multiple energy storage systems and demand-side response. First, taking the new type of power system with a high proportion of clean energy as the research object, this paper sorts out three key needs: grid flexible peak shaving, efficient clean energy consumption, and the guarantee of system operation economy. Based on these, an evaluation index system for the joint optimization scheduling of multiple resources in large power grids is constructed. Second, according to the proposed evaluation index system, fully considering the efficient utilization of multiple energy storage systems and demand-side response, a multi-resource, multi-objective, two-level peak shaving optimization scheduling model for large power grids is established. In this model, the upper-level model aims to minimize the fluctuation of net load to complete the startup combination plan of conventional units, while the lower-level model aims to minimize the curtailed clean energy and system operation costs to complete the optimization of the output curves of multiple resources, providing a reference for power grid generation plan formulation. Finally, based on the actual operation case of a provincial power grid in Southwest China, the effectiveness and advanced nature of the proposed modeling method are verified. The results show that compared with not configuring multiple energy storage or demand-side response resources, using multiple energy storage or demand-side response alone can improve grid peak shaving, clean energy consumption, and system operation economy to a certain extent. Furthermore, by jointly optimizing demand-side response resources and multiple energy storage resources, the utilization of multiple energy storage can be effectively improved, and the degree of improvement in the three key needs proposed is significantly greater than that of using multiple energy storage or demand-side response alone.

articleTitle: Simulation of Solar Phase Change Thermal Storage Distributed Energy System Based on Offshore Oil Platform
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: This study explores the design of a distributed energy system integrated with solar phase change thermal storage. Using MATLAB and Simulink, a mathematical model of the system was developed. Load demand was simulated using DeST software for a North Sea Oil Platform. A convolutional neural network (CNN) was employed for load forecasting, leveraging its effectiveness in analyzing time series data patterns. Suitable unit equipment was selected based on load simulations, and operations were conducted to evaluate load outputs and energy consumption changes across different seasons. The CNN demonstrated success in predicting cooling, heating, and power loads, aiding the platform in anticipating load fluctuations. Additionally, the solar phase change thermal storage system stores thermal energy during transitional seasons and poor weather, providing backup energy output. It also alleviates winter heat load pressure on the distributed energy system. Optimization strategies, including energy utilization rate evaluation and genetic algorithm applications, were employed to enhance system efficiency and maintain stable operation. The results improved energy management during typical daily operations across all seasons.

articleTitle: A Review of Health State Estimation Algorithms for Retired Lithium-ion Batteries
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: The state of health (SOH) of lithium-ion batteries serves as a crucial indicator of battery performance and reliability, making accurate estimation of SOH essential for enhancing battery longevity. Consequently, this paper categorizes and compares existing SOH estimation methods within the framework of Battery Management Systems (BMS). For instance, the Coulomb counting method is straightforward and intuitive; however, it is disadvantaged by prolonged measurement durations and significant errors. The open-circuit voltage method is uncomplicated and user-friendly, yet it necessitates extended settling times and has a restricted number of evaluation dimensions. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy offers high accuracy but depends on precise modeling and parameters. The Kalman filter method is precise and exhibits a minor error; however, it necessitates a substantial quantity of data for training and validation. This paper analyzes the advantages and disadvantages of various State of Health (SOH) estimation methods, discusses critical points within the technical field, and offers guidance and recommendations for future research and practical applications of SOH estimation methods.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Method for Rapid Prediction of Cascading Failures in Renewable-Integrated Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: With the continuous development of renewable-integrated power systems, the probability of cascading failures in the power grid has significantly increased. Traditional cascading failure prediction methods struggle to handle the complexity and operating conditions of the new power grid in terms of timeliness and accuracy. Therefore, this paper proposes a Random Forest and SHAP analysis model based on real-time measurement data from the Wide Area Measurement System (WAMS). The model uses the operational state information of the power grid from cascading failure samples to quickly predict the system's cascading failure risk, demonstrating good prediction accuracy, speed, and generalization ability. Additionally, the SHAP analysis method is used to explain the prediction results, identifying which features are most important and how they influence the model's prediction performance. Test results on the IEEE 39-bus system case show that, for a sample set of 14,000, the Random Forest model achieves a prediction accuracy exceeding 90%, with a prediction time of only 0.12 seconds for the validation set. Moreover, the SHAP analysis provides a good explanation for the prediction results.

articleTitle: A Data-Driven Approach for Regional PV Power Plant Cluster Output Prediction and Uncertainty Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: To improve the accuracy of Photovoltaic (PV) power generation forecasting and ensure the safe scheduling and stable operation of power systems, we propose a combined forecasting method based on Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) and the Rime Optimization Algorithm (RIME) to optimize an attention mechanism-based Convolutional Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory Neural Network (CNN-BiLSTM-AT). Addressing the issues of nonlinearity and non-stationarity in the time series signals affecting PV power generation, we select inclined irradiance, horizontal irradiance, temperature, and humidity as feature input variables. The VMD algorithm is employed to decompose these variables into several distinct modes, with each component modeled separately. Furthermore, the RIME optimization algorithm is utilized to optimize the hyperparameters of the CNN-BiLSTM-AT algorithm, effectively resolving uncertainties in parameter selection and slow convergence rates. Finally, we conduct a case analysis using measured data from distributed PV sites in Australia. The results demonstrate that compared to traditional neural network forecasting models and fixed-parameter combined forecasting models, the VMD-RIME-CNN-BiLSTM-AT model improves the prediction errors for 72 hours, 24 hours, and 4 hours by at least 0.83%, 1.11<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, and 1.41%, respectively. This method exhibits higher predictive accuracy and stability.

articleTitle: Research on Short and Long-Term Prediction of New Energy Generation Power Based on VAE-GAN
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: New energy generation power is affected by multiple factors such as meteorological conditions, equipment status and grid dispatching demand, and its output shows strong volatility, intermittency and randomness, which brings great challenges to grid dispatching. In this paper, a new short and long-term prediction method combining Variational Autoencoder (V AE) and Generative Adversarial Nets (GAN) is proposed to solve the shortcomings of traditional models in accuracy and generalization ability. Firstly, key features highly related to power generation are extracted from multi-dimensional meteorological and load data through mutual information (MI) to ensure the stability of model input. Secondly, VAE is used to perform latent distribution learning and feature coding on historical data, and the future power sequence is generated by combining the adversarial training mechanism of GAN generator and discriminator, so as to continuously optimize the authenticity and accuracy of prediction results. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified in short and long-term prediction tasks. Compared with BiLSTM, LightGBM, Informer and other mainstream models, the Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAP E) of short-term prediction is reduced to 2.46%, and the coefficient of determination is increased to 0.977. The MAPE of long-term prediction is 3.37%, and the coefficient of determination is 0.961. The results show that the proposed method not only significantly improves the prediction accuracy and stability, but also has good generalization ability, which can provide reliable support for the scheduling optimization and planning decision-making of new energy generation power, and provides an innovative method exploration for new energy generation power prediction.

articleTitle: Integrated AGC Error Operation and Abnormal Instruction Online Identification
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: With the continuous advancement of power grid automation, current online identification of Automatic Generation Control (AGC) Error Operations and Abnormal Instructions presents several deficiencies, including inadequate coverage of identification methods, incomplete feature extraction, and insufficient in-depth analysis of online identification results. This paper establishes an integrated AGC online identification system to address these issues. First, rational/abnormal feature extraction is performed through multi-source information correlation analysis, employing logical language representation and knowledge graph representation. Second, the Significance of Data analysis method is utilized to determine the criticality levels of AGC input/output information. Finally, for various abnormal scenarios, the system integrates expert scoring, statistical analysis, and complex network methods to determine online identification probability and alert classification, ultimately generating operational outputs. Case analysis validate the system's effectiveness in simultaneously handling Error Operations and Abnormal Instructions. The proposed integrated online identification system for AGC Error Operations and Abnormal Instructions effectively mitigates existing deficiencies, significantly enhancing the reliability and operational stability of AGC systems.

articleTitle: Optimized Defogging Algorithm for Dark Channel Based on Multi-Scale Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: To address the issue of significant discrepancies between the estimated transmission in traditional single-image dehazing algorithms and the actual scenario, a multi-scale convolutional neural network-based dehazing algorithm optimized by dark channel prior is proposed. The algorithm utilizes guided filtering, which preserves edge smoothness, to filter the feature transmission map extracted by the convolutional neural network, making the processed transmission closer to the actual transmission of the input hazy image. Subsequently, the dark channel prior theory is employed to obtain the global atmospheric light value of the hazy image, and finally, The atmospheric scattering model serves as a crucial tool when engaging in the operation of image dehazing, effectively enhancing the clarity of images affected by haze. The outcomes of the experiments indicate that this algorithm surpasses the latest approaches in both qualitative and quantitative evaluations. The algorithm put forward shows remarkable enhancements in peak signal - to - noise ratio and structural similarity, leading to significantlyenhanced dehazing performance.

articleTitle: Gearbox Fault Diagnosis Method Based on Weighted Adversarial Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: This paper proposes a gearbox fault diagnosis method based on weighted adversarial transfer learning. This method reduces the difference in data distribution under different working conditions through adversarial training, and introduces a weighted strategy to improve the alignment ability of key features. Experimental results show that this method can effectively improve the fault diagnosis accuracy under cross-working conditions and has strong robustness.

articleTitle: Fault Identification Method Based on BP Neural Network in Accelerator Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Accelerator as a large scale of electrical facilities is trending towards high energy, high intensity and high reliability in the future. Next generation of accelerator will require unprecedented stability of distribution networks. Traditional monitoring methods have some limitations when detecting and analyzing subtle and complex power quality problems. A big data platform built for HIRFL(The Heavy Ion Research Facility in Lanzhou) distribution network integrates various big data technologies and combines historical data with online operational data of the distribution network. Based on this platform, this paper constructs, trains and deploys BP neural network models to identify faults in the distribution network. The results demonstrate that the models have outstanding capabilities of learning and generalization accompanied by accurate identification and classification of faults. This method is significant for the informatization and intelligence of future accelerator distribution networks.

articleTitle: Data Privacy Protection Algorithm for Carrier Communication Nodes in Power Internet of Things Based on Frequent Itemsets
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Because the original data of the carrier communication node of power Internet of Things is non-stationary and nonlinear, its discreteness is large, which is not conducive to feature extraction, which leads to the possibility of data privacy protection and low data security. Therefore, this paper proposes a data privacy protection algorithm based on frequent itemsets for power Internet of Things carrier communication nodes. Through the set rules, the network resources of the power Internet of Things are analyzed, the corresponding itemsets are connected, the residual components are calculated, and the correlation between two adjacent data is extracted by using frequent itemsets. The comprehensive attributes of the data set are obtained, the local information entropy of the communication node data privacy is described, and the data sequence characteristics of the privacy data are extracted, to construct the data privacy protection objective function and realize the data privacy protection algorithm design of the power Internet of Things carrier communication node. The experimental results show that the algorithm in this paper shows a low data information loss rate on multiple data sets, which can effectively reduce data information loss and protect the privacy and security of data. Under both internal and external attacks, the anti-attack performance is over 98%, after privacy processing by this algorithm, privacy leakage can be limited to the maximum extent, and privacy protection performance is excellent.

articleTitle: Research and Implementation of Intelligent Monitoring System for Power Transmission Line Faults
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Power transmission lines, though widely distributed, remain vulnerable to various hazards. While visual monitoring technologies have significantly reduced manual inspection workloads, conventional monitoring devices still exhibit limitations under nocturnal conditions, particularly regarding in detail preservation. These constraints necessitate further improvements to ensure the secure and stable operation of power systems. This paper presents a Transformer-based and HVI-GLARE Fusion Low-Light Image Enhancement network (THG-LLIE) that integrates HVI color space characteristics with generative latent feature retrieval methodology. Comparative experimental analysis demonstrates that our proposed algorithm achieves superior image enhancement results across both quantitative and qualitative metrics relative to state-of-the-art enhancement approaches. Additionally, we have developed a domestically produced AI chip based on our proprietary architecture, enabling implementation of an intelligent AI-based detection system for power transmission line fault monitoring.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Substation Monitoring System Based on HarmonyOS and Broadband-Narrowband Wireless Communication Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: This research focuses on the design and implementation of a substation monitoring system based on HarmonyOS and broadband-narrowband wireless communication technology, aiming to address the issues of poor communication reliability, insufficient compatibility and scalability, and limited data processing and analysis capabilities inherent in traditional substation monitoring systems. The study provides a detailed analysis of the HarmonyOS architecture and its potential applications in the power sector, as well as the principles and characteristics of broadband-narrowband wireless communication technology. Through comprehensive requirements analysis, a hierarchical system architecture was constructed, encompassing key aspects such as HarmonyOS adaptation, broadband-narrowband wireless communication network deployment, and data processing and storage. During the system implementation phase, hardware device selection and installation, software system deployment, and integration debugging were completed, and the system's effectiveness was validated through functional, performance, and stability testing. Practical case studies demonstrate that the system significantly improves the accuracy and real-time capabilities of monitoring data, enhances fault warning and processing efficiency, and reduces operational and maintenance costs. The research findings provide a new pathway for the development of substation monitoring technology and also point out directions for further optimization and expansion in the future.

articleTitle: Design and Verification of a Highly Reliable Integrated Sensing and Transmission Monitoring Module for Substations Using Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: To address the reliability challenges of equipment condition monitoring in the complex electromagnetic environment of smart substations, this paper designs an integrated sensing and transmission monitoring module based on heterogeneous wireless communication. This solution breaks through the limitations of traditional wired monitoring systems by integrating multimodal sensors for temperature, vibration, and partial discharge, and achieves dynamic data compensation through an improved Kalman filter. A heterogeneous wireless architecture combining ZigBee and LoRa is constructed, where ZigBee adopts a hybrid topology for networking, and LoRa ensures long-distance transmission using spread spectrum modulation. A smart communication protocol stack is developed, integrating adaptive frequency hopping, forward error correction, and multipath redundancy mechanisms, reducing the bit error rate to the order of 10–<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> at a 15dB signal-to-noise ratio. Tested in a 110kV simulated substation, the module achieves a data transmission success rate of 99.6% within a 1200m communication radius, with an average latency of less than 42ms, reducing energy consumption by 37% compared to single-mode communication and improving resistance to sudden interference by five times. The system has been certified according to the DL/T 860 standard, providing a reliable solution for unmanned operation and maintenance of smart substations. Keywords-Smart Substation; Heterogeneous Wireless Communication; Integrated Sensing and Transmission; Reliability; Adaptive Frequency Hopping; Multimodal Sensors.

articleTitle: Analysis of Carbon Emission Reduction Potential of Electric Vehicles and Application of Carbon Inclusion
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: With the elevation of “carbon peaking” and “carbon neutrality” to the level of national strategic priorities, electric vehicles have garnered widespread attention due to their carbon reduction advantages. This paper uses carbon credits as the carrier of the carbon inclusion mechanism and establishes a method for forming carbon credits specifically for electric vehicle charging. Considering the need for aggregated trading, a two-tier trading model involving carbon aggregators and emission-controlled enterprises in a regional carbon inclusion market is designed and solved. The upper tier involves the economic models of the trading entities—carbon aggregators and emission-controlled enterprises—forming the supply-demand relationship between the two parties. The lower tier involves a regional carbon trading price decision model based on the supply-demand ratio. The results indicate that the proposed trading scheme, which integrates fragmented carbon inclusion resources and enables participation in regional carbon markets through electric vehicle charging, effectively expands the application scenarios and value of carbon inclusion. In the future, with technological advancements and policy support, the carbon inclusion mechanism is expected to play a more significant role in promoting electric vehicle adoption and achieving carbon reduction in the transportation sector, contributing to the realization of the “3060” goal.

articleTitle: Synergistic Mechanism Design and Market Modelling of Demand Response Center, Trading Center and Dispatching Center for New Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: The continuation of the traditional trading center and dispatch center power market operation under the new power system may be difficult to adapt to the regulatory needs of multiple types of flexibility resources participating in the market. This study combines the development of China's electric power market with the actual power operation and management departments, considers the regulation characteristics of large amount of flexibility resources, and innovatively proposes a “three-center” collaborative operation mechanism of demand response center-trading center-dispatch center, which provides a more convenient management platform for market-based demand response under the vigorous development of new energy.

articleTitle: The Operation Control Strategy of The Distribution Stations with On-Load Capacity and Voltage Regulating Transformers
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: With the access of high proportion distributed photovoltaic and random load, the problems of unbalanced three-phase load, voltage limit, distribution transformer, and line loss are becoming increasingly prominent in the distribution stations, which will seriously affect the reliability and economical operation of the distribution stations. Existing studies rarely introduce O-LCVRT to participate in the research on operation control of distribution stations. This paper proposes the operation control method of distribution stations with O-LCVRT. Given the problems of voltage over limit and power saving and loss reduction of distribution transformers, the operation control model of distribution station containing O-LCVRT is established, the control strategy and application effect of on-load capacity and voltage regulating transformer in photovoltaic - energy storage platform area is explored. The operation constraints of O-LCVRT, as well as other major equipment and components, are set. Aiming at many typical application scenarios, the objective function of minimum total operating cost, including loss cost of O-LCVRT, is established to solve the optimal operation control strategy of the model. Finally, the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed model are verified through the analysis of practical examples and simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Electricity-Carbon Synergy Modeling for Thermal Power Plants Based on Electricity High Frequency Data
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: A power-carbon synergy model for thermal plants, using high-freq power data, aims to cut emissions and promote sustainable energy. It predicts load via CEEMD, GRNN, and cubic spline interpolation. Analyzing electricity-carbon joint ops, it builds an optimization model. Using NSGA-III with clustering to improve reference points, it finds a compromise solution. Tests show accurate load prediction and effective optimization, boosting user satisfaction >92.44% and reducing carbon intensity & yield fluctuation.

articleTitle: Secondary System Failure Risk Assessment Based on Copula Function
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: The improvement of substation intelligence brings more uncertainties to the secondary system reliability analysis. The traditional secondary system reliability analysis method usually starts from the independent equipment in the system, lacking the analysis of equipment correlation and system integrity, and cannot accurately match the requirements of the secondary system failure risk assessment of intelligent substations. In this regard, a secondary system failure risk assessment method based on Copula function is proposed. The reliability model of the equipment is established through the exponential distribution to characterize the life distribution of individual equipment in the secondary system. The Copula function is used to analyze the correlation of different devices in the same power supply circuit of the secondary system and to establish a system reliability analysis model considering the mutual influence of different devices in the same power supply area. For the power supply module, main board and communication port module in the secondary system, a fault chain is established and combined with the reliability model of a single power supply area to derive the reliability model of the whole secondary system. The effectiveness of the secondary system failure risk assessment method proposed in this study is verified by simulation, and it is proved that increasing the number of power supply loops can effectively reduce the secondary system failure risk under the condition of increasing the length of fault chains due to the improvement of substation intelligence.

articleTitle: An Auxiliary Method of Relay Protection Setting for Transmission Lines Based on LLaMa2-7B
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: The precise operation of relay protection devices for transmission lines is contingent upon the accuracy of setting values. The current approach to the operation and maintenance of relay protection setting values lacks sufficient intelligence, predominantly depending on specialized soft-ware. In response to these challenges, this study introduces an auxiliary method for relay protection setting based on LLaMa2-7B. The proposed model not only provides setting values for relay protection but also offers recommendations based on transmission line data. Initially, a dataset comprising 252 relay protection setting lists for 110kV-220kV transmission lines from a regional grid was assembled and preprocessed. Subsequently, the LLaMa2-7B model was modified and fine-tuned for training, enabling it to focus on the task related to protection setting values prediction while maintaining general language generation capabilities. Cross-validation and task separation techniques are employed to enhance predictive accuracy. Finally, case results indicate that the model's root mean square error in predicting setting values, with line parameters and control words as input, is as low as 0.45%, which is a 12.83% reduction compared to the direct fine-tuning method using the dataset. This proposed method facilitates the precise prediction of relay protection set-ting values, thereby aiding in the validation and calibration process.

articleTitle: Aggregation Modelling of Grid-Forming Renewable Power Plant for Real-Time Simulation of Power Grid
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Renewable power plant based on the grid-forming converter has the function of actively supporting the grid frequency and voltage, and in order to correctly assess the impact of large-scale grid-forming renewable power integration on the security and stability characteristics of the grid, it is necessary to accurately model and simulate the grid-forming renewable power plant based on the research. In this paper, we propose a two-machine aggregation modeling method for grid-forming renewable power plant that multiplies the control signals of the primary circuit of the inverters, which solves the problem that the single-machine multiplication method may lead to a large oscillation of the output current due to the large multiplication coefficients in the real-time simulation environment. Based on the simulation modeling analysis of real grid cases, the proposed aggregation modeling method can accurately reflect the dynamic process of grid-forming renewable power plant interacting with the grid, and significantly improve the simulation rate.

articleTitle: Electricity Spot Market Trading Mechanism Considering Renewable Energy Curtailment and Peak Shaving Compensation
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: To address the conflict between renewable energy participation in market competition and guaranteed integration, a trading mechanism tailored for high-penetration renewable energy systems in the electricity spot market is introduced. First, considering the market-oriented integration of renewable energy, the clearing mechanism of the electricity spot market is refined. In a trading environment where renewable energy and thermal power units jointly participate in market bidding, a generation substitution model is established, activated in response to wind and solar energy curtailment, to fully utilize the peak shaving capability of thermal power units. Second, a corresponding settlement mechanism is proposed, where thermal power units are compensated for peak shaving, with costs covered by renewable energy units benefiting from enhanced integration opportunities. Finally, simulation results demonstrate that this mechanism ensures an optimal match between supply and demand for peak shaving resources in the electricity spot market, promotes the effective integration of renewable energy, and reasonably compensates thermal power units for peak shaving costs. This not only encourages thermal power units to undertake flexibility retrofits but also fosters fair competition and equitable proceeds allocation among market participants.

articleTitle: Voltage Equalization Strategy for the Input Stage of MMC-Type Power Electronic Transformers Based on Dynamic Average of Capacitor Voltage
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Traditional voltage-balancing strategies for modular multilevel converter (MMC)-based power-electronic transformers often encounter significant challenges, including high computational complexity in sorting algorithms, elevated submodule switching frequencies, and frequent power device operations. To mitigate these issues, this paper proposes an advanced voltage-balancing strategy for the input stage of MMC-based power-electronic transformers, utilizing the dynamic average value of submodule capacitor voltages. The proposed approach integrates the average voltage variation per cycle as a constraint within an optimized bubble sorting algorithm, thereby minimizing unnecessary switching state transitions. Furthermore, a predefined maximum voltage deviation threshold is introduced to ensure that the capacitor voltage uniformity complies with stringent engineering requirements. The efficacy of the proposed strategy is rigorously validated through a comprehensive Matlab / Simulink simulation model of an MMC-based power-electronic transformer. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a 21% reduction in switching frequency while maintaining capacitor voltage deviations within 5%, significantly enhancing system efficiency and operational reliability compared to conventional approaches.

articleTitle: Research on Operational Optimization Decision-Making Methods for New Energy Alliances Based on Multi-Scale Balanced Cost Allocation
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: In order to realize load trimming and valley filling and balance load peak and valley power difference in real time, this paper combines the different power generation characteristics of new energy and traditional energy, proposes a multi-energy power supply method based on the collaborative optimization of wind power, photovoltaic power, hydropower and thermal power. The peak and valley energy blocks are used to determine the power undertaken by the consortium, and the Shapley value of the multi-scale dynamic cost optimization decision-making method is designed with a focus on the optimal allocation of internal resources within the alliance and the multi-agent power generation combination's multi-scale cost balance optimization. At the same time, the optimal power generation combination is selected based on the TOPSIS comprehensive evaluation model of grey relational degree and entropy weight to further improve the optimization. Case analysis shows that the operational mechanism of the multi-energy alliance can effectively mitigate the fluctuations in new energy output, substantially boost the share of new energy generation within the alliance, and enhance the overall economic performance of the alliance. This method provides a theoretical basis for the power generation planning, and combination optimization of cost control and power generation in decision of each entity in the alliance. It has important practical significance for the coordinated and efficient operation of multi-energy system.

articleTitle: Calculation of the Virtual Power Plant Baseline Load Considering the Temperature Sensitivity of load
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: The efficient operation of virtual power plants cannot be separated from accurate load management, and thus the accuracy of baseline load calculation is crucial. This paper analyses the current situation of virtual power plants' baseline load calculation in China and discusses the limitations of traditional baseline load calculation methods. Aiming at the load with temperature-sensitive characteristics, an improved method based on clustering and confidence statistics is proposed. Elaborating on the key aspects of the method, such as data processing, cluster analysis and confidence statistics analysis, it reveals how to improve the accuracy of baseline load calculation. The validity and reasonableness of the proposed calculation method are also verified through examples using actual load data from a certain place in China, the conclusion shows that the proposed method has significant advantages in improving the accuracy of load forecasting and reducing error, especially in coping with the fluctuation of temperature and extreme weather conditions, which shows stronger adaptability. This will provide a more reasonable basis for the optimal scheduling of the virtual power plants and enhance the operational efficiency and stability of the virtual power plants in the power system.

articleTitle: Research on Reactive Power Optimization System of Power Grid under High Proportion of Clean Energy
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: With the high proportion of clean energy connected to the power grid, its output shows significant volatility and uncertainty due to natural factors. Traditional reactive power compensation and voltage control strategies are difficult to cope with, resulting in increased difficulty in grid voltage control and prominent voltage quality problems. Concurrently, the dynamic nature of clean energy integration is causing continuous evolution in power grid structures. To address these challenges, the establishment of a reactive power optimization system proves essential. Such a system effectively regulates grid reactive power, ensures voltage quality, reduces grid losses, enhances clean energy utilization capacity, meets user power quality requirements, and elevates the grid's intelligence level. The implementation of this system is expected to yield considerable economic and social benefits for power grid operations.

Author Keywords: power grid reactive power optimization system

articleTitle: Modeling and Robust Control for Modules in Electric Power Insurance Loss Assessment and Claims Robot
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: This study presents a new robust model-based control method to reduce the effects of variable system parameters and workload on the performance of power insurance claim assessment robots' articular modules.It combines PID control with robust compensation and model-based strategies to improve precision in uncertain conditions. The controller is carefully designed according to the dynamic model and includes a Lyapunov-based component to handle uncertainties in system dynamics. This strategy, enhancing traditional PID or reconfiguring robust control, is easy to apply and provides clear advantages. Theory shows the controller ensures stability and reliability through uniform boundedness.Additionally, a Matlab-based simulation platform has been used to create a controller prototype, simplifying development and debugging. Finally, simulations confirm the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed control method.

articleTitle: Research and Application of Remote Operation and Maintenance Technology for Substation Monitoring System Based on Zero Trust Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: With the accelerated advancement of the intelligent transformation of power systems, the demand for remote operation and maintenance (O&M) of substation monitoring systems has become increasingly prominent. However, the traditional network boundary protection model has gradually exposed numerous limitations when dealing with complex and ever-changing cyber attacks. In response to the cybersecurity risks present in traditional remote O&M, this paper proposes a security protection technology scheme for remote O&M based on the zero-trust mechanism. By constructing a zero-trust secure network communication architecture and employing multi-factor authentication and dynamic trust evaluation mechanisms to build a protection system, efficient and secure remote O&M operations can be achieved. Experimental results demonstrate that this scheme can reduce O&M time by 86% in a real-world substation environment, with a success rate of 98.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> in defending against man-in-the-middle attacks and spoofing attacks. It ensures controllability, traceability, and least privilege control throughout the O&M process, meeting the requirements for the construction of a new protection system for power systems.

articleTitle: Design of Lightweight and Low-Cost Micro-Meteorological Sensor for Forest Fire Prevention of Distribution Line Based on XTU Terminal
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Aiming at the traditional micro-weather monitoring scheme for distribution lines, which has the problems of difficult power collection, inconvenient communication, high equipment cost and operation and maintenance cost, this paper proposes a lightweight and low-cost anti-mountain fire micro-weather sensor design scheme based on XTU terminal. The scheme realises the real-time monitoring of multiple meteorological elements and the deep integration of power distribution automation system through hardware integration, software optimization and system integration design. This paper describes in detail the design background, demand analysis, overall design principles, hardware design, software design, and integration design of the sensor. It enables the sensor to achieve high accuracy, high reliability, and low power operation in complex environments, which is of great significance for enhancing the power system's ability to prevent hill fires.

articleTitle: Application of Visible Light Artificial Intelligence Recognition and Millimeter Wave Radar Ranging Technology in Transmission Line Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: In response to the urgent need for monitoring transmission lines, an innovative fusion of millimeter wave radar and visible light image recognition has been adopted to achieve front-end recognition of invading objects in transmission line corridors and measurement of the minimum gap between transmission lines. By using millimeter wave radar scanning and ranging, combined with visible light image recognition, sub meter level accuracy distance recognition can be achieved for the front-end hidden dangers of the 700 meter long and 80 meter wide transmission line corridor and its surrounding areas, effectively identifying potential external intrusion hazards, reducing the false alarm rate of transmission line monitoring alarms, and more efficiently ensuring the safety of transmission lines.

articleTitle: Exploration of Economic Benefit Analysis and Optimization Strategies for Energy Storage System Configuration in Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: The integration of energy storage systems (ESS) within microgrids presents significant economic benefits and potential for optimization strategies. This paper rigorously investigates the economic performance of energy storage configurations in microgrid applications, analyzing systemic interactions and efficiencies. The study implements advanced econometric models and computational simulations to evaluate the cost-benefit dynamics over diverse operational scenarios. By synthesizing empirical data and leveraging optimization algorithms, the analysis identifies critical factors influencing the economic outcomes of ESS deployment. The findings elucidate the optimization pathways that enhance the value proposition of energy storage within microgrids, balancing investment costs against operational savings and reliability improvements. The paper concludes with strategic insights for microgrid designers and operators, offering tailored recommendations for energy storage system planning that optimize economic returns while supporting broader energy resilience and sustainability objectives.

articleTitle: Annual Time-Series Production Simulation Model with Multiregional Interconnections Based on Optimized Cycle Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Medium/long-term time-series production simulation is critical for power balance analysis in high-renewable power systems. This study proposes a yearly 8760-hour simulation model for multi-regional interconnected systems, integrating operational models for conventional thermal, hydropower, pumped/electrochemical storage, wind, and photovoltaic units at the equipment level. System-level constraints, including regional power balance and inter-regional transmission limits, are incorporated to enhance realism. To address computational complexity, a optimizing cycle decomposition technique is introduced, dividing the annual simulation into 52 weekly cycles for sequential optimization, ensuring computational tractability. The model is validated using planning data from a provincial system in Eastern China, achieving a total solving time of ~30 minutes. Results confirm the model's capability to track real-time operational states while balancing accuracy and efficiency. This approach provides a practical framework for power system planning and operations in large-scale renewable-integrated grids

articleTitle: Optimal Operation Strategy of Electric Vehicle Battery Charging and Swapping Stations for Frequency Response Service
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: A value function approximation based strategy is presented to make intra-day operating decisions of electric vehicle battery charging and swapping stations for battery charging management and frequency response service. The intra-day operation is formulated as Markov decision process to reflect stochastic sequential decision feature. An appropriate piecewise linear function is adopted to represent the expected long-term cost at each time period, which is trained offline by mini-batch gradient temporal difference learning. During intra-day operations, the power baseline and frequency response reserve are obtained online, wherein the trained value function is invoked. Numerical results show that the proposed strategy can ensure the above dual provision. Moreover, the offline training by mini-batch gradient can reach 98.43% of the theoretical optimum.

articleTitle: Research on Optimal Scheduling Strategy of Shared Energy Storage in Industrial Parks Considering Demand Response
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: This article studies the power dispatching model of shared energy storage and the operational economy of the ESS unit. First, the structure of the integrated energy system in the industrial park is elaborated. Then, the individual independent energy storage structure of the park is introduced, and the deficiencies of this model are analyzed. After that, the shared energy storage model based on centralized energy storage is presented, and the improvements in its effective operation time and operational economy are analyzed. Finally, a multi - objective optimization model for power dispatching and operational economy applied to the shared energy storage system is proposed. Considering the emergency dispatching response, the operational performance of the shared energy storage system is improved, and this is verified through the simulation.

articleTitle: Analysis on the Operation of Inter-Provincial Multi-Channel Centralized Bidding Transaction in Power Market
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: The continuous deepening of the construction of the national unified power market has led to the gradual expansion of the scale of inter-provincial medium- and long-term market entities and trading channels. The traditional single-channel transaction mode, primarily relying on bilateral agreements and listing, struggles to meet the demand of large-scale optimal allocation of power resources, and the efficiency of trading organization needs to be improved. Inter-provincial multi-channel centralized bidding transaction came into being. However, with the regular organization of transactions, operation monitoring and risk prevention have become urgent problems to be solved. In this regard, this paper first introduces the inter-provincial multi-channel centralized bidding trading mechanism, then summarizes the current situation and effectiveness of the trading operation, and finally thinks about and looks forward to the future construction direction of trading mechanism, aiming at supporting the improvement of the decision-making level of transaction operation.

articleTitle: Optimization Study of Energy Management of Intelligent Unloading Device Based on Supercharged Power System
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: To cope with the dual demands of loading and unloading efficiency and environmental protection in the modern logistics industry, this paper investigates an intelligent unloading device energy management method based on a supercharged power system. By combining a diesel generator with a power battery to form a dual-source energy supply architecture, it can provide sufficient power when the unloading vehicle is under high load and shave peaks and fill valleys during the low load or idle phase, realizing a comprehensive balance between fuel economy and emission control. The paper first establishes a system simulation platform including a diesel fuel consumption model and a battery SOC model, and then factors such as fuel consumption, emission, and battery life are incorporated into a multi-objective optimization framework to explore the performance differences among strategies based on rule-based control, offline dynamic programming (DP), and model predictive control (MPC). Simulation results show that the optimization approach can reduce fuel consumption by 5% to 9%, and significantly smooth battery SOC and reduce emissions compared with the traditional empirical strategy. The hardware-in-the-loop test preliminarily verifies the effectiveness of the proposed method, which supports the subsequent popularization and application under more complex or high-power working conditions.

articleTitle: Software Technology for Emergency Wireless Communication Systems in Power Grids Integrating BeiDou, Shortwave, and Tiantong
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: To address the complex power emergency rescue environment in scenarios involving network, power, and road disruptions (the “three disruptions”), this study proposes a Beidou-integrated emergency wireless communication system for typical power business scenarios. The system primarily consists of four subsystems: the Beidou-3 communication subsystem, shortwave communication subsystem, Tiantong satellite communication subsystem, and integrated communication subsystem. Leveraging Beidou as the foundation, supplemented by shortwave and Tiantong, the system harnesses the advantages of Beidou short message communication technology to establish a three-dimensional integrated communication architecture for power systems that coordinates space, air, and ground. This architecture achieves adaptation to power business needs and resolves the issue where traditional network coverage blind spots cannot meet differentiated power business demands. Testing results demonstrate that the system exhibits good functionality and performance, as well as a certain degree of stability and security.

articleTitle: Day-Ahead and Intra-Day Two-Stage Coordinated Optimal Scheduling for Active Distribution Networks with Cluster Integration of Thermal Storage Electric Heating Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Thermal storage electric heating, as a common flexible load resource, holds significant potential for reducing system operating costs and promoting the integration of renewable energy. To address issues such as the volatility of distributed power output, load forecasting errors, and the temporal differences in the operational characteristics of various dispatchable resources in active distribution networks (ADNs), this paper proposes a two-stage coordinated optimal dispatch strategy for ADNs that incorporates clustered thermal-storage electric heating systems. Firstly, based on the electro-thermal conversion and thermal storage characteristics of thermal-storage electric heating, a model is established for the thermal demand and load characteristics of electric heating users' buildings. Secondly, a two-stage optimization strategy encompassing day-ahead and intra-day scheduling is developed. In the day-ahead scheduling stage, an optimization model is constructed with the objective of minimizing the comprehensive operating costs of the ADN. In the intra-day scheduling stage, a rolling optimization method is employed to adjust the day-ahead schedule by considering both system economy and the deviation costs of unit outputs, while coordinating fast- and slow-response resources across different time scales. Finally, the proposed strategy is validated using a modified IEEE 33-node test system. Case study results demonstrate that the proposed strategy effectively balances user-side comfort and grid-side economic benefits, achieving coordinated optimization across multiple time scales and enhancing system stability and operational efficiency.

articleTitle: Flexible Resource Cross-Regional Game Optimization and Scheduling under High Proportion of Renewable Energy
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: Flexibility can be achieved between different regional power grids, enabling regions with a high proportion of renewable energy to obtain flexible resources from other regions, thereby ensuring the safe and flexible operation of the power grid. Based on this, this paper proposes a cross-regional optimal scheduling method for multivariate flexible resources considering a master-slave game. Firstly, the flexible supply capacity of wind and solar energy, along with the flexibility adjustment demand of renewable energy, is quantitatively analyzed. A multi-agent optimization model for the upper-level region is constructed with the goal of minimizing the net income of each operator and aggregator. Secondly, the flexibility and mutual aid capability of the tie-line are analyzed, and an optimal dispatching model for the lower-level multi-regional power grid is developed with the objective of minimizing the operating cost of each regional power grid. This model engages in a master-slave game with the upper-level model. Finally, three interconnected IEEE-39 node systems are established for case analysis. The results demonstrate that the proposed double-layer optimal scheduling model based on the master-slave game can effectively reduce the system's operating costs and enhance the overall flexibility and mutual aid level of the power grid.
